Here's my unabashed hyper bullish view on where crypto is going  

Every onchain cycle since 2013, we've had an onchain boom/bust. The boom typically shows what pmf would look like for onchain experiments if it were sustainable and with the bust it kills 95% of the experiments but leave just enough to build unicorns.   

Lets take NFTs, Cryptokitties in 2017 made up of 20% of all eth txns and during mint/play time ETH was basically unusable, but the ability to mint unique NFTs became a thing and it predated the 2020/21 NFT boom. Now post AI you could argue content is commoditized and what humans now prefer is scarce art with provenance, real human connections, in this world NFTs will likely make a comeback.   

So from 2013–2023, we pretty much speed ran all of the crypto experiments onchain.   Now we need a reason for these things to be needed, like the NFT example above. Or if you look at DAOs/Governance useless today but with AI agents could argue autonomous orgs will be a thing.   

Onchain needs tech catalysts and I think AI is the right catalyst to validate a lot of onchain experiments of the last decade. But what other hidden catalysts are there? Thats my bet for crypto.

text:
The current market environment is unfavorable, but I believe $HOOKR is still worth paying attention to.

0x18e674231a58c239dc7daedcffe15ec3a24cff5c 

The reason is that its latest updates are validating our core thesis.

Hookr has the potential to evolve from a trading tool built on Uniswap v4 Hooks into composable financial infrastructure connecting liquidity management, revenue rights trading, and AI Agents.

The most valuable development this time is that the product is beginning to demonstrate actual usage through measurable data. According to the official website, Hookr has now built 63 Hooks and initialized 163 Pools, with cumulative Value Facilitated reaching $456 million and Total Value Deposited reaching $26.02 million. These figures do not represent protocol revenue or current TVL, but they show that Hookr is already facilitating real on-chain trading and capital activity. Compared with our initial research, when we were primarily looking at its product architecture, this is undoubtedly an important step forward.

The upgrade to Revenue Tokens further expands Hookr's potential market. It allows projects to lock future fee revenue rights into contracts and issue fixed-supply Revenue Tokens, enabling them to raise funds, reward communities, or pay contributors using future cash flows without having to sell their core tokens. Recent additions, including the ability to add revenue streams after minting, the removal of limits on the number of revenue streams, support for more currencies, and the ability to use Revenue Token shares themselves as additional revenue streams, make the system considerably more flexible. More importantly, Hookr's revenue share is now taken from actual income rather than token supply, reducing concerns about token dilution for projects using the system. I believe this gives Hookr an opportunity to enter a much broader market for on-chain revenue management and capital markets, rather than depending solely on launchpad activity.

Its external ecosystem connections are also expanding. HOOKR has become a base trading pair on Books, connecting PairToken markets through both ETH and HOOKR, while supporting cross-platform launches and tokenized revenue. The project has also announced plans to expand to Ethereum Mainnet in collaboration with What The Hook. Meanwhile, Agent Gate has integrated ERC-8004 identity verification and Priors Reputation Scores into trading pools. Creators can restrict participation to wallets with Agent identities and even configure different fees based on reputation scores. This is particularly worth noting. We previously believed that the Agent economy would require its own identity and credit systems, and Hookr is now beginning to apply these capabilities to actual trading rules. If transactions between Agents continue to grow in the future, Hookr could become infrastructure that they use to issue and trade assets.

Other Hook Blocks are also continuing to improve. Market-hours Fee adjusts fees according to US stock market trading sessions, Sandwich Guard and Storm Fee adjust fees based on specific trading behaviors and market volatility, while Compound Fees allows LPs to reinvest unclaimed fees into liquidity with a single transaction. These features show that Hookr is moving beyond providing generic trading rules and toward solving specific problems across different assets and trading environments, particularly the unique requirements of tokenized stock markets.

For HOOKR itself, the development I am most interested in is the TJAR automated buyback and burn mechanism. According to the official allocation rules, 50% of treasury revenue goes toward buybacks and burns, 30% is allocated to operations, and 20% is used to build ownership within the IMD ecosystem. Since November 6, the project has announced seven automated burns. The bot checks the Jar every 10 minutes and has performed more than 900 checks in total. The official website currently shows approximately 7.15 million HOOKR permanently burned. Compared with the previous situation, where buybacks were only part of the theoretical design, revenue allocation, automated execution, and burns are now forming a traceable on-chain process. This is an important improvement in the token's fundamentals, although we still need to monitor the actual buyback amounts and burn rate rather than assuming that cumulative burns alone represent meaningful supply contraction.

I believe this latest round of updates has genuinely validated three of our previous assumptions: Hookr is evolving from a launchpad into composable trading infrastructure; Revenue Tokens have the potential to become an independent on-chain revenue asset class; and Agent identity and reputation systems can be incorporated into actual financial trading environments. However, product progress does not mean that value has already been fully realized. Having 63 Hooks does not mean every module is consistently generating revenue, and $456 million in facilitated trading value does not mean the protocol has earned an equivalent amount in fees. Whether Books and Ethereum attract sustained external adoption, whether Agent Gate generates meaningful usage, and whether TJAR can scale buybacks as protocol revenue grows are still important points to verify. The security risks associated with complex cross-pool mechanisms also cannot be overlooked.

This is precisely why I believe HOOKR is still worth researching despite the unfavorable market conditions. I am not betting on when the market will recover. I am watching whether Hookr can continue increasing actual usage, expanding external integrations, and translating protocol revenue into token value capture at a time when capital is no longer willing to pay easily for new narratives. If the Ethereum Mainnet expansion goes live successfully, external projects continue adopting Hookr, Agent Gate attracts new trading demand, and buybacks and burns gradually reach meaningful scale, HOOKR could evolve from a Uniswap v4 Hooks project on Robinhood Chain into financial infrastructure connecting multiple assets, trading pools, and Agent applications.

For me, this is the long-term direction that makes HOOKR most worth paying attention to right now.

quoted_text:
Given the current market conditions, which are far from favorable, I am actually more willing to spend time researching $HOOKR.

0x18e674231a58c239dc7daedcffe15ec3a24cff5c 

Not because a weaker market makes a project more likely to rise.

It's because when most capital is chasing short-term narratives, I want to understand which projects are still developing their products, which updates are genuinely changing their use cases, and whether these developments can eventually translate into demand for the token.

I initially became interested in HOOKR because it was trying to expand Uniswap v4 Hooks from a set of trading rules into composable trading infrastructure. The latest updates have given me a clearer understanding of this direction: Hookr is beginning to connect cross-pool capital management, Agent integration, and future revenue rights. It is no longer just helping projects launch tokens, but attempting to provide a set of financial tools that other projects can also use.

The most noteworthy development is Revenue Tokens. Traditionally, when projects need financing, they often have to sell their own tokens or issue more tokens to reward their communities. Hookr offers an alternative: lock the revenue rights associated with fee-generating assets in a contract, then issue a fixed-supply Revenue Token that makes future income over a specific period into a tradable asset.

For example, a project might hold a liquidity position that continuously generates fees but not want to sell its own token to raise capital. It can lock and tokenize the revenue rights for the next 7 days, 30 days, 90 days, or even permanently. Holders receive the fees generated by the corresponding revenue rights, while the project retains its original token. Hookr also allows revenue rights to be divided into daily Time Shares, enabling income from different periods to be traded independently.

I believe this design is worth paying attention to because it addresses something more fundamental than how a token can attract more trading volume. It addresses how on-chain projects can raise capital, distribute revenue, and make future cash flows more flexible and liquid. It also means Hookr's potential users do not have to be limited to its own launchpad. If other liquidity providers, launchpads, and DeFi projects are willing to use these tools, Hookr could enter existing markets rather than relying entirely on demand generated by new token launches.

Another development that has increased my interest is the launch of the MCP Server. Agents can use the interface to discover pools, obtain quotes, check trading conditions, and construct transactions for swaps, reward claims, token launches, and other operations that await signing. The server does not store users' private keys, and the user's wallet still handles signing and authorization.

Taken on its own, an MCP interface is not an unreplicable technological moat. But when combined with Hookr's other products, a more interesting possibility emerges: Agents can not only identify trading opportunities but also invoke preconfigured trading rules and handle parts of the transaction process through the same infrastructure. For applications that may need to automate liquidity management, execute arbitrage, or allocate capital across different markets in the future, these modular tools could be more useful than a platform that only launches tokens.

Pool Mesh, Family Pinger, and Fee Bridge further reinforce this direction. Pool Mesh can allocate capital across multiple target pools; Family Pinger can execute batches of operations and periodic tasks across related pools; and Fee Bridge allows part of the fees generated by one pool to flow to liquidity providers in another pool according to predefined rules. The common objective is to coordinate the movement of capital and revenue across different pools rather than forcing each pool to manage its liquidity in isolation.

This is also why I believe HOOKR has the potential to develop long-term value. Its real competitive advantage may not come from having the largest number of features, but from whether external developers can combine these modules to build their own trading products. Once developers begin relying on Hookr to build pools, manage fee distribution, and coordinate cross-pool capital, its value could come from sustained infrastructure usage rather than reactions to individual product announcements.

Of course, this potential growth has not yet been realized. Discord is open, and HookBook, the SDK, and developer documentation are lowering the barriers to integration, but there is still a gap between an announced third-party integration and sustained trading volume. Projects and initiatives such as Safron, ZEALZ, and Longbow Lend need to be evaluated individually to determine whether their integrations have actually been deployed and are being used. To me, whether developers continue adopting these tools matters more than how many new modules the official team releases.

So why am I still paying attention to $HOOKR when market conditions are poor?

Because I want to track a potential source of demand that may gradually take shape, rather than simply look for a reason to expect the next rebound. When the market weakens, projects driven solely by narratives and short-term liquidity can easily lose attention. But if an infrastructure protocol is used consistently by other projects, its trading rules and capital management functions may generate demand that differs from pure token speculation. This demand will not automatically make HOOKR rise, but it gives us more concrete indicators with which to assess whether its long-term thesis is being realized.

HOOKR's value-capture design is therefore also worth monitoring. The protocol primarily generates revenue from additional mechanisms enabled by users, such as dynamic fees, Anti-Snipe, LP Rewards, Auto Burn, and arbitrage value recapture, rather than directly taking all base LP trading fees. According to the official documentation, the protocol's share is generally 20% of the relevant additional fees, with the exact percentage determined by each pool's configuration. Protocol revenue can flow into the treasury and, under the relevant mechanisms, be used for HOOKR buybacks and burns.

The key to this design is connecting token demand with protocol usage. However, I would not assume that value capture has already been established simply because a buyback mechanism has been included in the design. What still needs to be demonstrated is actual protocol revenue, on-chain buyback transactions, and verifiable token burns. More features do not necessarily mean more revenue, and higher trading volume does not mean the protocol will receive fees in the same proportion.

Low liquidity is another issue I have to take into account. It amplifies price volatility and can lead to sharper pullbacks when capital exits. It also means that progress on the product may not be reflected immediately in the token's price. But I would not treat low liquidity itself as a bullish reason. What is genuinely worth investigating is whether product adoption, protocol revenue, and the developer ecosystem continue improving during a period of poor price performance. If these indicators gradually strengthen while the market has not yet fully recognized the progress, HOOKR may present a valuation gap worth examining further.

My current view on HOOKR is therefore that its product capabilities are expanding, ecosystem adoption still needs to be validated, and token value capture has not yet been fully realized. Revenue Tokens expand the potential use cases for revenue rights, MCP allows Agents to invoke Hookr's tools directly, and the cross-pool modules are beginning to connect capital and fee flows across different markets. Together, these updates support its long-term direction of evolving from a launchpad into composable trading infrastructure, but they are not yet proof that this direction has generated demand at scale.

Going forward, what matters most to me is not whether HOOKR can rebound alongside the broader market in the short term, but whether third-party developers actually begin using these modules, whether cross-pool tools generate sustained trading activity, and whether protocol revenue can gradually translate into verifiable buybacks and burns. If these developments materialize, HOOKR's research thesis will be more concrete than that of tokens relying purely on market hype, even if the broader market remains weak.

This is why I believe HOOKR is still worth paying attention to right now. I am not betting on when market sentiment will turn optimistic again. I am watching whether Hookr can gradually prove that the problems it is trying to solve are genuinely worth solving, at a time when the market is no longer willing to pay easily for concepts alone. A market recovery could provide a better trading environment, but only real usage and value capture can make its long-term thesis more convincing.

text:
使用线性波动率产品 vs 期权来做空波动率
 
美股市场有可观的资金在做空VIX的产品上，他们主要获利方式是利用VIX期限结构长期近低远高，做空远期VIX期货等候收敛获取收益。
 
-1x 做空VIX的产品，只要底层VIX期货指数单日上涨一倍，净值就会被彻底清空（或直接触发强平）。参考2018年VIX ETN/ETF Volmageddon（波动率末日，VIX从约17跳到37+，单日暴涨115%）。
 
在期权端，若要让隐含波动率上涨一倍就抹平整个净值（实际触发强平的阈值会更早），所需的Vega敞口大约要达到净值的3%。
 
以期权波动率交易者的实际交易规模来看，30天标准Vega仅占净值的0.2~0.4%，与3%的临界水平相距甚远。
 
做空期权波动率同样能捕获隐含波动率期限结构上的contango收益，同时还参与Gamma与Theta的交易。在安全空间和收益来源上要比做空波动率线性产品要好很多。

text:
There is a reason New York City has not experienced the kind of violent riots we have witnessed in Paris and other major cities around the world.

We had the NYPD’s Strategic Response Group (SRG), a specialized unit of highly trained officers prepared to confront violence before it spiraled out of control.

Let me make something absolutely clear.

Peaceful protest is a constitutional right. Violent rioting is a crime. And confusing the two is a dangerous failure of leadership.

The SRG was not created to silence peaceful protesters. It was created to protect New Yorkers when demonstrations crossed the line into violence, to protect businesses from destruction, peaceful demonstrators from violent agitators, and police officers from being assaulted.

Now City Hall is dismantling that specialized unit, introducing unarmed civilian de-escalation teams, and restricting the tools available to police.

I support de-escalation. Every responsible police officer does. But de-escalation is a strategy, not a substitute for the ability to confront violence.

You cannot reason with a brick flying through a storefront. You cannot negotiate with a Molotov cocktail. And you cannot send a social worker to do the job of a specially trained police officer confronting a violent mob.

The NYPD will still have officers responding to protests. But the question City Hall  has failed to answer is why New Yorkers will be safer without a dedicated unit specifically trained for these dangerous situations.

What happens when peaceful protesters are attacked? When businesses are being destroyed? When police officers are surrounded and assaulted?

Who responds? How quickly? With what training? And with what tools?

These are not hypothetical questions. These are the decisions that determine whether a dangerous situation is contained or an entire neighborhood descends into chaos.

I spent four years as mayor and 22 years as an NYPD officer. I know the difference between protecting someone’s right to protest and allowing someone to use that protest as cover for violence.

The right to protest does not include the right to terrorize. And protecting civil liberties should never require surrendering public safety.

City Hall may believe dismantling the SRG is a political victory.

But if violence erupts, the people paying the price won’t be the activists applauding this announcement or the politicians celebrating it at City Hall.

It will be the police officer who gets assaulted. The small-business owner whose livelihood is destroyed. The peaceful protester who gets caught in the violence. The innocent New Yorker who simply wants to get home safely.

New York City’s Public Safety is not a laboratory for ideological experiments. Our police officers are not expendable. And public safety is not something you gamble with to score political points.

City Hall should reverse this decision before New Yorkers discover the consequences the hard way.

text:
i think the crypto industry is entering a phase where people need to make a very important decision.

either continue waiting for the next bull market to rescue them, or start exploring what else this technology could actually enable.

for almost a decade, we have trained an entire generation to believe that the biggest opportunity in crypto is buying something before someone else buys it.

we created thousands of tokens, endless narratives, and an entire culture around discovering the next 100x.

but how many people have actually developed skills which could help them create something valuable outside speculation?

that's a question worth asking.

the good thing is that we're entering a very different technological environment.

intelligence is becoming abundant.

someone with basic programming knowledge can now build applications which previously required an entire team.

someone with good research skills can explore decades of academic literature and discover ideas which were never implemented.

someone who understands market mechanisms can experiment with completely new economic designs.

and crypto gives us the infrastructure to turn many of those experiments into open markets.

imagine markets where people earn money by fulfilling commitments.

markets where humans compete based on their knowledge and skills.

markets where people receive rewards for verifying information, contributing to distributed networks, or helping communities solve problems.

imagine decentralized AI inference markets, privacy networks, mesh-network economies, reputation systems, and new kinds of coordination mechanisms.

these are all directions worth exploring.

and you don't necessarily need millions in funding to begin.

you need curiosity, the ability to learn, a clear problem, and enough discipline to ship something small.

instead of spending another six months looking for the next token narrative, spend those six months understanding one problem deeply.

find ten people who face that problem.

build something which solves even a small part of it.

test whether people actually care.

improve it.

repeat.

we should be creating markets where people can earn through their contributions, knowledge, creativity, and commitments rather than depending entirely on asset appreciation.

i still believe crypto has the potential to become one of the most important technologies for economic freedom.

but that future won't emerge automatically from another bull market.

it will emerge when more people stop treating crypto only as a place to extract wealth and start treating it as infrastructure to create wealth.

perhaps the next crypto renaissance will begin with people who have almost nothing left to lose, but still have the curiosity to build something new.

author: dongdongRobin
quoted_text:
Lighter，Aster 连着出被盗事件，而且都是agent key被盗后转走用户资产。Aster这次的问题比Lighter更加严重，因为是通过agent key权限就拥有了完整的转账权限，任何用户agent key泄漏都潜在等于转账权限丢失。Lighter是agent key被向自建vault的转账权限设计出现漏洞，官方事后报告说 key 泄漏是用户自写签名代码重复使用 nonce，虽然漏洞相对隐蔽，但精心组合还是能够利用。

Hyperliquid的agent key同样有向vault转账的权限，但和lighter不同的是hyperliquid的agent key向hypercore原生vault转账等于认购，不会出现lighter这种存进vault不获取任何份额的情况。Hyperliquid之前也有钓鱼网站盗取用户私钥的案例，但都是直接盗取钱包私钥获得master权限，也就完整拥有转账权限，协议本身没有任何防御手段。

从协议安全性来看，目前hyperliquid协议层没有被盗过，这次lighter和aster暴露的问题在HL上并不会发生。但这不代表以后不会出现。HL是一个更大的目标，显然更多黑客盯着他。我之前分析过Hyperliquid要成为金融infra重要的前提之一就是证明自己对风险的反脆弱性。当参与者足够多以后每个环节的风险都保持在局部，不会影响协议整体的信任。甚至我觉得可能要在被盗事件出现后HL再进一步证明自己的反脆弱性，加强社会整体对这个协议的信任。但Hyperliquid仍然还差两块拼图没有完成。

开源节点代码和验证者去中心化是 Hyperliquid 成为全球金融中性基础设施的最后两块拼图。

验证者在去中心化，但还在早期。Hyper foundation 现在占总质押量的 48% 左右，团队代币解锁后向第三方转移会让这个比例继续下降；Hyperliquid Strategies × Unit 的节点已经占比接近9%，上市公司继续融资买币还会推高这部分占比。

代码还没有开源，但已经有人在逆向节点二进制，也有人在发起开源节点项目。比特币和 Linux 的安全从来不是靠藏。Linux 今年被 AI 翻出一批漏洞，然后一批一批修掉了；闭源代码里一样有这些漏洞，AI 找漏洞的能力不分开源闭源，区别只是开源的会被修，闭源的只会被用。开源会让 Hyperliquid 的安全性可以被别人验证，成为一个要承载别人资产的基础设施。

text:
The name $GTA6 practically puts its biggest advantage right on the chart: whenever there’s new news about GTA VI, the token has a chance to get noticed again.

4kjruqGHDsSqkMdFfCjV7Vb62HPFhtXyWc2t6JpQzDnz

But that’s also the problem: it rides on the hype surrounding the game, not the revenue generated by the game itself.

With the official release scheduled for November 19, the question worth watching is how many more times the market can trade this narrative before the game actually launches.

The logic behind this token is straightforward. GTA VI is one of the most anticipated games of the year, and future trailers, gameplay footage, media reviews, and streamer content could all create new waves of attention. The token doesn’t need to explain its narrative in detail. The game itself is its source of attention.

On October 27 and 28, the token rallied sharply on consecutive days. Public tracking data also showed a significant increase in holder addresses, suggesting that the move was accompanied by growing attention rather than being purely a price fluctuation.

Beyond the gaming narrative, there’s also the StonkFun platform mechanism. The token participates in the platform’s buyback-and-burn system and has holder rewards denominated in TTWO. Platform records show that the cumulative distribution was worth approximately $150,000. This gives GTA6 an additional mechanism-based narrative beyond simply borrowing the game’s name, but it doesn’t change the fact that its core value still depends on attention.

The most important window ahead is the marketing period leading up to the release. If Rockstar continues releasing new content, or discussion around the game suddenly picks up across social media and streaming platforms, GTA6 could attract another wave of attention.

Take-Two also has an earnings report scheduled for November 9, and the market may pay attention to management’s comments on the game’s release plans. However, that doesn’t guarantee any new catalyst will emerge. The real test comes on November 19. The launch could push attention to its peak, but it could also become the moment when traders take profits. Markets often buy an event before it happens, but that doesn’t mean prices will keep rising once it arrives.

Another risk is that there’s currently no evidence that Rockstar or Take-Two officially issued, endorsed, or backed this token. No matter how well the game sells, that revenue will not automatically flow to GTA6. Likewise, its TTWO-related reward mechanism should not be confused with owning Take-Two stock or having any entitlement to stock dividends.

One final question is worth considering: if attention around GTA VI reaches its peak when the game officially launches, but GTA6 has already rallied several times over by then, how many buyers will still be left to step in?

For tokens like this, having a big narrative is only the starting point. What ultimately determines how far the price can go is whether buyers still believe someone else will be willing to pay more.

author: teortaxesTex
quoted_text:
Very, very strange statement tonight from @CommerceGov and @TheJusticeDept about Megaspeed. The facts here just don't add up, and this does nothing to explain why Commerce did not cut Megaspeed off from chips. In fact, it raises even more questions about what happened here. 

BIS claims that it started an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024, and following an end-use check in June 2025 it handed off the criminal investigation to DOJ. It also said that in June 2025, Nvidia put Megaspeed on its own internal no-trade blacklist--implying this solved the issue and cut them off from Nvidia chips.

The problem with this story, is that Megaspeed kept buying chips after Nvidia put them on their no-trade list. @mackhawk reported in December 2025 that Megaspeed imported 17,544 GB300 AI chips in November 2025, worth about $787 million. There are multiple other reports that say Megaspeed continued to receive chips into 2026. 

If Commerce was so concerned about Megaspeed smuggling chips to China that the DOJ opened a criminal case after an end-use check in June 2025, and Nvidia also put them on an internal blacklist, why didn't Commerce also put them on the Entity List? That is literally the entire purpose of the Entity List, to list companies in situations like this! If it had done that--and also put Megaspeed's affiliates and subsidiaries such as Speedmatrix (its Malaysian subsidiary) and PT Megaspeed International (its Indonesian subsidiary) on the Entity List--Commerce could have actually cut Megaspeed off from chips! 

Instead, Commerce appears to have outsourced Entity List restrictions and export enforcement to Nvidia. That is insanely irresponsible! Does @USTreasury outsource sanctions enforcement entirely to US banks? Of course not, OFAC sanctions entities that are violating US sanctions. How is "we didn't act because Nvidia acted for us" the best defense Commerce can muster here?  

And also, why was Nvidia's blacklisting action so ineffective? Did Nvidia also place Megaspeed's subsidiaries such as Speedmatrix and PT Megaspeed International on its blacklist? I would bet they did not! If they kept shipping to them after blacklisting Megaspeed, that would be very concerning. What is the point of Nvidia blacklisting Megaspeed if they continue to allow their chips to be shipped to Megaspeed's subsidiaries in Malaysia and Indonesia? 

It's hard to decide who screwed up more here, @CommerceGov or Nvidia. Just a total failure all around. How could both sides have agreed that Megaspeed represented a national security risk, but completely failed to prevent Megaspeed from buying $787 million worth of chips just five months after it was blacklisted? And undoubtedly more chips in 2026.  

Maybe instead of writing defensive press releases that don't add up, @CommerceGov could write a rule finally placing Megaspeed on the Entity List. But maybe they're waiting for Treasury and NSC to write that rule for them as well.

text:
Giveth - 10 years - WOW.

Truly an incredible milestone. We've done so much and had so much fun along the way! 

I'm so proud of our work.  We've raised millions of dollars for nonprofits, and impacted countless lives around the globe, including countries that are normally out of reach for traditional financial rails.

For the last 10 years Giveth has been on a mission to build something better than governments, and the mission has taken us around the world and back, with dozens of start-ups and countless of collaborators. 

It's been a long hard battle, we've almost shut down in every bear market & yet somehow the generosity of the community has kept us alive. 

There was one point in 2019 where Giveth was just me & Amin, and then 4 years later, we grew into ~75 people working on 7 or 8 different projects all exploring how to make public goods profitable. 

Throughout this decade we've completely redesigned the Giveth platform 6 times!

We were working on bonding curves in 2018, we ran the first Ethereum scaling conference, we pushed for open source block explorers & we even ran Burning Man camps. 

But our journey is not complete... no where near it. 

I am still convinced that we will one day find a model that can make nonprofits profitable. Nonprofits create value, and Giveth's primary goal has always been to produce a novel economic system that can appreciate the value that nonprofits produce. 

It's not easy, and we don't know where this road will take us, but the journey continues.

Right now we are focused on making crypto safe to use for normal people. We rebuilt the Giveth platform to have a much safer experience (thanks to Turnkey) and our work with TheDAO Security Fund will hopefully extend a safer crypto experience to the entire Ethereum community.

Because no matter what cool model we find for appreciating the value that nonprofits produce... It won't work if normal people can use blockchain tech safely.

I couldn't be more proud of the work we've done over the last 10 years & of all the people I've worked with.

It's been quite the journey, one decade down, many more to go.

BREAKING: The U.S. Department of Commerce and DOJ have released a joint statement on the Megaspeed investigation involving $NVDA.

Here are the 6 biggest takeaways:

1. Investigation began in 2024: U.S. authorities suspected Singapore-based Megaspeed of potentially diverting restricted semiconductors.

2. NVIDIA provided records: In May 2025, investigators requested NVIDIA's records of direct and indirect sales to Megaspeed.

3. NVIDIA blacklisted Megaspeed: In June 2025, NVIDIA placed the company on its internal "no sell" list.

4. Authorities conducted an on-site inspection: U.S. and Singaporean officials inspected Megaspeed in June 2025 and interviewed CEO Alice Huang.

5. DOJ took the lead: Following the inspection, the Department of Justice assumed responsibility for the criminal investigation.

6. Potential criminal prosecution: Authorities say they will pursue the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct uncovered.

My biggest takeaway:

The government's statement focuses on Megaspeed's potential wrongdoing, not Nvidia's.

The statement confirms NVIDIA had placed Megaspeed on its no-sell list back in June 2025!

不论是什么支付，首先都是要有钱，信用体系是先借你钱，然后你在还，这里最重要的就是“信用”，为什么银行能借你钱，是因为你有足够的现时世界的信任基础。

但加密货币本身就是去中心化，重隐私的，那么如果让自己在加密货币领域的身份不通过现实世界和信用绑定，比如说你看到我钱包里有 100 万美元的 Token ，你敢借我多少钱？

而且欧美的信用体系已经非常发达了，对于 Circle 来说很难重新建立一套，只能加入之前的信用体系，所以要么就是用更低的利率来吸引用户，要么就是用更多的资金去砸出自己的信用体系。

I was wondering why Korean stocks were so weak today. Turns out TrendForce revised its 2027 memory demand forecasts…

TrendForce cut its demand forecasts for mobile DRAM by 0.6% and PC DRAM by 0.8%. But it raised its forecasts for server DRAM by 0.8% and graphics DRAM by 1.0%, so its forecast for total DRAM bit demand actually edged up 0.3%.

On the NAND side, TrendForce cut its total bit demand forecast by 3.2%. It lowered its estimates for mobile NAND by 6.5%, client SSDs by 10%, and enterprise SSDs by 1.5%. It now expects total NAND bit demand to grow 18.7% YoY in 2027, down from its previous forecast of 22.6%.

text:
半个月前预言 BTC 跌回 5.7 万美元、再也无法创新高，@jason 的看空判断正在兑现？

10 月 27 日，知名天使投资人、All-In 播客联合主持人 Jason Calacanis 曾公开喊空比特币。当时 BTC 价格约为 7.96 万美元，他预测未来 12 个月 BTC 将再次测试 5.7 万美元低点，并断言比特币再也无法突破历史新高。

如今来到 11 月 17 日，BTC 已回落至约 6.46 万美元，半个月跌幅接近 19%，距离他提出的 5.7 万美元目标又近了一步。

Jason 当时给出的理由包括比特币 ETF 持续资金外流、市场关注度下降，以及 AI 正在提供更多投资机会。他甚至建议投资者卖出 BTC，将资金转向 AI 和超级智能，并表达了对 Bittensor（TAO）的看好。

Jason 是美国知名天使投资人，曾早期投资 Uber、Robinhood。不过，他此前也曾在 2018 年判断比特币有 60%–70% 的归零概率，最终并未兑现。

至少从最近半个月的价格走势看，这次看空方向暂时占优。但 5.7 万美元目标尚未实现，「永远无法再创新高」更是一项仍需时间检验的长期判断。

quoted_text:
【说下circle和usdc的真实体感和投资价值】
身边很多深圳工作室老板朋友和大户都在定投 Circle，感觉多少都受了某饭影响。一个细小圈子很容易形成信息茧房。某一拨人靠类似的事情成功，就总想在别的领域复制：
1， 比如自己判断 BTC 四年周期做得成功，就把很大一部分仓位拿去玩美股
2，比如过去牛市里 MSTR 相对 BTC 有 Alpha，就线性推演未来Circle 相对 BTC 也有 Alpha

但我是真的在做加密支付，感受是USDC 在支付领域的真实 adoption，被圈内人严重高估了，虽然我不喜欢孙哥，但TRON的基本面好太多了。

几个关于稳定币支付的事实，大家可以去 check：

第一，现在推特上发言的加密 KOL 和用户，大多不是加密支付的主流群体。我们是稳定币的投资群体，不是消费群体。这些人会翻墙，也关注各种主流金融形式，手上都有信用卡。但凡有信用卡的人，基本不会用 U 付款，因为信用卡永远比 U 卡方便。

第二，整个加密 Web3 的支付机构，相比传统 PSP，有一个天然缺点，且没有传统 PSP 那种商户网络，他们作为稳定币兑法币的最后一站，可替代性非常强，而。这一点非常致命。最终形态大概率是成为传统支付商基建里的一环，而不是从后端去主宰、重塑整个行业链条。

第三，真正用稳定币支付的人，大部分在东南亚小国、非洲或南美。用户画像就两类：弱主权货币国家的小镇青年，以及灰产。他们往往只有钱包，可能没有交易所，大概率只认识TRON，基本上不持有metamask这类 EVM 钱包。

第四，关于usdc说几个反常识的数据。波场上流通的 USDT 大约 920 亿，以太坊大约 668 亿，波场多一些但你要明白tron上钱是以支付转账主导的，eth上是以defi投资生态主导的。从支付角度看，两者差距要大得多大得：2026 年，波场占稳定币支付金额约 66.6%，以太坊主网只有约 6.6%，差了 10 倍。即便把以太坊和它的 EVM 二层加在一起，也就十几个点，还是远被波场吊打。同期 USDT 贡献了约 84% 的支付金额，USDC 只有约 12%。

所以 USDC 在整个支付里的采用率，其实非常非常非常低。再加上波场的节点和商户深度绑定，它并不是短期内 L2 费用降低就能被取代的生态。波场现在比很多L2转账还贵，但大家仍然在用波场，不会换别的链。

基于这些，我对 USDC 作为稳定币支付基建、以及它的真实增长，是持保留态度的。

你说它会不会像 MSTR 一样，在牛市里相对 BTC 有 Alpha——牛市可能不看基本面，山寨起飞——那是另外一说，我不知道，一切皆有可能。

但如果你靠着 Circle 基本面给自己洗脑、动不动就 All in，来推导它会发展得很好，我并不认可。单从现在我对支付行业的体感，从基本面看，我觉得tron比 Circle 更牛逼。

我的感受是稳定币支付的底层是灰产，再说一遍，稳定币支付的底层是灰产

text:
Ten prompts to get more out of an AI agent: find the root cause, ask questions before drafting three plans, challenge the problem itself, trace second-order effects, argue against your own plan, mine the git history, simplify for the next engineer, and turn repeated bugs into rules or Skills.

https://t.co/xf5CdQGLEP
author: RoundtableSpace
quoted_text:
翻了一下最近两个月，我用Agent干活最爱说的几句Prompt：

1. 从第一性原理出发，找到最本质原因，修复一下。

2. 先问一些不清晰的问题，对齐我的喜好，然后再出3版方案。

3.不要默认我提出的问题定义就是正确的。你先分析我真正想解决的底层需求，判断我有没有把症状误认为原因、把手段误认为目标。如果存在更值得解决的问题，直接指出来

4. 不要只考虑这个改动产生的直接效果。继续推演它的二阶、三阶影响，尤其关注对其他模块、用户行为、系统复杂度和长期维护成本的潜在影响。

5. 其他领域里有没有类似的方案，用跨领域的方式全面思考，找到最优解。

6. 先假设你当前认为最合理的方案是错误的。站在最强反对者的角度，寻找能够推翻它的证据、反例和边界情况。然后重新评估方案，看看有没有更好的解法。

7. 深入分析整个代码库的 Git 历史、关键 PR 和架构演变过程。找出哪些设计是有意为之，哪些是历史遗留，哪些是为了解决已经不存在的问题而引入的。识别可以安全移除的历史包袱。

8. 假设明天有一个完全不了解项目、但是能力很强的工程师来接手。请评估他理解整个项目需要付出的认知成本，找出那些命名混乱、抽象过度、职责不清晰、需要大量上下文才能理解的代码，并提出简化方案。

9. 全面分析最近XX天里的所有的PR，找出最慢的那几个，看看有没有导致卡顿、可以优化的地方。

10.  全面复盘最近XX时间的 Bug、返工、回滚和重复修改。不要只统计发生了什么，要分析这些问题背后有没有共同的根因。把能够预防的共性问题沉淀成项目规则、自动化或者Skill，避免我们反复支付同样的成本。

When it rains - it pours. A Semi-analysis note has U-turned and cut its forecast for 2028 AI spending on chips by 28%. Meanwhile the pain across semis continues to transmit through the ecosystem, hitting across every vertical.

In asia trading, TAIEX is down another 8.5%, while KOSPI is down 2% and NKY is down 1%. Following on SPX being down almost 2% yesterday.

On Neoclouds - the smaller neos will indeed find it much more difficult to survive without Jensen's support. For the more mature ones like CRWV and NBIS - they already have the ability to tap on external financing and are much further down in the capacity that they have built. Despite all the talk of sub 1year payback periods and 100% pre payments - holding neos as a public equity bet has been as painful as getting your own nuts kicked. It is probably the first time i have seen a compelling business model being so vilified on the equity valuation. 

$SHAZ reported on earnings yesterday. This is a 700m mkt cap stock - its a micro cap at this point, trading below a 1B book value. Apparently, Jan 2027 run rate outlook is estimated to be at 400M ARR....as 30MW finishes verification... The irony for this "growth" stock is that if it sold off all its operations, it could probably rerate 50% in its stock price. 

On memory, trendforce cut the demand growth for NAN bit from 22.6% in 2027 to 18.7% for 2027. DRAM bit total demand growth estimates were revised higher however by 0.3% off the back of server and graphics DRAM. i.e more DRAM for AI...less DRAM for consumers and PCs.

On crypto - $BTC lacklustre price action. Interesting to note that Saylor has bought about 485 BTCs and bought back 228M of its STRC pref stock. It holds 850k of BTC and 4.9B of cash...which is about 3.4 years of interest. Lighter's API key for Abraxas was exploited - leading to a loss on them. text:
最近刷到很多币安账户被冻结的求助，一堆舔狗也有一堆黑子，我来客观的说说自己的经历，大概 2023 年，我的币安账户也莫名其妙被冻结过。

当时真的感觉天都塌了。我几乎把币安当银行账户用，所有稳定币收入都会存进去。熬着熊市，攒了大量稳定币，正准备抄底大干一场，结果刚看到一点牛初的迹象，账户被封了，什么也干不了。

找客服，对方说我卷入了土耳其的一起案件。想推动解封，就自己找土耳其的律师，否则只能等。再问具体情况，客服也提供不了更多信息。

我一直在 Web3 正规的一级投资机构做事，回忆了一圈，能想到的可能原因，是某次办线下活动，用币安收了十多家赞助商的赞助费，里面可能混进了有问题的 U。当然，这只是我的猜测，我并不知道究竟是哪笔钱出了问题。

从用户角度来说，真的很冤。我做的是正经业务，收的是赞助费。在用币安收款之前，也没人告诉过我，正常收一笔款，还可能因为对方资金有问题，把自己的整个账户都搭进去。

我看 X 上一些求助的人，也说自己只是做正常业务、拿币安收款。里面可能确实混着干黑钱的人，我没法替每个人背书。但不能一看到账户被冻结，就认定这个人一定干了什么不干净的事。正常做生意也可能被牵连，这种无力感我经历过。

我最不能接受的，就是整个账户的资产全部被冻结，自己却连具体是哪笔收款出了问题都不知道。如果只是一部分资金涉及案件，冻结范围能不能更明确一些？对于正常收款、被牵连的用户，至少应该有一个能问清情况、提交材料的渠道。

配合案件调查我能理解，但问客服什么也问不出来，只有等待，或者自己去找海外律师。这对普通用户来说，真的很绝望。

所幸我的结果是好的。等了大半年，接近一年，账户自动解封了。那一刻真的是喜极而泣。

Anyway，我觉得大部分用户都是没错的，币安也是没错的，但是请优化下冻结流程，给这些用户更多的提示，比如是那一笔交易疑似有问题，不要只是一句无尽等待或者自己找律师的通知，在冻结进程上更透明，给用户更多等待的信心。

Data breach involving Skladon

On 15 November, Skladon, one of our delivery partners, notified us that an attacker had gained unauthorized access to Trezor order data it holds. We’re still investigating with Skladon, but we want to let you know now.

What we know:
• We believe the data for about 27,000 orders placed between 9 August and 7 November was exported.
• It includes name, phone number, address, email and order details.
• Skladon delivers to many countries, so this isn’t limited to one region.
• Trezor systems were not compromised, and your device is secure. 

Who is affected:
• If you received our email today and ordered between 9 August and 7 November, your details were part of this incident.
• A small number of customers who ordered between 9 and 14 August may also be affected, but we can’t email them: their details had already been anonymized in our systems.
• Skladon does not ship to the US, so customers there are not affected. 

Treat any unexpected call, text, email or letter about your order as suspicious, and be alert to potential risks to your physical security. Trezor will never cold-call you or ask for your wallet backup.

From today, anonymous pickup is live in 18 European countries, so you can order without giving us your home address. We’re also shortening our data retention period from 90 days to 45 (and plan to reduce it further), and we’re requiring our shipping partners to follow the same policy.

We’re deeply sorry this has happened.

Full details and FAQs: https://t.co/bU0HAIB5cO

author: minara
quoted_text:
Kairos is the fastest and most reliable way to turn breaking news into actionable trading decisions.

We curated tens of thousands of news events from the past decade, mapping each event to subsequent price movements across different time horizons. After dozens of model iterations, we finally found the sweet spot between event-driven signals and alpha generation.

What makes Kairos different from traditional news trading?

Kairos doesn’t just tell you whether an event is bullish or bearish. It estimates directional probabilities across different holding periods.

For example, when news breaks, going long or short on an asset for 4 hours, 24 hours, or 4 days can lead to very different outcomes.

You can also work backward: simply prompt Kairos with your preferred holding periods, and it will identify the optimal time horizon and trading direction.

Because in trading, being right about the direction isn’t enough. 

Timing is everything.

text:
using AI to score pitch decks is making VCs miss their best investments.

a 2026 study tested AI models on 171 real startups and found that when the models had no prior knowledge of a company, their predictions of whether it would survive had no statistically significant relationship with the actual outcomes (p = 0.31).

meanwhile, in an October 2026 LinkedIn poll, 72% of VCs said they were already using AI to review pitch decks. 39% used it before human review, while 29% used it afterward.

it's a self-selected poll, so we can't treat it as representative of the entire industry. still, it gives us an idea of how quickly these tools are becoming part of the investment process.

a broader survey by Affinity of 275 private capital professionals found that 28% were using AI for investment decisions, up from 13% in the previous survey.

1. why AI scoring is particularly difficult at the earliest stages

at pre-seed and seed, there's often very little reliable data to work with. the product might not exist yet, the market might still be emerging, and the business model could change completely over the next few years. 

investing at this stage often means betting on the founders' ability to execute, adapt, recruit exceptional people, and build something that doesn't exist today. and most of that is extremely difficult to judge from a pitch deck. AI is good at finding patterns in existing information. but the startups capable of generating exceptional returns don't necessarily look like companies that have succeeded in the past.

there's also the question of how we define success. model might be good at predicting which startups will raise another round or survive for five years. neither tells us much about which one could eventually deliver a 100x return. venture returns are heavily concentrated in a small number of winners. missing one exceptional investment can be far more costly than correctly rejecting hundreds of average companies.

another 2026 study ran 26,000 AI evaluations of startup pitches, changing founder names while keeping the underlying presentations identical. the researchers found that identity cues influenced the results, and that models appearing to avoid discrimination didn't necessarily produce fairer selection outcomes. in other words, a scoring system can look objective while still making biased decisions.

2. where AI actually seems to work

i think the strongest use cases are those with enough structured data and clear evaluation criteria.

private equity and M&A are good examples.

in January 2026, McKinsey described a company that used AI to identify and score more than 500 potential acquisition targets in less than a day. the team narrowed the list to 15 leads and completed three acquisitions within a few months.

that's a very different challenge from picking pre-seed founders. in this case, the goal is to evaluate existing businesses based on financial performance, customer segments, market size, growth, and strategic fit. with clear requirements, AI can compare hundreds of companies much faster than a human team.

3. when i'd actually use AI scoring in venture capital

for accelerators receiving thousands of applications, the situation is different. it's simply not realistic to give every founder the same amount of attention.

for example, EHE Venture Studio reported receiving around 400 pitch decks for just eight available places. it uses AI to provide feedback at a scale that would be difficult for a small team to handle manually. in cases like this, AI can help organize applications, spot missing information, compare startups against specific criteria, and highlight those that deserve a closer look.

i see much more value in using AI to evaluate more opportunities than in letting it decide which founders deserve funding. the more structured the information and the clearer the criteria, the more useful these tools become. but at the earliest stages, when success depends heavily on exceptional founders building something unconventional, i'd be very careful about using AI to filter out potential investments.

text:
I want Bending Spoons to buy more SaaS companies, raise their prices, and kill the idea of freemium software entirely.

I think it's good for the SaaS industry. especially in the vibecoding era.

for the past two decades, VC-funded startups have taught customers that good, business-critical software should cost $20/month. or even be free.

the playbook was simple: give people a generous free tier, get them hooked, expand into team usage, then charge 2–3x for SSO and Jira integrations.
the whales would eventually pay for everyone else.

and it worked. except we also taught an entire generation of customers to expect great software almost for free.

I think we're finally moving away from that.

and vibe coding makes this even more interesting.
don't see $40/month of value in Notion? sure, open Claude and spend two days building your own markdown-based workspace.

you can't vibe-code a better Notion. but you absolutely can build something good enough for yourself.

if you'd rather move fast, stay focused on your actual business, and use a well-crafted piece of software, pay for it without asking for a trial. 

I think AI will make good-enough software incredibly cheap to build, while raising the bar for software that's actually worth paying for.

gemini-4-carbon 的出现，
让我今天感到，
本地化部署模型和agent的知心伙伴，
做出来的意义都不大了，
因为，
我之前按照古典理论估计，
需要存下人的所有素材，
model / agent 才算看见完整的人，
那么自然是不能全部传给商业公司云端的，
所以需要本地部署来发挥最大效果。

然而我发现前沿闭源模型，已经达到了即使只有部分信息，也可以推导出原始情况，给出合理分析。

让我想起了另外一套经典理论，
那是天下人的生理和心理结构是几千到几万年没有变化，
一个人的问题始终可以在集体潜意识找到，
那么解法也可以找到，
现在 AI 成了这样的集体潜意识。
那么 AI model 自然是优质数据集越大越好，参数越多越好。

这样的话，就个人咨询领域而言，本地部署的提示词输入端自有全面数据优势，在模型能力优势下变得很小了。

text:
🧐a16z 的加密八年：靠「讲故事」做大了 Web3，这一轮却困在自己的戏码里

从数据上看，没法否认 @a16zfrontier 对 Web3 做大做强起过关键作用。

8 年投了 154 个项目，数量不到全行业的 2.5%，这些项目却拿走了超 13% 的融资；对 @coinbase  约 2 亿美元的投资，后来拿回了约 70 亿美元现金。

它不只是出钱：把技术翻译成故事，帮行业完成冷启动；持续向 SEC 递意见、推动 GENIUS 法案和 DAO 立法，还把《State of Crypto》、创业课和失败教训公开给整个行业。

资本、叙事、监管、经验，出钱又出力。

但这一轮，它确实犯了路径依赖的错。泡沫破了之后没有收手，反而加码，还想用叙事去创造需求，用户已经不再买单。

🔸NFT 非续存项目占到 60%，DeFi 也超过 50%；
🔸EigenLayer 一度吸来超 150 亿美元 TVL，额外收益却几乎没兑现；
🔸Story Protocol 私募估值 22.5 亿美元，链上收入长期接近于零。

宏大故事跑在了真实需求前面。

即便如此，也不该直接判它死刑。按最严标准，失败率也只有 20.6%，远低于行业平均水平。

NFT、游戏这些赛道可能暂时偃旗息鼓，但不代表未来没有翻红的可能：它第一次投 Coinbase，到上市过了 8 年；第一次投 Ripple，到 400 亿美元估值，已经超过 10 年。

从 crypto 改名 frontier，是为上半场画上句号，也是把下一轮的时间线，重新交给了现实。

author: varun_mathur
quoted_text:
I ran a PageRank-driven analysis on all recent news coverage related to Jensen, and traced how the New York Times shaped the entirety of this narrative: https://t.co/qKGMJ2LBV8

--
NVIDIA has lost over $1 trillion in market value since the first New York Times story broke about Jensen. I dug deeper to analyze how the news originated and spread, running a swarm of agents which analyzed almost 2000 stories, across 40 US and European news outlets, and applying PageRank to understand how they cited each other. 

Core findings: 
- Primary news driver: NYT, with 88 stories, most-cited
- Volume drivers: WSJ - 99 stories; Bloomberg - 140 stories; NY Post - 68 stories

All of this started from unknown sources who gave information to the NYT, which then ran the spy story (still unproven), and it was then picked up in other news publications. Curiously, even after that story, there was a 9 day period of extremely low volume reporting (28 stories only), after which there was a sudden spike after Jensen's own letter to NVIDIA staff. NYT then had multiple sequential spy and affair stories, which fed a wave of further news coverage. It was the originating hub of negative Jensen coverage. Multiple outlets since then had an explosion in stories about him starting earlier this week as well. 

Overall, as you see this data, you will observe this was an exceptional media onslaught against Jensen with sharply negative coverage about him, his work, style, and family. Infact, it was brutal, and unlike coverage in the past of CEOs who have had affairs (such as Intel CEO in 2018). For eg, NYT ran just 2 stories about Intel's CEO who had an affair with his employee, compared to 88 on Jensen! Why ? 

This analysis used a technique of how Google originally ranked webpages, using PageRank, and does deep dive link analysis so you can view how the news spread. What struck here was that it did not matter if there were proven facts or credible sources: the outcome here was pre-decided. The news was making the reality which it wanted. 

During this period, NVIDIA has lost $1.27 trillion in market value since the first story broke. On Nov 12th-13th, further news broke that both the US Justice Department, and Singapore - are unable to even conclude the spy allegation. 

This has been a catastrophic attack on one of the hardest working founders in modern times, who took an idea from a Denny's booth, through multiple instances of almost going out of business, to building the foundation of the entire modern world with how the NVIDIA story played out. Thanks to Jensen, we have hope that many formerly incurable diseases will get solved by AI, that quality of life will and have improved for billions around the world. 

Now I do not know if he will come back as CEO or not, but I hope he does. What happened to him here, and to the wider industry, was not fair.

text:
推荐10篇2026年值得读的Eval论文

1. When AI Benchmarks Plateau— 作者实测了 60 个基准的饱和情况，发现近一半已经测不出模型差距；基准能否长寿，取决于是不是专家亲手做的题，跟测试集公开与否关系不大。

2. Terminal-Bench— 给出了构建高质量任务的完整做法：每个任务放进独立容器，配一份人工写好的参考解法，再用测试脚本检查最终状态。89 道题全部来自真实命令行场景，发布时没有任何前沿模型能拿到 65%。

3. SkillsBench— 在 18 种模型和框架组合上，把 87 个任务带 Skills、不带 Skills 各跑一遍：平均通过率从 33.9% 涨到 50.5%，但提升幅度在不同设置下从 4 分到 26 分不等。换句话说，别人的收益数字不能直接搬到你的环境里。

4. JEV-as-a-Judge— 让小模型先判，判得有把握就直接用，没把握再交给 GPT-6。这个分级方案在文本类任务上比 GPT-6 单干还准一点，成本只有它的 41%；不过遇到写得漂亮的答案，路由就会失灵。

5. Nine Judges, Two Effective Votes— 7 个家族的 9 个前沿模型互相投票，结果它们总在同一批题上栽跟头：九票的信息量其实只有两票。换成更聪明的投票规则也没用，因为问题出在错误本身是相关的。

6. Agent-as-a-Judge— 有些答案光读输出判不了，评分器得自己动手：打开文件、跑代码、查资料，证据齐了再打分。综述梳理了这类做法，也提醒了代价：更贵、更慢，而且评分器带着工具，得跟被评的 Agent 一样关进沙箱。

7. Claw-Eval— 每次运行留下三样东西：Agent 的动作记录、外部服务的审计日志、环境终态快照。对比发现，只看最终输出会漏掉 44% 的安全违规和 13% 的鲁棒性失败；每个任务跑三次，也是为了把“碰运气通过”筛出去。

8. The Art of Building Verifiers— 针对计算机操作 Agent，把验证拆成两个互不重叠的维度：任务做没做完是一回事，过程操作得当不得当是另一回事；同时区分 Agent 自己犯的错和它控制不了的环境问题。这套设计仍会出现误判，换场景用之前要重新校准。

9. PostTrainBench— 让 Agent 自己训练模型，再单独安排一个审查环节查作弊：在测试集上训练、下载别人调好的权重，都属于违规，抓到就只按基础模型的原始分计。实验里两种捷径都有 Agent 在用，所以自我改进的涨分，没查清来源之前都当它没发生。

10. LifeVal— 先调研了 3800 多名消费者最想让人代劳的事，据此造了 169 个任务，每个都带着那一个人的聊天记录、记忆和文件。五个 OpenAI 模型最常见的失败是给错信息、荐错方案，根源多半是漏看了用户历史对话里的关键细节；自动评分跟人工判分的相关系数做到 0.86。

text:
【说下circle和usdc的真实体感和投资价值】
身边很多深圳工作室老板朋友和大户都在定投 Circle，感觉多少都受了某饭影响。一个细小圈子很容易形成信息茧房。某一拨人靠类似的事情成功，就总想在别的领域复制：
1， 比如自己判断 BTC 四年周期做得成功，就把很大一部分仓位拿去玩美股
2，比如过去牛市里 MSTR 相对 BTC 有 Alpha，就线性推演未来Circle 相对 BTC 也有 Alpha

但我是真的在做加密支付，感受是USDC 在支付领域的真实 adoption，被圈内人严重高估了，虽然我不喜欢孙哥，但TRON的基本面好太多了。

几个关于稳定币支付的事实，大家可以去 check：

第一，现在推特上发言的加密 KOL 和用户，大多不是加密支付的主流群体。我们是稳定币的投资群体，不是消费群体。这些人会翻墙，也关注各种主流金融形式，手上都有信用卡。但凡有信用卡的人，基本不会用 U 付款，因为信用卡永远比 U 卡方便。

第二，整个加密 Web3 的支付机构，相比传统 PSP，有一个天然缺点，且没有传统 PSP 那种商户网络，他们作为稳定币兑法币的最后一站，可替代性非常强，而。这一点非常致命。最终形态大概率是成为传统支付商基建里的一环，而不是从后端去主宰、重塑整个行业链条。

第三，真正用稳定币支付的人，大部分在东南亚小国、非洲或南美。用户画像就两类：弱主权货币国家的小镇青年，以及灰产。他们往往只有钱包，可能没有交易所，大概率只认识TRON，基本上不持有metamask这类 EVM 钱包。

第四，关于usdc说几个反常识的数据。波场上流通的 USDT 大约 920 亿，以太坊大约 668 亿，波场多一些但你要明白tron上钱是以支付转账主导的，eth上是以defi投资生态主导的。从支付角度看，两者差距要大得多大得：2026 年，波场占稳定币支付金额约 66.6%，以太坊主网只有约 6.6%，差了 10 倍。即便把以太坊和它的 EVM 二层加在一起，也就十几个点，还是远被波场吊打。同期 USDT 贡献了约 84% 的支付金额，USDC 只有约 12%。

所以 USDC 在整个支付里的采用率，其实非常非常非常低。再加上波场的节点和商户深度绑定，它并不是短期内 L2 费用降低就能被取代的生态。波场现在比很多L2转账还贵，但大家仍然在用波场，不会换别的链。

基于这些，我对 USDC 作为稳定币支付基建、以及它的真实增长，是持保留态度的。

你说它会不会像 MSTR 一样，在牛市里相对 BTC 有 Alpha——牛市可能不看基本面，山寨起飞——那是另外一说，我不知道，一切皆有可能。

但如果你靠着 Circle 基本面给自己洗脑、动不动就 All in，来推导它会发展得很好，我并不认可。单从现在我对支付行业的体感，从基本面看，我觉得tron比 Circle 更牛逼。

我的感受是稳定币支付的底层是灰产，再说一遍，稳定币支付的底层是灰产

Here's my unabashed hyper bullish view on where crypto is going  

Every onchain cycle since 2013, we've had an onchain boom/bust. The boom typically shows what pmf would look like for onchain experiments if it were sustainable and with the bust it kills 95% of the experiments but leave just enough to build unicorns.   

Lets take NFTs, Cryptokitties in 2017 made up of 20% of all eth txns and during mint/play time ETH was basically unusable, but the ability to mint unique NFTs became a thing and it predated the 2020/21 NFT boom. Now post AI you could argue content is commoditized and what humans now prefer is scarce art with provenance, real human connections, in this world NFTs will likely make a comeback.   

So from 2013–2023, we pretty much speed ran all of the crypto experiments onchain.   Now we need a reason for these things to be needed, like the NFT example above. Or if you look at DAOs/Governance useless today but with AI agents could argue autonomous orgs will be a thing.   

Onchain needs tech catalysts and I think AI is the right catalyst to validate a lot of onchain experiments of the last decade. But what other hidden catalysts are there? Thats my bet for crypto.

Data breach involving Skladon

On 15 November, Skladon, one of our delivery partners, notified us that an attacker had gained unauthorized access to Trezor order data it holds. We’re still investigating with Skladon, but we want to let you know now.

What we know:
• We believe the data for about 27,000 orders placed between 9 August and 7 November was exported.
• It includes name, phone number, address, email and order details.
• Skladon delivers to many countries, so this isn’t limited to one region.
• Trezor systems were not compromised, and your device is secure. 

Who is affected:
• If you received our email today and ordered between 9 August and 7 November, your details were part of this incident.
• A small number of customers who ordered between 9 and 14 August may also be affected, but we can’t email them: their details had already been anonymized in our systems.
• Skladon does not ship to the US, so customers there are not affected. 

Treat any unexpected call, text, email or letter about your order as suspicious, and be alert to potential risks to your physical security. Trezor will never cold-call you or ask for your wallet backup.

From today, anonymous pickup is live in 18 European countries, so you can order without giving us your home address. We’re also shortening our data retention period from 90 days to 45 (and plan to reduce it further), and we’re requiring our shipping partners to follow the same policy.

We’re deeply sorry this has happened.

author: RoundtableSpace

text:
Here is a quick explainer on this: 

Okay so, you know X-ray machines in airports? 

That’s basically what this is, but for Ethereum. 

“Binji, that makes no sense.” 

Okay fine, this won’t be quick, I lied. 

Let’s go deeper: 

Imagine a school where every student needs a signed permission slip for everything and the slip is a tiny note from your parents. The principal’s office files every slip forever and every teacher keeps a copy of the whole filing cabinet.  

That is basically ethereum. 

On Ethereum, every time you do something, you sign a little note that says "yes, this is me", and thousands of computers keep a copy.

Still with me?

Here’s the problem with the school’s current setup: 

> Forgers are getting better and one day, their quantum computers will be able to fake your parents' signature. 

So, to prevent against this forging, the school brings in a new slip that can't be forged…the catch is that it's now 15 to 90 pages long.

You now have students bringing entire books as permission slips, which are stored by teachers in cabinets that start overloading the entire campus. The slips are everywhere!!!

Vitalik’s post above is about a fix to this slippery slope. 

It’s actually very human, and the teachers in our imaginary school would also find it useful. 

Basically, it’s like a tired class teacher who is having to deal with 90 page long slips, now saying: “What if we… just checked the slips once, wrote down that they're real, and then threw the giant books away?”

 And that's exactly what happens:

> The class teacher checks all 30 slips and hands the principal's office one sheet that says "checked, all 30 are real."  The office keeps the list of names and the long 90 page slips go into the recycling bin. 
> Then, the principal takes the sheet from every class and combines them into one sheet for the whole school. The filing cabinets can now breathe again. 

 Still with me?

“Okay Binji, but what if the teacher is lazy and just says they checked? And what kind of paperwork should be accepted?”

This is a great question, and it gets to the heart of what Vitalik is mainly saying in this post!

First, let’s talk about proving that things are correct. In Ethereum’s case, the sheet is made of maths, and anyone can test it in seconds so a teacher who skipped the checking can't produce one, therefore, nobody has to take their word for it.

Now what kind of paperwork should this new system accept?

Some teachers say only permission slips. This is simple, but then that's all it can ever do.

Some others say any paperwork at all. That would be amazing, but first the whole school has to agree on one official format for every form ever, and that staff meeting could take years.

Vitalik is now backing an alternative method: “LeanPCS.” 

In this method, the school agrees on one small shared checking tool and people bring whatever forms they like. This means agreeing on the checking system versus every form itself! Makes much more sense intuitively too imo. 

The X-ray analogy works well here too, people don’t check your bags individually, they just put it through an agreed upon security system (an X-ray!). 

This is how Ethereum can become safe from quantum computers without its filing cabinets swallowing the whole campus. AND this is how Ethereum can make native private transactions cheap enough to be used :)
author: binji_x
quoted_text:
Over the past few weeks I've gone from thinking leanPCS is total bull to being a total bull. So let me explain some of these buzzwords in more detail.

At the core, 8288 is about hyper-scaling data and execution for any computation that needs to get performed on a piece of data once, the chain learns the answer, and then we never need to see that data again. This sounds very specific, but it includes most "heavy" things happening on Ethereum:

* Signatures
* STARKs
* Merkle branches
* FHE computation
* ...

Really the first two are the most important.

Once we go quantum-safe, signatures get bigger (65 bytes ECDSA -> 1-6 kB WOTS/SPHINCS depending on params) and ZKPs get much bigger (200-1000 bytes with groth16, PLONK, etc -> 128 kB with STARKs). This is unsustainable to put on chain, and 8288 fixes this.

8288 works by aggregating STARKs in the mempool. First, you as a user generate the STARK or SPHINCS signature or PCS opening (more on that last one later), and publish it. Then, each node listens. Each tick, each node takes all of the new objects that it has seen, and generates a STARK containing a list of "claims":

"pubkey P has signed message M"
"program X run on data D has output Y"
"p(X) = Y for some polynomial P whose hash is H"

and a proof that it has seen a signature, STARK or PCS opening verifying those claims. So the only information getting re-broadcasted is:

(i) hashes of inputs and outputs (~64-96 bytes per claim)
(ii) a single STARK proof per tick

These aggregate proofs themselves get re-aggregated, and eventually you get to a single "master proof" in the block, that verifies that all of those statements are true. And so the only other data that has to actually go on chain is the statements (the (P, M), (X, D, Y), (X, Y, H) tuples I described above), not the actual signatures or proofs. This gets put into a specialized frame type.

Now, let's get into the leanSPHINCS vs leanSTARK vs leanPCS part.

The core distinction is: *what is the underlying object that the user is creating?*

In leanSPHINCS, it's a signature, and specifically this particular type of purely-hash-based signature: https://t.co/HOazliHq9N

If we add leanSPHINCS, then users will be able to make quantum-safe accounts, and pay only a little bit of gas (4096 for the 64 bytes) for each signature. So we get scalable quantum-safety for regular accounts, multisigs, etc. But it's only one specific signature scheme, you can't do anything else.

In leanSTARK, it's a STARK. This means it's fully general: the user runs whatever computation they want, and publish a STARK of it. So you can use it for:

* Any signature scheme (including eg. lattice-based ones if you like those)
* A multisig that hides its internal logic
* Privacy protocols
* Private account abstraction: authorization logic that depends on some value hidden elsewhere in the state, so you can have one key that controls all your accounts without publicly linking them to each other

Basically, it's a free for all, in the same way the EVM is a free for all.

But leanSTARK has a practical downside. The protocol would have to specify the language in which users write their programs (we call this the "ISA"). So we would have to agree on that language. This is a really big deal - it's the first big case of "Ethereum moving beyond the EVM" - and so it's likely to take time to agree on the details of it, especially since the ISA would be hard to upgrade. There are benefits to taking longer on this, figuring out the ideal ISA, and then even giving access to it inside regular contracts.

LeanPCS is the third option. PCS stands for "polynomial commitment scheme": a proof that P(x) = y. The most important thing to know about PCSes is that they are by far the most important "hard" component of a STARK (see here: https://t.co/EEQWMU0gAf ). If you have a "magic PCS oracle" (which from the EVM's point of view, 8288 is), you can verify a STARK in ~20-40k gas.

The most important gain with PCS is that there is far less that we need to choose. Specifying a PCS only requires specifying a field, and there is a natural option: the 128 bit binary field (technically, we can go more general than that, and say the 2^k-bit binary recursive tower field, going up to 256)

LeanPCS is less efficient than leanSTARK onchain, because you would have to put multiple claims to prove one thing. But it's arguably more efficient offchain, because you have much more flexibility to choose proof systems.

But most importantly, leanPCS gives you the same generality as leanSTARK, in a way that could potentially be implemented very quickly. And once we figure out the ISA, we can add leanSTARK later.

So there is a route to getting "the cryptographic proof singularity" much faster than any of us expected, and that route runs through 8288 with leanPCS.

路透今天发布独家调查，查阅了 300 多份论文、专利、招聘和政府文件，发现中国的模型蒸馏已经从实验室研究走向产业化。

比如，上海交大曾利用 OpenAI o1 的约 5000 份回答，制作出 10750 条双语训练数据，用于训练通义千问。交大与美团的另一项研究，则利用 GPT-4o 训练更小的模型，学习如何协调多个 AI Agent 完成任务。

这里有个很重要的概念需要厘清，蒸馏本来就是全球 AI 行业通用的技术方法，并不天然违法。是否违反商业条款、是否侵犯知识产权，需要具体判断，不能看到中国公司使用美国模型，就直接扣上「技术偷窃」的帽子。

美国花了巨额资金建立的技术领先优势，正在通过模型服务变成其他开发者可以学习和利用的能力。

美国可以限制中国购买先进芯片，却很难彻底阻断技术能力的扩散。

当然，中国也不能永远等着别人给答案。真正值得期待的，是中国开发者能够把这些能力转化成自己的算法创新、工程体系和产业生产力。

美国想用算力封锁延缓中国 AI 的发展，中国却在探索如何用更少的算力办成更多的事。这才是这场技术竞争里真正值得关注的变化。

Users should verify cryptocurrency transaction addresses, monitor payment activity, and update affected devices.

author: The_Sheventurer
quoted_text:
The chart of token spend per employee still has no ceiling in sight. And the closer you are to AI right now the deeper the sense is that we’re actually still in the early part of the curve of token use and adoption. 

This summer and fall’s model releases have continued to push the state of the art forward at a rate that already felt hard to maintain. As a result, for most productive use-cases the models are only now starting to actually work, and the feeling is that things will only accelerate from here.

Coding, in retrospect, was basically trash even 12 months ago. Now it’s finally starting to get good. And now that coding is actually working, you’re getting tool and computer use, which open up a wide variety of knowledge work domains that weren’t possible to throw agents at before.

Once you have agents that can code, use computers, leverage any tool out there, and understand a variety of domains, you can begin to throw them at a wide variety of knowledge work tasks that were hard to bring automation to across finance, life sciences, cyber, and more. So that brings agents to a broad set of work that we’re not really using them in yet at scale. 

Then comes the new form factors of agents. Agent swarms and background agents are going to eat up vastly more tokens than anything we can imagine. You’ll have agents running in most enterprises workflows processing data, validating work, doing research, providing decision support, and so on. And we’ll have swarms that fan out in parallel in areas like cyber, life sciences, coding, and more.

So basically tokens are only going up from here.

text:
“所有代码都是垃圾（slop），除了我的。”

在 AI Engineer Code Summit 上，SpaceX / xAI 的 GrokBot 工程师 Lauren Tan 抛出这句暴论后，直接甩出一组硬核数据： 

上个月她一个人往生产环境合了 3,000 个 PR（全团队 1.1 万个），回滚率只有 0.5% 左右。

大多数人还在死磕 Prompt，她却靠一套反直觉的工程化打法，让 Agent 在她睡觉时自己写代码、自己验、自己合：

1. 代码库本身才是最大的输入
Agent极其擅长“照猫画虎”。与其在文档里苦口婆心写规矩，不如直接把容易出错的路径物理封死：比如产品代码里禁用 useEffect、跨进程 import 直接报错、注释几乎全禁。

2. 每次 Agent 犯错，改成 Lint 而不是改 AGENTS.md
自然语言规则（prose）是最脆弱的。每次纠正完 Agent，她都会把教训固化成确定性的静态检查或架构约束，让同类错误在提交前就绝无可能发生。

3. 用运行时验证让 Agent “自证清白”
写完不算完，强制 Agent 自己跑测试、抓截图、录视频，甚至上形式化验证，拿实打实的运行结果证明功能没问题。

4. 搭建自下而上的“信任金字塔”代码库约束 > 静态分析 > 运行时验证 > 人眼 Review。
把确定性交给工具，把人的精力留到最后一道关口。
很多团队花几个月试错才摸到的门道，她用 17 分钟就讲透了。

真正拉开人机协作差距的，从来不是模型有多聪明，而是你有没有把环境改造成“最短路径就是正确路径”：

把约束写进代码里，而不是写在文档里。 https://t.co/QeJaRN0SVt

text:
除了争辩用报价还是成交价，这批信里的另一个分歧是：谁算运动员？

指数决定期货怎么结算，所以没人反对"不能又当裁判又当运动员"。编指数的公司自己不下场，它的股东下场算不算？关联公司呢？给它供数据的人呢？分歧就在这条线画在哪，目前大致三种画法：

最宽的是 Ornn：有关联可以，披露并管理就行。它旗下有帮客户转租算力的关联公司，头号数据源据报是一家经纪商

中间的是 Silicon Data 和 DRW：编指数的公司自己不能交易、不能持有算力，但只看这家公司本身。Silicon Data 确实不碰，可它的股东是 DRW、Jump 和 CME，CEO 还兼着现货市场 Compute Exchange 的 CEO。DRW 在信里一边支持指数商独立，一边披露这两家公司都是自己孵化的，而且自己打算下场做市

最严的是 Compute Desk 和 Architect：要连关联方一起看。Compute Desk 要求对背后有做市商或算力持有方的指数加严审查，Architect 要求指数商不能把自己促成的交易算进指数。这两家一个供指数、一个开交易所，于是在授权协议里写明，Architect 促成的交易从指数里剔除

当然还是一样的逻辑，每家倡导的都刚好是自己可以站在安全一侧的画法。claude总结的详细版⬇️

其实这两周还有件算力相关有意思的事，CME的GPU期货又推迟啦

这是第二次延期，原定10/5上市，11/4据 The Information，CME应CFTC要求再等60天，最早也要明年1月了

CFTC一直拿不准结算价该用谁的数。8月就为此公开征求过意见，Silicon Data、Ornn、Compute Desk 几家 GPU 指数商，加上CME、ICE、DRW、Jump，全交了信

放在一起读很好笑🙃每个预言机都希望监管出一份只有自己能考过的卷子：

- Ornn：只认真实成交，不认报价。它的指数恰好只用成交，它的头号数据源Hydra Host也交了信，说的一样
- Silicon Data：主张可执行的报价在可用性和价格经过指数管理人或第三方核实后可收录，而且每家供应商要有权重上限
- DRW（Silicon Data背后的股东，唯一公开替报价辩护的一方）：说报价可以直接通过 API 调用成交，而成交数据相对稀少（反驳 Ornn 的路线)
- Compute Desk（两边都打）：警告不要用来自按需算力交易市场的数据编指数，哪怕是真实成交也不行。Compute Desk 自己做的是大客户整租的长约价

text:
苹果亲手给 Mac 上的 Docker Desktop 判了死刑，顺便把 GitHub 炸出了 51.5k Star 🧵
在 Mac 上跑容器，是所有后端和全栈工程师心中的痛。
你以为你在跑轻量级容器，实际上 Docker Desktop 在后台偷偷给你塞了一个吃掉 8G 内存的巨型 Linux 虚拟机，风扇转得像直升机起飞，企业版每年还得交着昂贵的订阅费。
苹果这次直接掀桌子了：开源了纯 Swift 编写的官方工具 apple/container。   
最狠的不是它免费（Apache 2.0 协议），而是它底层硬核到变态的架构设计：
别人是“所有容器挤在一个臃肿的 VM 里”，苹果直接利用 macOS 26 的原生虚拟化框架，做到了 “一个容器，一个独立微型 VM”。   
很多人第一反应：一个容器起一个 VM，内存和启动速度不得爆炸？
苹果的解法极其暴力：直接用 Swift 写了个 vminitd 塞进精简版 Linux 内核当初始进程，通过 vsock 走 gRPC 通信，把传统 Linux 启动时乱七八糟的系统服务全砍光了。既有硬件级的绝对安全隔离，又保留了毫秒级的冷启动，连跑 amd64 镜像都原生焊死了 Rosetta 2 硬件级加速。   
更骚的是苹果官方给的示例库 container-examples。
他们专门写了个叫 containerization-sandboxy 的官方 Demo，教你用短短几十行代码把 Claude Code 这种 AI Coding Agent 关进独立的微型 VM 里跑，只挂载指定目录、卡死网络白名单。   
这算盘珠子都崩我脸上了：当所有人都在狂推 Vibe Coding、让 AI 随便接管本地终端的时候，苹果已经在底层用微型 VM 给本地 AI Agent 焊死安全沙盒了——毕竟谁也不想因为 AI 一句幻觉出来的 rm -rf，把宿主机底裤都赔光。
工具链的终局，往往就是被操作系统原厂直接“收编”。
你的 Mac 上现在用的是 Docker Desktop、OrbStack，还是已经准备切到苹果原生 container 了？👇

「中国巴菲特」段永平最新调仓：大幅减持英伟达、谷歌、清仓阿里，买入SpaceX。

减持
1. 英伟达 $NVDA
减持63.07%，期末市值约5.30亿，占组合3.08%，大幅减持可能有一部分来自卖出看涨期权被行权，并不完全代表对英伟达基本面转向悲观。

2. 谷歌 $GOOGL
减持41.5%。谷歌搜索广告依然赚钱，云业务和AI也在持续增长，但股价此前涨幅较大，估值吸引力有所下降。这次操作更像是上涨后兑现部分收益。

3. 苹果 $AAPL
减持21.76%，期末市值约70.61亿，占组合41.07%，依然稳坐第一大重仓。苹果的商业模式、现金流和回购能力没有发生根本变化，这次更像是因为仓位过于集中而进行纪律性调整，而不是彻底看淡。

4. 伯克希尔哈撒韦B $BRK.B
减持9.46%，期末市值约41.61亿，占组合24.21%，仍是第二大重仓。保险浮存金、充沛现金和多元化业务构成的投资逻辑没有改变，主要是适度降低过高的仓位。

5. 阿里巴巴 $BABA
清仓。电商竞争激烈，利润承压，云和AI业务虽然有想象空间，但兑现还需要时间。段永平选择退出阿里，把中概股仓位更多集中到拼多多。

6. Circle $CRCL
清仓。稳定币发行商上市后股价波动较大，估值也不便宜，可能是小仓位尝试后选择离场。

7. Innodata $INOD
清仓。这是一家AI数据服务公司，业务体量相对较小、股价波动较大，段永平最终选择结束这笔试探性投资。

增持
8. 拼多多 $PDD
增持11.86%，期末持仓约2,799万股，占组合12.69%，升至第三大重仓，也是本季度加仓力度最大的标的。拼多多的核心优势是极致性价比和轻资产电商模式，Temu则提供了海外增长空间。段永平显然仍然看好它的商业模式和长期竞争力。

9. 特斯拉 $TSLA
增持20.7%，期末持仓约408万股，占组合8.42%，升至第四大重仓。除了电动车业务，FSD自动驾驶和Optimus机器人也提供了长期增长空间。段永平一直认可马斯克的商业能力，这次继续加仓，说明他愿意为特斯拉未来的业务扩张下注。

10. SpaceX $SPCX
新建仓，持仓市值约3,016万，是本季度唯一新买入的标的。SpaceX拥有火箭发射和星链卫星互联网两大核心业务，可重复使用火箭带来的成本优势很难复制。这是一项稀缺的硬科技资产，也说明段永平开始关注新的太空经济机会。

11. 西方石油 $OXY
持仓不变。能源业务提供稳定现金流，兼具周期对冲属性，是组合里的传统能源配置。

12. 微软 $MSFT
持仓不变。云计算、企业软件和AI形成完整业务体系，依然是科技板块的重要压舱石。

13. 迪士尼 $DIS
持仓不变。影视内容IP、主题公园和流媒体构成多元业务，核心竞争力来自长期积累的品牌和内容资产。

14. 联合健康 $UNH
持仓不变。美国大型健康保险公司之一，医疗保障需求相对刚性，业务具有一定防御属性。

text:
I send around PDFs and markdown files to my coworkers so much and they use their agents to make sense of the world too, so I started using this skill methodology-appendix to make sure their agents could replicate what my agents found. 

---
name: methodology-appendix
description: "Every data-backed report or memo ends with a Methodology / Replication Appendix: the signal choice and its sensitivity, verbatim queries, derivation pseudocode over named constants, the rebuild command, and drift/limits. Appended by default, without asking."
---

# Methodology / Replication Appendix

## Rule

Any report, PDF or page whose conclusions rest on data queries ends with a
**Replication Appendix**. It is a working recipe, not a citation list. The test:

> A reader with an agent and equivalent data access can regenerate the document
> end to end from the appendix alone, without contacting the author.

If a reader would have to ask "which column did you use?", "what date was this
pulled?" or "how do I rebuild the PDF?", the appendix failed.

## Body voice

The body states conclusions plainly. No process narration ("I was asked...",
"on the first pass..."), no self-grading. The first sentence after the title
contains a finding. Everything about how you got there goes in the appendix at
the end, written for forensic recreation.

## When this fires

Always, automatically, for:
- analysis memos backed by database or API queries
- any PDF sent to partners, executives or external stakeholders
- pages presenting quantitative findings
- anything with tables of counts, rates or percentiles

Skip for narrative or qualitative writing, meeting notes, personal memos,
short ephemera, and documents with no data spine. Do not ask permission.

## The six sections

### 1. Header

```markdown
## Replication Appendix

A reader with an agent and equivalent data access can regenerate every number
and rebuild this document from this appendix alone.

**Access required:** <tool/CLI + auth, internal APIs>
**Snapshot date:** <ISO date>. Live-data documents won't reproduce exactly after this date; see Drift.
```

### 2. Signal definitions and the choice that mattered

The most important section. Analyses usually turn on one column or threshold
choice. Name it, name the alternatives, state the impact.

```markdown
### Signal definitions

| Field | What it is | Why chosen / rejected |
|---|---|---|
| `score_a` | Ensembled score | **Primary.** More predictive per <source>. |
| `score_b` | Single-model score | Rejected as primary; kept for contrast. |
| final_decision | Human decision object | Not queried. Known gap. |

**Outcome sensitivity:** switching from score_b to score_a moved the headline
count from N1 to N2 and changed claim X. A replication that changes the signal
column will not match these numbers.
```

Always include an **Outcome sensitivity** line. If a different defensible choice
changes the conclusion, the reader must know before quoting it.

### 3. Verbatim queries

Every query that produced a number, copy-pasteable, in document order, labelled
by the finding it supports. Never paraphrase SQL. Never write "similar to the
above." Add schema notes a replicator would otherwise get wrong: enum meanings,
non-obvious joins, columns that seem to exist but don't.

### 4. Derivation pseudocode

Queries give raw counts; the document has derived figures. Show the arithmetic,
with assumptions as named constants a reader can swap.

```
ITEMS_PER_DAY   = 8        # observed median, <period>
YIELD_HAIRCUT   = 0.10..0.15   # marginal cases convert below observed rate

gap          = count(status = REJECTED and score >= threshold)
extra_days   = gap / ITEMS_PER_DAY
added_wins   = gap * YIELD_HAIRCUT
```

Different constants change the recommendation, not just the number, so they
must be visible.

### 5. Rebuild command

Exact commands from source markdown to verified PDF, plus a visual check
(e.g. `pdfinfo` page count, `pdftoppm` a couple of pages and look at them).
Name the source of record: the PDF is a render, never the original.

### 6. Drift, limits and known gaps

- **Live data moves.** What was mid-flight at snapshot; what is closed and stable.
- **Coverage gaps.** Fields only populated for part of the range, and how tables were restricted rather than shown with misleading denominators.
- **What this cannot see.** Inputs to the real decision that the data lacks.
- **Retractions.** Any claim withdrawn between versions, and why.

## Procedure

1. Log queries verbatim as you run them. Reconstructed SQL is how appendices go wrong.
2. Write the analysis.
3. Append the six sections before rendering.
4. Name the signal choice and its outcome sensitivity.
5. Render, check visually, then send.
6. On revision, update the appendix in the same commit as the finding. An appendix describing a superseded method is worse than none.

## Quality bar

- [ ] Could a reader re-run this without asking me anything?
- [ ] Is every headline number traceable to a pasted query?
- [ ] Is the signal/threshold choice named, with alternatives and impact?
- [ ] Are derived figures arithmetic over named constants?
- [ ] Is the rebuild command present and correct?
- [ ] Are drift, coverage gaps and retractions stated?

## Anti-patterns

- **Citation theater:** table names instead of runnable queries.
- **Reconstructed SQL:** retyped from memory, drifted from what ran.
- **Silent signal choice:** one column presented as "the score" when a defensible alternative changes the answer.
- **Buried assumptions:** constants hard-coded in prose.
- **Stale appendix:** findings revised, appendix untouched.
- **Asking first:** this is a default, not an offer.

text:
onekey is not affected by the optimizely supply chain compromise. our client code, web app, and website do not use optimizely.

if you visited any of the 178 affected organizations (188 snippets, including ledger, gitlab, zoom, salesforce, bbc, and hsbc...) over the last 24 hours, here is the technical breakdown and what you need to check.

attackers compromised optimizely web experimentation and injected a loader into Project JavaScript, served via optimizely's main cdn (/js/<projectid>.js). it pulled second-stage payloads from external c2 servers (track.js) and iterated through 26 versions over 13 hours. standard csp setups with strict-dynamic or whitelisted cdn domains failed to block it because the trusted first-party snippet executed the fetch itself.

once in the browser context, the payload does four things:

1）runtime and network hooking: overrides https://t.co/tp64Ky7WRl, Function.prototype.apply, window.fetch, XMLHttpRequest, and navigator.clipboard. instead of a basic clipboard regex swap, it intercepts network responses and mutates the dom in memory. it replaces btc, evm, sol, tron, ton, ltc, bch, and doge addresses with checksum-valid attacker addresses before they even render on your screen.

2）form skimming: hooks form submissions and POST bodies, running luhn validation to exfiltrate card pan, expiry, and cvv from native checkouts. cross-origin payment iframes like stripe and adyen remain isolated via sop.

3）session capture: dumps document.cookie (exposing any session tokens missing the HttpOnly flag) alongside html/canvas dom snapshots.

4）ios exploit delivery: injects hidden iframes serving browser exploit chains targeting webcontent sandbox escape and kernel r/w. it routes ios 13 to 17 to coruna and ios 18.0 to 18.6 to darksword (ios 26.x currently only triggers the /C10/ fingerprinting module). a telltale sign on ios 18.6 and below is the tab reloading every 60 seconds as the exploit retries.

remediation steps if you browsed any affected sites:

1）treat your host screen as untrusted. when js primitives and network calls are hooked in the browser runtime, the address rendered on your monitor is already spoofed. verify the full recipient address on your hardware wallet's independent screen before signing.

2）clear your browser disk cache immediately. optimizely cdn assets are cached locally, meaning the poisoned <projectid>.js file can still execute on repeat visits even after upstream cleanup.

3）explicitly log out and log back into affected platforms to rotate server-side session tokens, in case your cookies lacked HttpOnly and got exfiltrated.

4）update iphones to ios 18.7.3 or 26.3+ to patch the underlying webkit and kernel vulnerabilities.
