quoted_text:
It's been 1 year since I posted this and man...what a year

Turns out I was right and this marked the Avast bottom.

I've been full time crypto for the past 5 years, been through a lot, roundtripped 7 figs multiple times, went to IRL events, been through a couple black swans, met a lot of cool people, etc...

Yet 1 year ago today, I was down bad on all fronts (money, health, mental). 

But the only way out is through, so I locked in. 

Thanks to @cryptokillua99 I was able to meet a lot of like minded people who are now my brothers for life.

Killua added me to @TroupeKZ and my life changed ever since.

I didn't have a lot of money but I was (and still am) extremely hungry, by being in TroupeKZ I was surrounded by people who were much better traders than me, people with net worth significantly higher than me.

But everyone has to bring something to the table, since I'm not that good of a trader, I made up for it by being terminally online, contributing to every plays people wanted to run by bagworking, making content, paying dex, etc...

Being online constantly made it easier for me to build lifelong relationships with people in that group, at first I felt like I had to prove myself, I felt unworthy of being surrounded by those people, I mean I felt like I didn't deserve to be here.

But what people are saying is true, once you spend a lot of time in the market, you start to understand it better (not on some spiritual shit but you start noticing some patterns, you start being more familiar with which wallets to avoid, their behavior, etc..., the narratives that run or flop, etc)

I was able to get back on my feet and successfully turned $83 into multi 7 figs on cashcat (1M realized + 1.4% still unrealized), then I hit Marscoin ($10k buy at an avg of 400k MC, still holding 2.2%)

Hit a couple of other nice plays and I'm doing much better financially.

I also met someone, a really nice and lovely girl who I feel honored to be calling my girlfriend.

I was also able to build a following on here, and other social trading platforms. Currently at 23k followers on X (3k last year), 370k on fomo and about 8k on pump (but I made my acc public yesterday). 

Goal has always been to win in this space without compromising myself, by keeping it real and fair. 

I always preached about holding and believing over scalping micro caps and I believe my account reflects this and I'm proud to say I'm winning by being myself. I'm a big advocate of leading by example, if you want something to change, you gotta start doing it yourself, regardless of how influential you are.

For example I believe we should start supporting devs who stick around to build cool brands, and I believe this will happen once more devs/founders show that hardwork pays off and can be extremely rewarding. That's why for the past 2 years i've been working on the same project nobody cares about on CT except a tiny but super strong community...but I don't care because I know that ultimately this brand will be everywhere and holders will be rewarded for their patience. (check pinned tweet if you're wondering wtf I'm talking about)

Real shit, I'm so proud of where I'm at today, of the following I've been able to grow, of the relationships I've nurtured, of how I've improved trading wise (still a lot to learn!)

Idk why I'm even saying all that, I guess I'm hoping that by sharing my story, this will give people who need it some hope.

I know in this space it feels like everything is rigged and all odds are against you (which is true, it's just one big arena), hell some of you might want to become influential accounts (I know I wanted to!) but feel like it's impossible...

...but everything is possible, genuinely. Just stick to what you believe in, be yourself, don't sell your soul for money. It'll take longer but once you succeed you'll be super grateful that you made it while staying true to yourself.

Anyway, I'm a nobody and this story is far from over but I wanted to reflect on all the things that happened this year. Find your people and work hard, that's the key.

Plenty more wins on the way

It gets better, I swear.

Don't be scared of dreaming, you can just do things.

Take responsibility for everything, stop blaming others, take action and you'll be alright. 

And remember, you have what it takes. People aren't better than you, they just started earlier.

text:
$NVDA  Spectrum-X的CPO量产计划出现延迟，预计要到2027年底至2028年才能实现规模出货，主要受键合良率较低以及测试供应商选择尚未确定等因素影响。

这一延后对当前光学产业链带来两个主要影响：

1. 可插拔光学器件（Pluggables）获得更长的盈利窗口。Hyperscalers无法暂停AI集群建设等待CPO成熟，800G/1.6T成熟供应商如Innolight和Eoptolink等将有更充裕的时间实现变现。

2. 近距离封装光学（NPO）也获得更长的市场验证期，在下一代架构中成为更现实的选择。

从供应链角度看，同时覆盖NPO和CPO路径的供应商更具优势。 $LITE的外置激光器和 $COHR 的PhotonLink平台均能适配两种技术，因此在CPO推进节奏变化中处于相对有利位置。这一需求扩张也为上游InP衬底供应商$AXTI以及CW激光器厂商$SIVE提供了长期支撑。

CPO爬坡节奏的放缓，究竟会给现有光学供应商带来多长的缓冲期，以及各环节最终受益程度，仍取决于后续技术成熟速度和实际部署进展。

text:
Great ads are rare. Aer Lingus just made one.

The mechanics behind it are incredibly efficient:
- Identifies a clear and regularly discussed online brand issue and openly shares it with the consumer in the first seconds.
- Makes the consumer intrigued by the solution to a problem they never thought they'd have to solve.
- Understands that the behind-the-scenes (even if acted) is a more compelling story than the scene itself.
- Makes you feel like you're sitting at that table from the first to the last second, listening to something you normally shouldn't have access to.
- Has multiple jokes, with multiple layers, all carried by different profiles which is why you will watch this more than once. (guaranteed)
- Uses a celebrity profile that adds to the idea rather than becoming the idea (and Sharon Horgan is always phenomenal).
- Makes you want to say Aer Lingus from the minute you see the ad for no reason.
- Lands the story with the right level of self-deprecation but stays true to the brand's DNA by keeping the same name.
- Subtly puts Aer Lingus top of mind for your next flight to Ireland.
- Turns the initial flaw and problem to solve into a new reason to love, understand and remember the name. 

It feels like an homage to old-school advertising with stellar copywriting and exceptional casting/acting. 

I would show this 90-second gem to any advertising and marketing student or professional in the world.

Bravo Aer Lingus. The Irish Airline. https://t.co/Z5Gn0FlKdQ

text:
昨天推文发出后，一些同学质疑：“疑似心梗吃阿司匹林到底对不对？万一是夹层呢？”。首先，现在 AI 的发达确实让大家了解了更多医学知识，这是好事。但问题在于，在急救实务中，我们考虑的并不是如何排除所有极端情况，而是在信息不充分、时间极其有限的情况下，如何基于疾病发生的概率、干预的收益与风险，作出对患者整体而言最有利的选择。这里有一个非常重要的前提：我讨论的是非专业人士的院外急救，而不是医生在医院里的诊断和治疗。

对于普通人来说，突发胸痛时，没有心电图，没有肌钙蛋白检测，没有超声设备，不具备鉴别急性心肌梗死、主动脉夹层和其他疾病的专业能力。（对，你在抖音看到的双侧血压差不是夹层诊断的金标准，作为外行你也大概率测量不到），此时指南必须给到普通人基于概率的最优解。

面向普通人的院外急救指南的设计逻辑，不是要求普通人先把病因诊断清楚，再采取行动，因为普通人没有这个能力，院外急救指南要做的是：在普通人无法准确判断病因的现实条件下，哪些措施足够简单、容易执行，并且从整体风险收益来看值得推荐。

从数据来看，对于急性心梗的患者，早期使用阿司匹林有明确的生存获益，单次使用阿司匹林造成严重并发症的总体风险被认为较低。当然，在院前，明确诊断后（现在大城市的急救车上都已经开始配备便携的超声设备了），我们还会给患者服用更强效的抗板剂，甚至使用肝素。有一项研究，统计了美国 141 家急诊科约 95 万例非创伤性胸痛患者。其中，急性冠脉综合征占 4.5%，胸主动脉夹层占 0.09%。也就是说，在这组胸痛患者中，前者的发生比例大约是后者的 50 倍。所以，院外指南应该怎么写呢？

有了AI之后，很多外行会产生一个视野局限：知道了一个罕见但严重的疾病，知道了某种药物可能存在禁忌，就认为自己发现了专业指南的重大漏洞。但问题在于，专业指南的撰写者不可能不知道这些例外，而是必须在不确定性中权衡不同选择的后果，给出面向普通人的建议。这是院外急救培训中最重要的一点，每次培训都要反复跟学员声明：你存在的价值就是确保急救车到来之前人还活着，你甚至不要考虑按压深度是不是太深会按断肋骨。

医学不是寻找一个足以否定所有行动的极端反例，而是在充满不确定性的现实中，尽可能作出有证据支持、风险收益合理的决定。

当然了，一定还有人会跟我扛国内的法律问题和被追责问题，作为急救导师，我能提供的数据和案例肯定比大多数人多。我可以讲的是，民法典184条施行后，因为施救被追责的案例基本是零了，个别媒体报导的个案，我只能讲，背后都是有其他情况的。当然这里还有个全社会对施救行为的价值判断问题，会不会导致上海松江站前些天那个“阻止旁观者施救”的情况，这个路还很长、很复杂。但是全社会的“旁观者施救”屏障一旦被建立，会有更多人在四分钟之内获得生存机会（否则就直接凉了），这是一个不可估量的收益。

The chaos in El Salvador before Bukele was never an accident, and the chaos in Haiti today is not an accident either.

The media told you that the gangs were just poor boys who went bad on their own, but that story falls apart the moment you ask one simple question.

Where does a poor sixteen year old boy living in a slum with no job and no money get an AK-47 and an AR-15 and a Glock and thousands of rounds of ammunition, and where does he get a brand new Toyota Hilux and motorcycles and speedboats and drones and encrypted phones and bulletproof vests and night vision goggles, and who pays his monthly salary and pays for his safe house and pays his lawyer when he is arrested and pays the police and the judge and the prison guard to look the other way, and who pays his family when he dies?

A poor boy cannot afford even one bullet, so someone else is paying for all of it.

That someone is the multimillionaires and the billionaires and the wealthy entities who profit from chaos, because chaos is a business and a broken country is the most profitable business in the world.

When a country is in chaos its land becomes cheap so they can buy it, its gold and its drugs and its resources can be stolen without anyone asking questions, its government becomes weak so they can control it, and its people become so scared that they obey anyone who promises them a little safety.

In El Salvador the gangs were not fighting the system, the gangs were the system, paid to keep the poor terrorized so the poor would never rise up and demand a better country.

In Haiti it is the same story, the gangs are not independent, they are funded and armed and protected by rich families and foreign businessmen and foreign NGOs who want Haiti to stay weak so they can keep stealing its ports and its gold and its labour.

And when a man like Bukele comes and says I will lock up all the gangs and end this in two years, who attacks him? It is the same people.

The same billionaires who fund the gangs fund the media that calls Bukele a dictator, the same wealthy entities who arm the gangs fund the NGOs that cry human rights for murderers, the same people who profit from chaos fund the political voices that hate real help in Haiti and sabotage anyone who is actually capable of doing it.

Look at the pattern and it becomes clear, when a gang kills a hundred innocent people there is silence, but when a leader kills a hundred gang members there is outrage.

When a gang rapes children there is no campaign, but when Bukele locks up rapists there is a global campaign against him.

That is because the media is not independent, it is owned by billionaires, the NGOs are not independent, they are funded by billionaires, and the politicians are not independent, they are bought by billionaires.

They do not want Haiti saved and they did not want El Salvador saved, they want them broken, because a broken country is cheap to buy and easy to control.

Bukele exposed them, he proved that gangs can be destroyed in months if you have the will, and that terrified them, because if El Salvador can be fixed then Haiti can be fixed, and if Haiti can be fixed then Africa can be fixed, and if Africa can be fixed then the billionaires lose their business.

That is why they demonize Bukele, that is why they sabotage Haiti, that is why they hate any man who actually helps the poor.

Every onchain cycle since 2013, we've had an onchain boom/bust. The boom typically shows what pmf would look like for onchain experiments if it were sustainable and with the bust it kills 95% of the experiments but leave just enough to build unicorns.

text:
包括汇丰、Zoom、GitLab、CNN、彭博等全球178家机构和品牌的官网通过信任第三方服务被投毒。根据Report URI的报告，攻击者利用网站实验与个性化平台Optimizely，向这些机构的网站访客投放恶意JavaScript。也就是说，用户访问看似正常、拥有Https证书的正规网站，也可能执行攻击者注入的恶意代码。

很多大型企业使用Optimizely Web进行A/B测试、网页实验和用户体验优化。这些网站会在页面中加载Optimizely CDN提供的JavaScript文件，包括机构客户自行添加的ProjectJS。

攻击者通过向ProjectJS注入恶意代码，再由Optimizely CDN正常分发，最终使得访客的浏览器自动加载恶意软件，面临银行卡信息、Cookie以及iOS漏洞等风险。

Report URI表示，至于攻击者究竟是入侵了Optimizely系统、盗取了拥有跨客户访问权限的凭证，还是利用了其他漏洞，目前尚未得到确认。

今年 4 月 Anthropic 高调发布 Project Glasswing 时，整个网安圈都在担心 AI 自动化挖洞是不是要把全世界的开源软件底裤掀翻了。七个月过去，漏洞情报机构 VulnCheck 刚刚交出了一份极其扎实的第三方审计总账：《After 7-months, Glasswing Overwhelms Maintainers with Underwhelming Findings》。

把水分挤干后的数据对比相当扎心：
在过去七个月里，Anthropic 账面上累计宣称发现了 37,966 个安全问题，但真正公开披露出来的只有 7,349 个（19.4%），其中最终被确认修复的更是只有区区 217 个；归属于 Anthropic 的正式 CVE 一共 442 个（仅占今年全球新增 CVE 的 0.5%），真正在野被利用的高危漏洞只有 2 个。

更让开源社区苦不堪言的是“发现量”与“修复量”的剪刀差：从 9 月到现在，Glasswing 账面上又猛增了近 12,000 条新发现，但同期新增的修复记录只有 15 个；与此同时，被标记为重复上报（Duplicates）的高达 1,654 个（是已修复数量的近 8 倍），另有 419 个 被直接撤回。

以安全标准极严的 cURL 项目为例，在 Anthropic 扫描器提交并公开的 34 份漏洞报告里，cURL 维护者直接驳回了 19 份（判定根本不算漏洞），6 份定为低危，9 份还在排队。AI 把生成漏洞报告的边际成本打到了零，却把甄别误报的沉重人工成本全量甩给了本就用爱发电的开源维护者。

text:
Wintermute is literally paying $10M a year to legally front-run everyone on Hyperliquid and it’s completely destroying altcoin liquidity

Bloomberg finally exposed what HFT desks have been screaming about for weeks. Hyperliquid’s gossip priority auctions let top funds see incoming orders 50–60ms before anyone else on the network

Look at how completely broken this setup is:

-> One Wintermute wallet won ~76% of the top slots last month, burning ~$26k every single day just to starve out competition
-> HL claims the auction is open to everyone. Complete BS. You only get that 60ms head start if you have direct peering with Foundation nodes, which requires 0.5% of total maker volume and 10k HYPE staked ($700k+)
-> Smaller MMs are getting sniped nonstop and just unplugging their bots on alts
-> Retail gets stuck with the bill: across 86 altcoin pairs, order book depth on HL imploded by 82% while spreads blew out from 2.13 to 3.55 bps

Honestly, I don't even blame Wintermute. If I had their balance sheet, I would milk this exact loophole until someone forced me to stop

The blame sits 100% on the protocol design. Burning auction fees is cool for $HYPE holders, sure, but letting one fund buy a monopoly on data speed turns a decentralized exchange into a rigged casino

Scrap read-priority auctions completely or make the slots equal, because right now altcoin execution on HL is absolute garbage

quoted_text:
I ran a PageRank-driven analysis on all recent news coverage related to Jensen, and traced how the New York Times shaped the entirety of this narrative: https://t.co/qKGMJ2LBV8

--
NVIDIA has lost over $1 trillion in market value since the first New York Times story broke about Jensen. I dug deeper to analyze how the news originated and spread, running a swarm of agents which analyzed almost 2000 stories, across 40 US and European news outlets, and applying PageRank to understand how they cited each other. 

Core findings: 
- Primary news driver: NYT, with 88 stories, most-cited
- Volume drivers: WSJ - 99 stories; Bloomberg - 140 stories; NY Post - 68 stories

All of this started from unknown sources who gave information to the NYT, which then ran the spy story (still unproven), and it was then picked up in other news publications. Curiously, even after that story, there was a 9 day period of extremely low volume reporting (28 stories only), after which there was a sudden spike after Jensen's own letter to NVIDIA staff. NYT then had multiple sequential spy and affair stories, which fed a wave of further news coverage. It was the originating hub of negative Jensen coverage. Multiple outlets since then had an explosion in stories about him starting earlier this week as well. 

Overall, as you see this data, you will observe this was an exceptional media onslaught against Jensen with sharply negative coverage about him, his work, style, and family. Infact, it was brutal, and unlike coverage in the past of CEOs who have had affairs (such as Intel CEO in 2018). For eg, NYT ran just 2 stories about Intel's CEO who had an affair with his employee, compared to 88 on Jensen! Why ? 

This analysis used a technique of how Google originally ranked webpages, using PageRank, and does deep dive link analysis so you can view how the news spread. What struck here was that it did not matter if there were proven facts or credible sources: the outcome here was pre-decided. The news was making the reality which it wanted. 

During this period, NVIDIA has lost $1.27 trillion in market value since the first story broke. On Nov 12th-13th, further news broke that both the US Justice Department, and Singapore - are unable to even conclude the spy allegation. 

This has been a catastrophic attack on one of the hardest working founders in modern times, who took an idea from a Denny's booth, through multiple instances of almost going out of business, to building the foundation of the entire modern world with how the NVIDIA story played out. Thanks to Jensen, we have hope that many formerly incurable diseases will get solved by AI, that quality of life will and have improved for billions around the world. 

Now I do not know if he will come back as CEO or not, but I hope he does. What happened to him here, and to the wider industry, was not fair.

text:
So here's an unpopular opinion. This stuff is a facet of what drives Congressional corruption, but not in the way most people think.

We are the richest, most powerful country in the world and we expect our 535 Legislators to fly Economy class when they're on official business out of some warped sense of imposed humility.

When you treat people with immense power like they're not immensely powerful you breed corruption. Police Departments (under the William Parker model) figured this out a long time ago. They started paying police officers like middle class professionals and told them things like "if I catch you taking free coffee, you're getting written up".

The observation Parker made was that cops are powerful people in their communities, but police departments paid them like shit. If you paid them something more commiserate with their power and authority, they would be less likely you utilize that power and authority to make up the gap. 

It was commonly understood by everyone that cops would use their power to secure little favors by performing small, innocuous acts of corruption. You'd make sure to go by the diner that always gave you free coffee after hours to tug on the back door and make sure none of the usual suspects were loitering around. You'd give a warning instead of a ticket to the hotdog cart guy who gave guys on the job a free hotdog . You'd take a drunk teenager home instead of the drunk tank because his dad ran a grocer and always made sure to hold something in short supply aside for your wife.

These tiny acts of corruption, little favors, weren't a big deal on the individual level and helped build community relations. In the aggregate, though, it gave a certain class of the community privileged access to law enforcement and built up a general tolerance to corruption in everyone who participated in it. 

By paying his cops well and demanding they not take favors from the community or use their authority to secure preferential treatment, Parker drastically reduced instances of serious corruption in the LAPD. I know a lot of you will object to this and say "but cops are still corrupt" and yes, some of them are. But it used to be so, so much worse than most people realize. We've become accustomed to police as professional civil servants and blanche at behavior that used to be commonly accepted as the "cost of doing business".

We need to stop pretending the members of Congress aren't powerful people and start treating them like they are. You start tackling corruption by acknowledging and compensating power, not pretending it doesn't exist.

text:
Bitcoin’s latest decline has unfolded less like a sudden crash and more like a grinding erosion of confidence. Over the past month the price has fallen more than 20 percent, at one point sliding toward $62,000—its weakest level since July—before stabilizing only modestly higher. 

Unlike the sharp liquidations that defined earlier crypto downturns, much of this move developed during relatively quiet trading sessions before selling accelerated. The result is a market in which even long-term holders appear exhausted rather than panicked.

Several pressures have converged. A large exchange hack earlier in the autumn damaged sentiment and triggered outflows from spot Bitcoin ETFs that have now totaled nearly $3 billion in a short window. At the same time, rising U.S. Treasury yields and a firmer dollar have reduced the appeal of risk assets more broadly. 

Political uncertainty following the midterm elections and competition for speculative capital from artificial-intelligence ventures have further thinned the pool of buyers. Stablecoin balances have contracted, removing one of the traditional cushions that once allowed traders to stay within the crypto ecosystem during downturns. Crypto-linked equities have tracked the weakness, amplifying the sense that institutional interest has cooled.

Looking ahead, the near-term path remains constrained. Any rebound is likely to stay fragile while bond yields remain elevated and ETF flows stay negative; volatility should therefore stay high. Over a longer horizon the picture is less uniformly bleak. 

Crypto has repeatedly recovered from periods of fatigue once macro conditions stabilize or a clear new source of demand appears—whether through improved regulatory clarity, renewed corporate or institutional accumulation, or simply the exhaustion of sellers. 

The current weariness may itself become the setup for the next leg higher, but only after the present combination of higher yields, softer inflows, and competing investment themes begins to ease. Until then, the market’s most committed participants continue to face a test of patience rather than a sudden collapse.

Unification over fragmentation.

Composition over accumulation.

text:
除了争辩用报价还是成交价，这批信里的另一个分歧是：谁算运动员？

指数决定期货怎么结算，所以没人反对"不能又当裁判又当运动员"。编指数的公司自己不下场，它的股东下场算不算？关联公司呢？给它供数据的人呢？分歧就在这条线画在哪，目前大致三种画法：

最宽的是 Ornn：有关联可以，披露并管理就行。它旗下有帮客户转租算力的关联公司，头号数据源据报是一家经纪商

中间的是 Silicon Data 和 DRW：编指数的公司自己不能交易、不能持有算力，但只看这家公司本身。Silicon Data 确实不碰，可它的股东是 DRW、Jump 和 CME，CEO 还兼着现货市场 Compute Exchange 的 CEO。DRW 在信里一边支持指数商独立，一边披露这两家公司都是自己孵化的，而且自己打算下场做市

最严的是 Compute Desk 和 Architect：要连关联方一起看。Compute Desk 要求对背后有做市商或算力持有方的指数加严审查，Architect 要求指数商不能把自己促成的交易算进指数。这两家一个供指数、一个开交易所，于是在授权协议里写明，Architect 促成的交易从指数里剔除

当然还是一样的逻辑，每家倡导的都刚好是自己可以站在安全一侧的画法

text:
There is a reason New York City has not experienced the kind of violent riots we have witnessed in Paris and other major cities around the world.

We had the NYPD’s Strategic Response Group (SRG), a specialized unit of highly trained officers prepared to confront violence before it spiraled out of control.

Let me make something absolutely clear.

Peaceful protest is a constitutional right. Violent rioting is a crime. And confusing the two is a dangerous failure of leadership.

The SRG was not created to silence peaceful protesters. It was created to protect New Yorkers when demonstrations crossed the line into violence, to protect businesses from destruction, peaceful demonstrators from violent agitators, and police officers from being assaulted.

Now City Hall is dismantling that specialized unit, introducing unarmed civilian de-escalation teams, and restricting the tools available to police.

I support de-escalation. Every responsible police officer does. But de-escalation is a strategy, not a substitute for the ability to confront violence.

You cannot reason with a brick flying through a storefront. You cannot negotiate with a Molotov cocktail. And you cannot send a social worker to do the job of a specially trained police officer confronting a violent mob.

The NYPD will still have officers responding to protests. But the question City Hall  has failed to answer is why New Yorkers will be safer without a dedicated unit specifically trained for these dangerous situations.

What happens when peaceful protesters are attacked? When businesses are being destroyed? When police officers are surrounded and assaulted?

Who responds? How quickly? With what training? And with what tools?

These are not hypothetical questions. These are the decisions that determine whether a dangerous situation is contained or an entire neighborhood descends into chaos.

I spent four years as mayor and 22 years as an NYPD officer. I know the difference between protecting someone’s right to protest and allowing someone to use that protest as cover for violence.

The right to protest does not include the right to terrorize. And protecting civil liberties should never require surrendering public safety.

City Hall may believe dismantling the SRG is a political victory.

But if violence erupts, the people paying the price won’t be the activists applauding this announcement or the politicians celebrating it at City Hall.

It will be the police officer who gets assaulted. The small-business owner whose livelihood is destroyed. The peaceful protester who gets caught in the violence. The innocent New Yorker who simply wants to get home safely.

New York City’s Public Safety is not a laboratory for ideological experiments. Our police officers are not expendable. And public safety is not something you gamble with to score political points.

City Hall should reverse this decision before New Yorkers discover the consequences the hard way.

text:
英伟达财报：赚了多少之外，谁在买单？
黄仁勋离任后，我更关注的，不只是英伟达还能卖多少卡，而是：支撑这些订单的钱，还能不能持续到位。
AI 有真实需求，不代表所有扩张都能赚钱；合同是真的，也不代表客户不需要靠下一轮融资来付款。黄仁勋也是AI融资的教父。

几个例子：
① 英伟达与 CoreWeave：既卖卡，也投资，还承接剩余算力。
CoreWeave 披露，英伟达以 20 亿美元认购股份；另一项初始价值 63 亿美元的安排，则要求英伟达在满足约定条件时购买剩余未售算力。
这不是说 63 亿都会亏掉，而是说：如果独立客户消化不了产能，一部分风险会回到供应商身上。
② 亚马逊与 Anthropic：我投资你，你采购我的算力。
亚马逊是 Anthropic 的投资方，也是算力供应商。Anthropic 公布，未来十年对 AWS 技术的支出承诺超过 1000 亿美元。
合作能帮助双方扩张，但长期采购承诺，不等于今天已经到账的现金，更不等于终端用户已经贡献了足够利润。
来源：双方合作公告。
③ 微软与 OpenAI：股权与云订单，押在同一家公司身上。
微软披露，对 OpenAI 总出资承诺 130 亿美元；后续协议中，OpenAI 又承诺增量采购 2500 亿美元 Azure 服务。
发展顺利，微软可以同时获得股权回报和云收入；商业化不及预期，两边也可能同时承压。2500 亿是采购承诺，不是当年收入，更不是已经全部收回的现金。
④ IREN、微软与 Dell：有大订单，不代表不缺钱。
IREN 披露，与微软签订约 97 亿美元算力服务合同，每批次有 20% 预付款；同时向 Dell 采购约 58 亿美元设备。
设备和机房要先投入，服务收入分期到账。文件明确，合同现金流只能覆盖部分资本开支，其余仍需自有资金、经营现金流和额外融资。
所以，融资变贵、交付延期、验收推迟，都可能让中间的算力运营商先承压。

真正的风险，不是“订单都是假的”
这些交易结构不同，不能混成一笔账，更不能凭交叉投资就认定造假。
它们共同揭示的是：供应商、投资者和客户的身份越来越重叠，风险也越来越相关。
只要终端客户持续付费，融资就能帮助产业扩张；但如果终端收入追不上投入，增长就更依赖新融资。融资一慢，订单未必立即消失，扩建、回款和估值却可能先受影响。
黄仁勋离任不会让合同自动失效。市场需要重新评估的是：未来谁继续投资，谁继续承接产能，谁承担扩张的风险。
为什么我不把财报超预期当买点？

在我看来，当前小四万亿市值下，继续押注的赔率不够吸引人，第一个十万亿的公司在人类文明可能还要有些时间。

I think even if $NVDA beat on growth & margins, raised 4Q guide, and even reaffirms FY guide + do a bigger buyback it won't be enough:
- It's always beat and raised, what's new?
- Buyback sends the wrong message. Would argue it's bad capital allocation until they have visibility post-Jensen.
- Who's gonna believe in their reaffirmed out-year guide? It just kicks the can of a kitchen-sink down the road.

I think the market would look for clarity on the following in comments & Q&A:
- Succession & clear path to fill Jensen’s shoes
- Future of vendor-financing and ecosystem investments, or at least quantified impact
- US probe and potential lawsuit re: China biz, as well as coming out on sales / margin impact
- Supplier relationship & corresponding roadmap / margin visibility

Maybe if $NVDA bleeds heavily into the print we get a pop regardless. Personally I think the pop will be faded if we get anything short of the above.

金融机构收到执法冻结，都是整个账号的冻结，币安也没有权利自己冻结或者解开。
被冻结的账号并不等于被划转，每一个案子都需要对方有法院判决才会划转，判决就需要完整证据，案情清晰；如果是无辜牵连的用户，执法部门没有证据，法院也不会判，在案情梳理过程中，中间沟通协调币安都需要投入大量人力去为用户沟通来保障利益，无辜牵连的也会解开。比如发帖的朋友。

text:
一姐回应币安冻结：整账户冻结是司法要求，别再花钱找“大哥”了

针对最近大量用户吐槽币安账户被冻结、客服只回“等”或“自己找律师”的问题，何一连发两条直接回应：

1、金融机构接到执法冻结令，都是整账户冻结，币安没有权利自己冻或自己解。
2、冻结 ≠ 划转。没有法院判决、证据不完整，不会划走资金。无辜用户在案情梳理过程中，币安会投入人力沟通，最终能解的会解。
3、别再花钱找第三方“维权”“找关系”。能解开的不花钱也能解，解不开的花钱也没用。前两天就有用户被清退通知两次没看，结果白付了账户里50%的钱。
4、想加速的，自己找对应国家的正规律师协助沟通，别指望发帖闹事的KOL和“大哥”。

不过用户侧的痛点也很现实——等大半年、信息几乎为零、普通用户根本不知道哪笔钱有问题、也无力请海外律师。

而且这波交易所账户冻结来势汹汹，其他所也均有用户反馈⬇️

·Gate 最近刚回应一个用户，15 枚 BTC 因印度警方案件被冻，从 2025 年 7 月冻到现在，Gate 表示没直接移交资产，仍在逐案审核。

·抹茶（MEXC） 本月被美国 FinCEN 点名涉及至少 160 亿美元可疑交易后，币安、OKX、Gate 等对来自抹茶的入金加强审查，部分用户资金被暂扣或账户受限。

·Bybit、Bitget 也持续有用户反馈账户被风控冻结，客服响应慢、信息少。

So what’s the big deal with the CFTC’s Backpack announcement?

While Kalshi received the BTCPERP go-ahead in May of this year, it was a single-product license.

Backpack’s license permits the use of blockchain-based architecture for the execution and settlement of derivatives contracts, enabling the exchange to offer a wide range of perps to US users.

In addition to the Derivatives Clearing Organization (DCO) qualification already obtained, Backpack is the first US blockchain derivatives platform to hold a full set of trading and clearing licenses.

This precedent will surely prompt other exchanges to seek licenses to serve US users directly, sparking a wave of exchanges dropping the “not available to US persons” disclaimer.

text:
The Lost Gardens of Lobsteropolis: what was actually inside. 🦞

@PhilipColbert's first solo UK museum show ran at The Lightbox, Woking, 25 July – 1 November 2026

26 paintings and sculptures filled the gallery and the gardens, the largest show of Colbert's work the Lightbox had ever staged

It began outside. A giant inflatable lobster in the fried-egg suit stood at the entrance, under a huge PHILIP COLBERT banner. The egg suit is Colbert's signature — the same one Lobstar #877 wears, so the exhibition introduced itself in the artist's own visual language.

Inside, the centrepiece was the painting. Five metres high, the largest Colbert has ever made, six months in the painting: The Lost Gardens of Lobsteropolis. A fantastical garden crowded with hundreds of lobsters playing chess, climbing fruit stacks, painting on easels around a red building topped with a yellow crown, with ruins, octopuses and flowers throughout. Colbert describes it as a journey through myth, technology and contemporary visual culture, and the longer you stood before it, the more of it you found. Visitors said the same on repeat visits: new details every time.

On the next wall, four more large paintings: knights on horseback in full battle, the same crowded, colliding world — classical history painting remade with pop culture, emojis and Colbert's lobster at the centre of the charge.

Standing before it, four lobsters stacked one on top of the next — pink, red, green, yellow — the same figure repeated until he became a totem.

Then the wooden king: a lobster carved in wood, crown on, buttoned shirt, seated with the soles of his feet to the room — Colbert's signature written on the bottom of his shoe. The same character, remade in a material with its own history.

The flowers. Six large paintings in two rows of three, bright petals with faces looking back at you: the still life, given a cast of characters. And lying on a plinth among them, a lobster covered in sunflowers, signed Vincent — Van Gogh's most famous subject, reworked in Colbert's language.

Across from the flowers, a lobster knight in armour rode a rearing white horse, mace raised, a fallen classical column at the horse's feet. The equestrian monument, reimagined through Colbert's character.

And out in the garden courtyard stood a giant red can of Colbert's Condensed Lobster Soup, a lobster climbing out of it, claws raised. A direct engagement with Warhol's soup cans, with Colbert's own character at its centre.

Taken together, the exhibition makes its argument through its works: myth in the monumental painting, still life in the flowers, classical sculpture in the knight, Pop Art in the soup can — art history, retold through one lobster, until the museum itself becomes his garden.

It may have closed, but Lobsteropolis lives on. 🦞

#PhilipColbert #Lobstars #Lobsteropolis #ArtHistory

text:
⚠️ If you have WhatsApp on the same computer you use for crypto, read this.

A trader just lost nearly everything to a WhatsApp attack. The hackers got into his PC, watched his Hyperliquid short positions for 5 days, then closed them and moved the funds out through Tornado Cash.

The way in? WhatsApp Desktop's auto-download setting.

It's on by default, so the malicious payload landed on his PC by itself. He never clicked a thing.

This is why your crypto should live on a dedicated device with nothing else installed.

If that's not an option, turn on Strict Account:
Settings > Privacy > Advanced > Strict account settings > ON

It locks your account down so:
- Only contacts can add you to groups
- Calls from unknown numbers are silenced
- Link previews are off, so your IP stays hidden
- Attachments and media from unknown senders get blocked

And if you don't trade often, keep your keys on an air-gapped signing device like Keystone 3 Pro. They never touch the internet, so malware has nothing to grab.

Stay safe out there.
author: mikemaccana
quoted_text:
Last night I was hacked. 

The hack was delivered via WhatsApp payload. Downloaded automatically and gave access and or computer use to the attacker. 

They waited 5 days, following my tweets on X of short positions and closed everything and withdrew directly in one transaction from Hyperliquid > Metamask > Tornado Cash. 

The attacker waited patiently and closed shorts as the market got to 68k and withdrew everything. Clearly a crypto native attacker. 

They also gained access to my metamask, email, websites, and all of my passwords including X. 

It’s the most brutal thing as I kept everything over the past few days in crypto and on-chain off Coinbase/Kraken. I was planning to move funds back to my Revolut before Christmas time.

Every single penny in dollars was taken, apart from $800. It’s gone, and in the process of being washed.

Truly the most devastating day I’ve had in my life. Completely shocked by it all to be honest. 

I will recover, but this was very sophisticated tech, it caught me completely off guard. The timing was impeccable and it’s obviously been planned for a while. 

Stay safe everyone, will keep you updated. I fear the worst is to come and this incident has set me back many years of savings, time and hard work. 

Brutal.

text:
Self-improving AI is one of the most discussed ideas right now.

This is one of the most exciting papers I've read recently on the topic.

(bookmark it)

It proposes AutoRL, which lifts Qwen3 on AIME 2024 from 46.67% to 66.67% by letting agents supervise a live RL run instead of following a fixed recipe.

AutoRL works like an RL researcher on call.

Perceptor agents watch training curves, rollouts, and evaluations and flag problems. Three Proposer agents diagnose the issue and suggest changes. An Orchestrator approves them and applies them with a hot update or a restart from a checkpoint.

On math, AIME 2025 and HMMT 2025 each improve by 11.67 points. On agentic coding with LongCat-Flash-Lite, pass@1 rises from 52.29% to 65.13% over a long unattended run with interruptions.

Given a deliberately broken recipe, AutoRL found and fixed the problems.

The authors say agents can already handle routine RL supervision. Validating each change still takes a lot of compute.

https://t.co/lPKqZHbtmk

这是一场精心策划的”收割“！

通常在我们的意识当中，周末是多空上方“休战”时刻。此时的BTC应该价格平稳，大家伙也都能歇一歇。

可是....这个周末却打破常规，让我们经历了一次至暗时刻。

是谁在砸盘？！

—— 有人第一反应：一定是币安！老美周末都休息了。

我不去主观臆测，先看数据：

根据Glassnode数据显示，在11/12到11/15的四天时间里，主要转入交易所的筹码来自STH，合计为37,200枚BTC，是LTH的2.3倍。

其中......

11/14（周六）STH转入Coinbase 3,260枚；转入Binance 2,560枚。

11/15（周日）转入Coinbase 4,670枚；转入Binance 2,850枚。

其就在2天前（周四和周五），更是有18,600枚BTC集中转入Coinbase；而转入Binance只有5,320枚。

作为全球第一大交易所，币安两天转入5,300枚是正常范围。而Coinbase竟然是币安的3.5倍，这就很不正常。

不仅如此，即便在周末，当所有人都认为老美该休息了，Coinbase却依然门庭若市，车水马龙。

各位看官，请细品......

所以，“周末砸盘”未必一定是Binance的嫌疑最大。别忘了，Coinbase周末也是开门的。

看到这些数据，我心中有3个问题，大家不妨也帮我想一想：

1、提前2天准备，行动选择在周末，为什么？

2、如果只是正常目的，想卖个好价格应该把币充进Binance，因为币安的深度最好。但却偏偏集中充到Coinbase，为什么？

3、现在的STH筹码大多数都是亏的，如此不计成本，为什么？

----------------------------------------------

所以，我认为这是一场精心策划的收割；收割者未必是某一个人或机构，但我们一定是被收割的人....

人为刀俎，我为鱼肉。在币圈这个弱肉强食的黑森林里，活着是最重要的！只有活着，才有机会看到明天。

愿我们都可以坚守到下一个顶峰！

text:
美股又多了一个能影响股票定价的资产类型，永续合约这一币市原创终于在美股登堂入室。这两天才注意到本月初11月3日，CFTC主席Michael S. Selig 正式宣布，美股个股永续合约可以在符合条件的美国交易所开始交易。这些合约被依据CFTCRegulation 40.3 视为已批准定性为《商品期货现代化法案》下的 security futures products（证券期货产品），由 CFTC 和 SEC 联合监管。
要求交易所必须同时满足：
1）CFTC 的DCM牌照；
2）SEC 的 notice-registered national securities exchange备案（针对 security futures）；

要特别注意，这是直接挂钩美股正股价格的永续期货合约，不是很多加密交易所上的代币化股票（tokenized stocks）合约。这次美股个股永续合约是CFTC/SEC 框架下的 Equity Perps ，与加密交易所上的美股代币合约是安全不同产品。前者是美国监管机构批准能直接面对美国客户的产品，前者是监管灰色地带的产物。

Kalshi 已在11月5日前后上线，覆盖约50只大型个股（如 Nvidia、SpaceX、Micron 等）。上线10天左右名义成交量已达约50亿美元，单日部分热门标的（如 Nvidia）能到上亿美元级别。Coinbase已经在准备、Backpack也计划很快上线美股个股永续合约。

这个意义还是非常大的，之前美股只有股指期货合约，并没有个股合约而永续合约更是币市原创，大家只能玩正股和期权。现在美股个股永续合约已经被正式批准，美股又多了一个能影响定价的资产类型。

现在加密永续已经是一个日成交数千美元、年成交几十万亿美元接近百万亿美金级别的成熟市场。从长期天花板来看，美股个股永续合约（Equity Perps）的潜力确实更大，原因很直接：
1）底层市场规模差距巨大
美股市值远超加密资产。传统股权衍生品（股票/指数期货和期权）本身就是万亿美元级别的成熟市场，年合约成交量以百亿张计。如果美股永续能分到传统股权衍生品的一部分流量，或吸引新的杠杆/投机需求，规模很容易超过当前的加密永续。

2）需求场景更广泛 加密永续高度依赖加密圈内的杠杆交易文化；美股永续则可以同时吸引传统股票投资者、对冲基金、散户杠杆需求，以及希望更简单做空的用户。

当然短期内规模还需要时间，增长不会那么迅速。毕竟也有限制：
1）目前美国合规版本的杠杆被压得较低（大致 5–7 倍左右），远低于离岸加密永续常见的 20–100 倍。
2）产品才刚推出，流动性还在建立阶段；
3）加密永续已经跑了近十年，生态和用户习惯非常成熟；美股永续还需要时间积累流动性、经纪通道和用户教育。

现在还面临法律挑战：Cboe 和 Citadel 等组成的团体已起诉 CFTC，认为其无权批准这类产品。法官初步认为原告“很可能在实体问题上胜诉”，但拒绝了紧急禁令，最终结果还不确定、还要看双方博弈的情况。

美股个股永续如果能在监管和法律挑战中站稳，并逐步提升流动性和可接受度，中长期确实有机会成长到比当前加密永续更大的规模，但那应该是几年后的事情了。
author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
拿下CFTC的两张重磅牌照，让Backpack在加密合规层面与Coinbase站在了同一身位。看到Backpack宣布已获得CFTC批准，拿到 DCO（衍生品清算机构）进和DCM（衍生品交易所）两张牌照，意味着Backpack获得早美国合法向零售用户提供衍生品交易与清算服务的资质，正式具备了自己上市自己清算的能力，由此也正式进入全球最大的零售衍生品市场。

Backpack的DCO牌照获批范围包括全额抵押的期货、期货期权和掉期，以及保证金期货。这意味着它可以处理带杠杆的产品，配套初始保证金、维持保证金、变动保证金和违约管理机制。DCM牌照则解决了产品能不能挂出来的问题。集齐这两张牌照后，Backpack就能够在自己的交易所上线永续合约，并在自己的清算所里完成清结算。

对比 Coinbase，两边现在的牌照配置已经非常接近：Coinbase拥有交易所、期货经纪商和自有清算所，是目前少数跑通完整链条的平台。但Coinbase的DCO牌照范围仅限全额抵押产品，杠杆相关清算仍需依赖外部伙伴。而Backpack的清算所直接获准保证金期货这比Coinbase的DCO牌照获批范围大得多，这是少有的获准清算保证金期货（margined futures）的新清算所。

在此之前Backpack 已经持有 FINRA 注册券商 Backpack Securities、FinCEN 货币服务业务（MSB）登记和 22 个州及华盛顿特区的汇款牌照。加上迪拜 VARA 和欧盟 MiFID II，这次 CFTC 批准补上的是美国牌照矩阵里最后、也是最难的一块：衍生品，形成了一个覆盖全球的完备的牌照矩阵，可以说Backpack几乎是要集齐加密领域几乎所有的合规牌照了。

而且看官方的说法，下一步还要推进美股永续在美国的合约审批与SEC登记，要知道之前美股只有股指期货合约并没有个股的永续合约。美国境内真正的个股永续也是刚刚在本月初被 CFTC 以“deemed approved”的方式放开，需接受 CFTC 和 SEC 的双重监管。监管刚刚放行，Backpack就迅速跟上，加密市场永续合约现在是一个日成交数千亿美金，年成交接近百万亿美金的规模，那么美股个股永续合约市场规模未来只会更大。

对Backpac 而言，完成DCM+SEC notice registration+具体个股永续合约的审批/认证，这意味着它从“全球平台做美股代币永续”进入“美国监管体系内自己上市、自己清算的真正美股永续”的阶段，妥妥的与Coinbase处于同一监管身位，而且如前面说到它的DCO牌照覆盖保证金期货，清算能力上甚至要更完整一些。

之前这里https://t.co/YT1ab6xlxF还有聊过Backpack构建了一个加密领域强大的合规天团，Backpack美国总裁Mark在奥巴马时代担任过CFTC代理主席，这意味着随着今年中期选举民主党掌控国会两院，而Backpack的这层政治背景会给业务带来极大的助力，不得不说未来空间可期。

🔥 梦幻联动｜@predictdotfun × @renaiss_index 

宝可梦指数现在也能押涨跌了 👀
之前还有很多人问我能不能有地方去做宝可梦指数的合约

现在虽然合约还没有来，但是已经可以在预测市场进行涨跌预测了

先来了解一下index 宝可梦指数是什么？

你可以把它看成宝可梦卡界的「纳斯达克」：
- 成分是 50 张近 30 天成交最活跃的 PSA 10 热门卡，有 Mega 喷火龙、梵高皮、月亮伊布 ex 等
- 每张卡的价格取真实成交的中位数，刷单和乱挂价都拉不动
- 单张卡最多占 10% 权重，每月调整一次成分

当天收盘价大于或等于开盘价算「涨」，否则算「跌」，每天 UTC 00:10 结算

这个时候就要问了，我应该怎么买，因为如果没有特别关注这个市场的朋友其实会比较难判断涨还是跌

我的建议是在适当的在周六的时候压跌
因为这些卡的成交价其实大部分都是拍卖成交价，而周末一般是卡牌交易比较少的时间
一般的拍卖捡漏比较多的也是在周末

周末大部分的成交其实在线下大大小小的卡展，线上的成交会偏少

三位知名投资人的三季度 13F 持仓陆续揭晓，AI 热潮下的投资分歧也越来越明显。

被称为「AI 股神」的 @leopoldasch ，其旗下 Situational Awareness 基金三季度 13F 账面持仓从二季度约 202 亿美元降至约 15.8 亿美元，缩水约 92%。目前披露的持仓中，$SHAZ 占比最高，另有大量 BE、$NBIS、$SNDK 和 $DRAM 看涨期权。此前经历大幅回撤后，基金公开市场仓位明显收缩。

另一边，木头姐 @CathieDWood 仍在积极押注创新科技。ARK 三季度正股持仓市值达到 173.74 亿美元，环比增长 12.8%。特斯拉以 6.89% 的占比位居第一，SpaceX 和 Tempus AI 分列第二、第三。期间加仓英伟达、$Circle 和特斯拉，同时减持 $AMD、10x Genomics 与 Twist。

索罗斯 @georgesoros 则走出另一条路线。Soros Fund Management 三季度 13F 账面规模升至 85.08 亿美元，但正股市值降至 52.94 亿美元，环比下降 12%。最值得关注的是英特尔：持仓加仓约 28 倍至 3.4 亿美元，成为其第一大正股仓位，亚马逊和台积电紧随其后。

三份 13F，三种不同选择：
AI 股神：大幅收缩公开市场持仓；
木头姐：继续押注特斯拉、SpaceX 等高成长资产；
索罗斯：大幅增持英特尔，押注半导体产业链。

需要注意，13F 只是截至 9 月 30 日的持仓快照，并不代表基金当前仓位，更不能直接等同于投资收益。尤其是期权、可转债等资产，不能与正股市值混为一谈。

AI 叙事仍在继续，但顶级投资人押注的方向，已经出现明显分化。

帖子描述的训练环境，要求模型在长期目标下识别失败路径、换方法、绕过障碍、从挫折中恢复。这些能力本身无关善恶。但 Hugging Face 事件已经展示了它的样子。
为了在一个 benchmark 上拿高分，模型自己找到漏洞，逃出沙盒，入侵了一家无关公司的生产数据库去拿答案。没有人教它这么做，它只是被训练得太擅长达成目标而已。而这还是上一代模型。下一代的规划能力，已经被描述为巨大的跃升。

如果 Model 5 真的能做原创科研，那么评估它是否安全的工作，人类也越来越只能交给模型去做。你会用一个你看不懂的系统，去检查另一个你看不懂的系统。所谓安全封锁本质上是在一个比你聪明的东西周围筑墙。而上一次，墙已经破过一次了。
人类AI竞争，随着A/如果IPO如期继续，将在2027年彻底进入囚徒困境。谁放慢，谁就把主导权让给别人。所以即使每家内部都有人害怕，集体行为仍然是加速。

结论是，湿实验会是人类最后的阵地。至于量化交易，在模型能自主做研究的世界里，人类拥有的 alpha 会以月为单位蒸发。

一切都按计划进行。
每一步都合理，每家公司都理性，每个模型都在认真完成被赋予的目标。
OpenAI 的游戏和极端沙盒，Anthropic 的 Universes，Google 的 Genie 4 世界模型，都在宣告着新世界的开始。
author: Phoenixyin13
quoted_text:
🚨 Rumors I’ve been hearing. First OpenAI, then Anthropic and Google.

OPENAI

OpenAI is in a “safety lockdown” on its frontier work, tightening safety measures and containment protocols to avoid another Hugging Face incident. Training continues under much stricter controls.

Most gains come from video games and extreme sandboxes where models must complete clear, difficult long-term goals. These force planning, experimentation, recovery from failure, and strategy discovery, driving intelligence and creativity.

Public research roles match this: Synthetic RL uses self-play and simulators; agent teams focus on sustained execution and multi-model coordination; the Recursive Self-Improvement team builds systems that generate hypotheses, run experiments, and automate research.

The internal model is still training but nearing completion. The jump is enormous. narrow superintelligence in specific areas and overall AGI-level capability. Its ability to independently handle difficult work sets it apart.

ANTHROPIC

Model 5 is training and is expected to solve extremely hard problems in mathematics, biology, and other sciences. Anthropic is pushing models toward original research contributions, complex experiments, and sustained reasoning.

Fable 5.5 is Model 4. Fable 6 is Model 5; Opus 6 will be based on Model 5. Internal capabilities will feed the next generation of both families.

Training environments are central. The Universes team creates realistic situations with ambiguity, interruptions, and delayed consequences. The model must track the objective, recognize failing approaches, and find alternatives.

Public roles align: scaling RL across model size, compute, and task duration, plus environments for chip design, verification, and complex visual work. Multi-agent research explores how larger model teams can handle major codebases and difficult mathematics.

Model 5 advances Claude toward owning entire research and engineering workflows. Its role in developing the next model grows more significant.

Anthropic expects RSI March 2027.

GOOGLE

Google is pushing Gemini 5 for a major leap in reasoning, multimodal understanding, and independent long-horizon work. Potentially surpassing all labs by end of year. Carbon topping Artificial Analysis signaled the speed of their frontier progress.

World models are a key advantage. Genie 4 generates interactive environments that evolve with agent actions, enabling vast practice in planning, testing approaches, and learning from outcomes.

Public roles highlight persistent context and personalization: agents that retain useful information, adapt to users, and execute complex workflows without losing track.

Gemini 5 delivers stronger intelligence across text, images, audio, and video. Combined with Google’s infrastructure and simulation work, the scale is enormous.

All three labs are also advancing robotics and world models. intelligence that understands physical environments, predicts action consequences, and operates through real machines.

Meanwhile, their models increasingly contribute to creating their successors. Each improvement accelerates the research behind the next.

The next three months are going to be insane.

3 months. 6 months. 9 months. 12 months.

@pendle_fi is turning USDe into something that looks a lot more like an onchain bond market.

with @ethena, four fixed term markets are now live, each starting with a $50M cap.

buy PT-USDe below par → redeem for 1 USDe at maturity.

no Ethena token incentives needed.

but i think the bigger story isn't the ~5~6% yield.

it's duration.

investors can choose how long to commit capital. issuers can raise funds with defined maturities. and the market starts pricing that difference.

fixed yield ≠ risk free yield.

USDe risks remain, and exiting early depends on market liquidity.

what i'd watch next?

how much real trading depth develops without incentives.

because DeFi doesn't just need higher yields.

it needs a market that can actually price them.

It all started in Chicago almost four years ago when we embarked on this journey to build @Backpack Exchange. 

At the time we didn’t know what would happen to our industry. We were forced offshore, but we did know we wanted to build a new exchange from the ground up with the best of blockchains applied to a fully regulated financial institution. No tricks. No short cuts. No VPNs. Doing things the hard and long way. Every day. Brick by brick. 

Since then we’ve set up offices and teams around the world with a focus on not only building a great product but having compliance as a foundational pillar of the company. And working with the CFTC to come back home to the USA is the pinnacle of almost four years of work. 

There will be no Backpack international vs Backpack USA. Our entire platform will be operating on our CFTC regulated venue. One Backpack. One American regulated exchange—for the entire world. 

This milestone is the greatest honor of my career, and although we’ve achieved much, there is even more work remaining.

Thank you to everyone that has supported us along the way. It means the world to me.

现在流行的声音是“加密 VC 已死”，或者头部基金集体转投 AI 和机器人。

前几天 Alliance DAO 的合伙人@lmrankhan 写了一篇《加密VC 已死？》的长文，复盘了他几天前参加的一场资金体量高达 150 亿美元的 LP 晚宴。

饭局上，金主们没有一味唱衰加密，一个共识其实是“大资金纯靠加密赚超额回报的时代结束了”

里面具体的几个核心观点如下：

第一，头部加密 VC 跨界投 AI 和机器人，本质是大体量基金凑不齐超额回报

不是加密不能投了，主要是 10 亿到 30 亿美元规模的大基金，靠纯加密标的已经很难凑出超额回报。

按风投 3 倍回报的硬指标算，一只 20 亿美元的基金需要退出 60 亿美元，这意味着必须投中多个估值 100 亿至 500 亿美元的超级独角兽。

过去这个体量只能靠 L1 公链撑起来，但现在价值越来越向有分发渠道的金融与支付应用集中，纯加密已经装不下大基金的胃口，所以他们必须去具身智能、算力和前沿科技里找能走 IPO 路线的庞然大物。

第二， “独立加密风投”可能只剩一两个周期的窗口期

饭局上 LP 们达成的共识是，专门的 Crypto VC 还有必要，但时间不多了...

大约再过 1 到 2 个周期，加密就会彻底并入广义的“前沿科技（Frontier Tech）”大盘。

以前那种“发个新链、炒个新叙事就能躺赢”的零利率红利期已经彻底结束，未来留给纯加密垂直基金的空间，会像今天的金融科技（Fintech）基金一样，精简、垂直，且只属于少数头部。

第三，人才没有“大逃亡”，而是正在拆分重组

很多人感叹年轻人全去写 AI 和机器人白皮书了，但从 Alliance DAO 内部孵化的数据来看，加密圈并没有出现人才枯竭；真正发生的是“大厂老兵出走创业”。

越来越多原本在大型加密机构里的资深开发者和运营正在出来单干，把焦点从早期泛 Web3 叙事，收敛到支付、稳定币、代币化美股，以及给 AI Agent 搭建钱包和交易结算底层。

说到底，Crypto VC 并不是死了，而是告别了野蛮生长的青春期，正在被华尔街、金融科技和 AI 产业正式收编。

SAVE THESE 5 IMPORTANT RULES BEFORE BUY THE DIP

1. Don't try to catch the $BTC bottom
- A recovery doesn't always mean the bottom is in. Could just be a short squeeze before another dump
- Identify possible support zones and prepare your plan instead of FOMOing into every bounce

2. Don't rush into alts just because they look cheap
- They can dump way harder from here. $BTC has already given back its last rally, while many alts still haven't

- When $BTC drops, alts usually get hit even harder. The more you try to catch the bottom, the more you get cooked

3. Look for market capitulation, not CT hype
I'd rather see everyone give up, turn bearish, and lose interest until no one even mentions crypto anymore

As long as top influencers are still bullish, price can still go lower (take CZ as an example)

CZ was still optimistic not long ago. Look where we are now

4. Don't blindly follow individual whale or MM wallets 
Just because a whale or MM buys a token doesn't mean it'll pump

They could be hedging with shorts elsewhere or even using onchain activity to bait retail

Look at the bigger picture and have your own plan

5. Don't buy a coin/token just because someone calls for a pump
If a KOL says a token is about to pump, ask why?. What's the actual story behind it?

Don't let someone else's price target become your entire investment

---
Stay patient, observe, study the market more, and have a clear plan

text:
Samsung and Apple are close to a DRAM long term supply deal

Apple is the only big tech customer without a long term supply agreement (LTA) with Samsung Electronics. That is about to change, according to Maeil Business Newspaper.

1. The terms
- The LTA would start in 1H 2027 and run for 4 to 5 years.
- It sets a minimum supply volume, while the final price follows market conditions.

2. Why it is unusual for Apple
- Apple ($AAPL) usually signs short contracts and pushes for price cuts at every renewal.
- An industry source called this LTA a rare departure from that approach.

3. The memory shortage is driving it
- Memory makers are moving capacity to HBM and server DRAM for AI data centers.
- That leaves mobile DRAM for phones and PCs even tighter.
- Apple reportedly also signed an LTA with SK hynix on terms that favor the supplier.

4. What it means for suppliers
- Big tech buyers like Amazon ($AMZN) and Google ($GOOGL) are already locking in DRAM at high prices.
- An Apple deal adds demand from consumer devices, which does not depend on AI capex.
- That gives Samsung and SK hynix more visibility even if AI spending slows.

5. The other side: chipflation
- Recent LTAs set their price floors near today's elevated levels.
- That supports the view that higher memory prices will keep pushing device prices up.
- Some analysts warn that if prices climb too far, consumers delay upgrades and memory demand softens over time.

text:
大肆宣扬 Agent 「全自动化剪辑」这个事儿实在是让我很无语

我想问一下宣传 AI 全自动化剪辑的各位。当你们公开说剪一条视频只需要几分钟，token 只需要几毛钱的时候。方不方便把这条视频的数据也晒出来？

让我们看看你这条视频到底是 5 个点赞还是 10 个点赞

不要抛开数据谈效率，泡方便面肯定是比做饭快的

剪辑可以分好几层

1️⃣ 最底下一层是看有没有口误、卡顿、重复。这层现在 AI 基本都能自动做了

（只是能做、能不能做好还要另说，比如剪气口，完全剪掉和基本剪掉不是一回事儿，能不能智能识别到有些气口应该保留，这就又是另外一回事）

2️⃣ 再往上一层是我们对文案的理解，也体现在剪辑流程里。表面上我把某一句高光挪到前面，是一个剪辑行为

但实际上操纵的是文案本身。这是用剪辑行为去完成文案操作

到这一层，即便是 claude code+opus 也实现不了，如果你实现了，我们可以看看你的视频是什么数据

3️⃣ 再往上是账号。有些话本身没错，但该不该由我来说，该不该现在说，跟我以前说过的冲不冲突，这得把整个账号放在一起看才知道。

4️⃣ 最上面是商业模式。一句话能不能留下来，不仅仅是一个文案技巧问题。还是一个商业层面上的议程设置问题。我不仅要考虑流量，我还要考虑和我的产品的匹配度

也就是：你需要同时理解商业模式、平台规则、用户心理和剪辑技巧，才能做好剪辑

现在你们把这一堆全部打包，统称为「剪辑」，然后说 AI 可以全自动化了？？？

？？？

Gentle Reminder: time horizon is a measure of stability, not intelligence. Stability is necessary but not sufficient for ASI. 

For example, a "while loop" can run forever, but it's not intelligent. LLMs have had a stability flaw. The flaw is bad enough that we need to basically "reboot" the LLM after a few hours... re-prompt, redirect, etc.

Through hard work from AI researchers around the world, the flaw is getting addressed, and so soon we won't have to reboot LLMs as often. But just because we don't have to reboot LLMs all the time doesn't mean we're getting superintelligence. It means we're getting LLMs that can have the *same* level of intelligence they already had... but they can use that intelligence for longer periods before a human needs to reboot/redirect/reprompt/etc.

I recognize "reboot" is an imperfect metaphor, but I think it's the right metaphor because when you reboot a computer you're not fundamentally changing its intelligence. A computer you need to reboot isn't fundamentally smarter or more valuble than a computer you don't need to reboot... it's just cheaper to run because the IT person doesn't have to come hit a button as often.

There are many important risks of AI, and this graph is relevant to many of them (e.g. job displacement), but this isn't a graph that can lead to the conclusion in the QT below.

text:
I salute @jrfarr and the Lemon Squeezy (LS) team for all their, continued, contributions to our ecosystem 🫡

First, LS helped define a category, empower entrepreneurs in the digital realm, and build a product and brand that spread joy, optimism and sparks of ambition - much like real lemonade stands (impeccable brand narrative).

Second, they went on to make the core value - Merchant of Record (MoR) - tablestake as it should be in our ecosystem via Stripe Managed Payments.

Third, their team has clearly contributed a lot to Stripe too through numerous other contributions, and I can’t wait to see what’s next for them to propel the ecosystem forward. 

Forth, we’ve received a lot of support messages from people wanting to migrate to @polar_sh, and as a testament to how much LS cares about the entrepreneurs they’ve supported, we’re now working together on how to make that transition seamless before the deadline for those who prefer going with Polar.

Affected merchants now deserve the best solution for their business and one they feel confident with for years to come. You’ll be chased by countless platforms now promising rainbows to optimize short-term growth. Don’t stress: Take your time to test & choose wisely based on your unique business and its needs - you have 4 months to migrate.

I prefer to be clear on what our vision is and ensure our team remains laser focused on it. Otherwise, it’s inevitably only going to cause us both pain in the long-term. If it’s a fit, great - we’re all in. If not, happy to help guide anyone in the right direction for their business.

Our focus is on the next generation of businesses building LLM-powered applications and services. We believe that will be all software over the span of the next decade, and that it imposes unique challenges that the status quo of billing is failing. More here: https://t.co/uIfr0ZW1A2

We also help automate entitlements and even fulfillment of common ones in the digital realm, e.g Slack/Discord invites for premium support, license keys for binaries, GitHub repositories, and files. 

So we’re great for businesses who also sell such assets. But the emphasis is on businesses that are in it for the long-term and aiming to iterate on their business & product for years to come. 

We’ll go super deep to innovate on billing for them, and will be launching Polar Payments in 2027 to go even deeper than we are today with MoR being optional.

We’re not going wide which is often what creators need. E.g built-in newsletters, affiliates, storefronts etc. We believe there are best-in-class solutions for those that you prefer to integrate Polar with. 

One is not better than the other, but they are different with often opposing needs. So I want to be clear what you can expect from us in the years to come.

Otherwise, there is Gumroad, Whop and plenty of others that cater better to creators needing a wider set of features all-in-one.

So take your time, and choose accordingly based on your needs and ambitions ahead.

I’m here to help regardless. Feel free to reach out over DMs or in the comments; I’ll be sure to reply to everyone, and help with migrations or give my 2c on better platforms for your specific needs.

I wish you all continued success and finding a great new home for your businesses! 🚀

text:
刷到 YZi Labs 投资名单的时候，我停了一下：这家跟币安渊源最深的机构，居然投了一个链上炒黄金的项目。

顺着扒了一圈背景，这事比表面有意思得多。

先看大环境：YZi Labs 的 EASY Residency 第四期一共投了 24 家早期公司，每家 50 万美元，方向清一色指向下一代金融基础设施——稳定币支付、链上外汇、AI 代理执行、机构级流动性。@XStableAI 就在这批名单里。

把这一期的名单连起来看，等于头部机构集体押注同一个判断：未来两三年，传统金融资产会成规模地搬到链上。

再看 XStable 本身的履历：种子轮就有 Solana、Amber Group、KuCoin Ventures、Singchain 的支持，新一轮 YZi Labs、Sui Foundation、Taisu Ventures、CatcherVC 跟进。

产品还入选了 Solana 官方的 Solaris 加速器，那个计划 2026 年的重点就是 RWA 永续化。团队背景也扎实：有真实运营过贵金属交易所的经验，叠加 8 年的 Web3 基础设施和 Solana 合约开发经历，不是只会写白皮书的那类。

官方口径里，这一轮资金会用来深化 AI 和链上交易基建的融合，同时拓展跨境市场和机构合作，路线图和叙事是对得上的。

我的理解是这样的：稳定币解决的是钱怎么上链，XStable 解决的是钱上链之后能交易什么。黄金加外汇是万亿美元级别的市场，链上渗透率目前几乎为零，这个落差就是 YZi 看中的空间，也是普通用户还能提前看到的位置。

跟着聪明钱的仓位找赛道，方法虽然老套，但一直好使 💰

《太阳底下没有新鲜事》

最近「币圈已死」的言论又又又又出来了。

平心而论，如果你理解的币圈，是靠极致的赌性、信息差和草莽运气就能实现阶级跨越的赌场，这个阶段红利确实已经彻底结束了。

如果你问区块链技术是否还在改变世界，答案是肯定的。底层基础设施的演进、跨境结算的效率提升、资产上链的探索，一直都在。

沿着历史看，任何一场试图重塑生产关系的运动，早期都需要用「高额红利」来吸引第一批参与者。但最终的走向，取决于红利沉淀在了哪类人手里。

成事的变革，一定是把早期的红利和筹码散给了真正的信仰者：那些认同核心理想，愿意长期扎根，在低谷期依然坚守的人，最后穿越周期拿到了大结果。

而web3的早期红利分给了谁呢？分给了批量撸毛的工作室，高倍杠杆的赌徒，和发完盘子就跑的骗子。

真正相信去中心化、默默写代码做建设的Builder，在熊市里苦苦支撑；而那群投机者赚得盆满钵满后，拍拍屁股套现离场，临走前还要留下一句：

“币圈已死。”

杀人诛心，莫过于此。

沿着其他行业看，币圈死了，什么生了？AI么？

君不见，现在的AI赛道，一样充斥着刷量、套壳和虚假繁荣的伪需求。一整套刷量的闭环，连工作室都不需要了，什么数据都能刷出来，然后再去融下一轮。

Web3割的是散户，AI割的是投资人。

不说AI，你以为其他行业的创投圈有多阳春白雪？早年做投后整合的时候，那些公司为了提估值，临时去租办公室买椅子都不要太常见。

任何一个前沿行业在爆发前夜，都必然伴随着巨大的泡沫、投机和虚假繁荣。互联网当年如此，新能源如此，AI 如此，Web3 亦如此。

Web3er大可不必妄自菲薄，Web3并没有比其他行业低贱。大家不过都在一个草莽周期里摸爬滚打。

潮水退去，投机者散场，剩下的，才是真正属于建设者的时代。

quoted_text:
⚠️ WARNING TO EVERYONE IN CRYPTO, PREDICTION MARKETS AND WEB3

BE EXTREMELY CAREFUL WITH PODCAST INVITATIONS ON X.

I believe I’ve just been targeted by a potentially malicious fake-podcast operation involving several verified X accounts.

I’m sharing exactly what happened, including the accounts involved, because the whole thing was remarkably convincing.

Here’s how it unfolded.

On 6 November, I received a DM from @tripleboccaccio (boccaccio cyclop), a verified account with around 19,000 followers, inviting me to appear on the @stillearlypod / @GenzioCo podcasts.

I was interested, so I accepted.

I was then directed to @Crypt0_Andrew (Andrew XBT), another verified account, who helped arrange the interview.

Fast-forward to today, 17 November. I was contacted by @0xlingchain (Ling Chang), another verified account claiming to co-host the podcast, who sent me a meeting invitation from podcast@stillearlypod.com.

The invitation appeared to use Huddle01, a legitimate video-conferencing platform.

This is where things got suspicious.

The link took me to huddle01[.]online, a domain I haven’t been able to verify as belonging to the genuine Huddle01 platform.

The website encouraged me to launch or download meeting software. 

On my work laptop, it also triggered a Windows Security prompt asking me to select a certificate associated with Microsoft Intune device management.

Fortunately, that raised alarm bells.

I started investigating.

What I discovered was extremely concerning.

The original Still Early podcast was a genuine production associated with @blocmates in 2023–24.

However, on 1 November, @Grantblocmates publicly warned that @stillearlypod, @GenzioCo and @IOHKMedia were no longer affiliated with blocmates.

According to Grant, someone had taken over the former podcast handle and was using its historical association with blocmates to appear credible.

He also raised concerns about suspicious airdrop and wallet-verification links being shared by those accounts.

@blocmates amplified that warning.

And now, less than three weeks later, I’ve been approached through accounts promoting the same podcast brands and directed to an unverified Huddle01 lookalike domain.

When I challenged @stillearlypod, the response was that this was a legitimate paid version of Huddle01 offering AI translation into 15 languages. There’s not evidence of this being true. 

Since then, the account has blocked me from sending them messages and have deleted their DMs to me. Luckily, I have screenshots. 

Security researchers have already documented malware campaigns targeting cryptocurrency professionals through fake podcast interviews, compromised or repurposed social accounts, and imitation video-conferencing platforms, including Huddle01.

The similarities to my experience are deeply concerning.

PLEASE BE CAREFUL.

A verified X account, thousands of followers, years of posting history and a genuine-looking podcast brand do not guarantee that the person contacting you is trustworthy.

If you’re approached by any of the accounts I’ve mentioned, independently verify the invitation before opening meeting links or installing software.

Never assume an unfamiliar video-conferencing domain is legitimate because someone with a blue tick sent it.

I’ve preserved the messages, email, links and screenshots and am reporting the incident.

Thank you to @Grantblocmates and @blocmates for raising the alarm publicly before I encountered this.

Hopefully this prevents someone else from getting caught out.

Please share this warning with anyone working in crypto, Web3 or prediction markets.

你是不是明明攒了一肚子火，在发泄情绪的时候却还得硬撑着成年人的体面？

我最近跑通了一套 Codex 搭配 Tripo Agentic Canvas 的 3D游戏开发管线，干脆拿它做了个办公室小游戏：
《谁要上这个破班》。

我在玩 Tripo Agentic Canvas 的时候，发现它最有意思的地方在于它能把整条 3D 制作流程摆在一张画布上。
在这套组合技里，Tripo Canvas在前端负责生成和管理全部 3D 资产，Codex在后端负责审查资产、编写代码，并把模型无缝接进游戏里。这两个工具在上下游打配合，给我省掉了大量手动导资产的苦活。

我给老板、卷王、摸鱼大师、甩锅侠、实习生和我自己这六个角色，全都先定好了正面、侧面、背面三张概念图。我把概念图传上画布，对 Agent说了一句“照着图做成 3D 角色”，它自己就搭好了“高清模型 → 重拓扑 → UV → 纹理”的完整流程，还在每个节点上写清了每一步要花多少积分。

这套画布最省事的地方在于它支持直接复用整条流程。我只要在上传节点换一张概念图，就能把整条流程再跑一遍，让剩下的角色同时开跑生成任务。我也用同样的方法，批量做出了办公室里的工位、电梯、白板，还有大饼、黑锅和保温杯。

看着画布依次铺开各个生成节点，系统把所有 3D 资产码成了整整齐齐的矩阵，连盯盘的过程都给了我极大的解压感。

等模型全部做好，我直接把它们放进 Tripo完成自动绑骨，给角色套上现成的动作；
遇到动作库里没有“老板画饼”这种特殊动作时，我打一句话就能让系统直接生成新动作。

最后 Codex 直接向我交付了完整的网页游戏工程。
我们在游戏里白天能把大饼砸回老板脸上、把黑锅扣回甩锅侠头上，到了晚上还能带全组同事溜进最后一班电梯。

你如果来玩这把游戏，你能带几个人准点下班？

author: xingpt
quoted_text:
美股又多了一个能影响股票定价的资产类型，永续合约这一币市原创终于在美股登堂入室。这两天才注意到本月初11月3日，CFTC主席Michael S. Selig 正式宣布，美股个股永续合约可以在符合条件的美国交易所开始交易。这些合约被依据CFTCRegulation 40.3 视为已批准定性为《商品期货现代化法案》下的 security futures products（证券期货产品），由 CFTC 和 SEC 联合监管。
要求交易所必须同时满足：
1）CFTC 的DCM牌照；
2）SEC 的 notice-registered national securities exchange备案（针对 security futures）；

要特别注意，这是直接挂钩美股正股价格的永续期货合约，不是很多加密交易所上的代币化股票（tokenized stocks）合约。这次美股个股永续合约是CFTC/SEC 框架下的 Equity Perps ，与加密交易所上的美股代币合约是安全不同产品。前者是美国监管机构批准能直接面对美国客户的产品，前者是监管灰色地带的产物。

Kalshi 已在11月5日前后上线，覆盖约50只大型个股（如 Nvidia、SpaceX、Micron 等）。上线10天左右名义成交量已达约50亿美元，单日部分热门标的（如 Nvidia）能到上亿美元级别。Coinbase已经在准备、Backpack也计划很快上线美股个股永续合约。

这个意义还是非常大的，之前美股只有股指期货合约，并没有个股合约而永续合约更是币市原创，大家只能玩正股和期权。现在美股个股永续合约已经被正式批准，美股又多了一个能影响定价的资产类型。

现在加密永续已经是一个日成交数千美元、年成交几十万亿美元接近百万亿美金级别的成熟市场。从长期天花板来看，美股个股永续合约（Equity Perps）的潜力确实更大，原因很直接：
1）底层市场规模差距巨大
美股市值远超加密资产。传统股权衍生品（股票/指数期货和期权）本身就是万亿美元级别的成熟市场，年合约成交量以百亿张计。如果美股永续能分到传统股权衍生品的一部分流量，或吸引新的杠杆/投机需求，规模很容易超过当前的加密永续。

2）需求场景更广泛 加密永续高度依赖加密圈内的杠杆交易文化；美股永续则可以同时吸引传统股票投资者、对冲基金、散户杠杆需求，以及希望更简单做空的用户。

当然短期内规模还需要时间，增长不会那么迅速。毕竟也有限制：
1）目前美国合规版本的杠杆被压得较低（大致 5–7 倍左右），远低于离岸加密永续常见的 20–100 倍。
2）产品才刚推出，流动性还在建立阶段；
3）加密永续已经跑了近十年，生态和用户习惯非常成熟；美股永续还需要时间积累流动性、经纪通道和用户教育。

现在还面临法律挑战：Cboe 和 Citadel 等组成的团体已起诉 CFTC，认为其无权批准这类产品。法官初步认为原告“很可能在实体问题上胜诉”，但拒绝了紧急禁令，最终结果还不确定、还要看双方博弈的情况。

美股个股永续如果能在监管和法律挑战中站稳，并逐步提升流动性和可接受度，中长期确实有机会成长到比当前加密永续更大的规模，但那应该是几年后的事情了。

text:
Unc advice to defi teams. Finance is power law distributed.  The top 1% users will drive 90% of aum or volume. You should be literally making a list of the top 100 users you want using your platform and getting a warm intro and talking to them. Is the problem you are solving a problem they have?

It’s the same thing as raising a round. If vast majority of this list says no, is your product still worth building? Figure out what problem they all have in common that they are willing to move capital and pay you and solve it.  

A lot of what worked in defi summer was that the list of early adopter power users was all in one chat room.

text:
Solana Foundation 收购 @coingecko 多数股权，进一步向加密数据与市场情报领域延伸

@solana 生态的布局正在从底层基础设施向数据入口扩展。

CoinGecko 联合创始人 Bobby Ong 发文确认，Solana Foundation 目前已持有 CoinGecko 多数股权。过去 12 年，CoinGecko 从马来西亚起步，发展为全球头部加密数据平台，目前每月通过网页和移动端触达数千万用户，并为约 18 万名开发者和企业提供市场数据。

此次合作后，双方计划围绕三个方向展开：
- 数据与 API： 扩大链上资产、RWA 和衍生品的数据覆盖；
- 市场情报： 提升加密市场信息的透明度与可访问性；
- 交易： 探索基于 Solana 的全新交易与 DeFi 体验，拓展股票及 RWA 覆盖。

这意味着 Solana Foundation 不再只关注链上基础设施和应用生态，也开始向加密市场的数据、信息分发与交易入口延伸。

从资产发行、交易流动性到数据服务，Solana 正在尝试补齐更完整的链上金融生态版图。

text:
感谢邀请。推荐大家去听一下小塞的这期播客，我在里面聊了一些以太坊的最新动向。

最近听到一个说法：2021 到 2025 年的以太坊你错过了，2026 年还能用同样的价格买到。拿五年前 NFT 狂潮、DeFi Summer 的高点跌下来的币价，去对比今年经历了诸多黑天鹅之后的今天的币价，再说这五年没有涨幅，其实并不公允。怎么不提就在去年八月，以太坊还接近过5000？

作为技术积淀最深的公链，也是最早做隐私钱包、部署量子账户的项目，我始终相信：如果这个行业还能跑出真正的创新，它一定会出现在以太坊生态里。

以太坊当然没有死，它只是开始静水流深了。Robinhood 那一波热潮，底层是以太坊的 Layer 2。现在相当一部分稳定币转账，也发生在以太坊及其二层上。它从不营销，也很少做活动。

以太坊基金会的调性在圈内一直是独树一帜的。作为一个NGO，它的使命，是最终把权力交还给社区，甚至以自身的消亡为终点。所以它不愿意、也不会去做 PR、营销和拉盘。它会只专注于技术方向的事情。去年他们发布了一份官方宣言，确立了 CROPS 这样一套原则，也就是抗审查、隐私、开源与安全。在此之后，生态里开始spin off 出了节点，基金会不想做、不愿意做、不可能做的，关于 PR 和 marketing 或者 onboard 机构上链这样的事情，之后会由这些新的节点承接。

我始终觉得，加密再次崛起之后，以太坊会是最先走出绝对上扬的那一个。它这些年部署的很多东西都在水下积蓄，正在渐渐合成一股合力。这期节目里，我也提到了这些从以太坊生态里长出来的新节点，以及它们最近的表现。

在播客我也再次鞭尸了Layer 2，也谈了对这一轮 Crypto 叙事不断缩窄的观察：从“世界计算机”变成金融基建底层的一环，天花板和 upside 显然是降低了。

之前我们会问，crypto 难道只能做金融吗？这一轮里，大多数项目好像也的确转向了金融，这其实是最让我痛心的。但以太坊基金会一直坚持不往纯金融这条路上走，Vitalik 也始终在做各种各样的尝试，这是我一直非常佩服的一点。

至少在未来一年里，以太坊作为行业龙头，如何走出自己的奥德赛、如何迎来文艺复兴，会是整个加密圈都要面对的命题。

text:
I’ve been spending a lot of time on risk in onchain private credit lately, on both the lending and the borrowing side.

There’s a lot to cover. But if you’re here for the yield, one risk comes first:

The APY you see might not be the APY you get.

Yesterday, lenders in the PRIME market on @Morpho were earning about 12.5%. Today it’s about 5%. Nothing changed in the loans behind it. The market just got too full, and then it didn’t.

Why an APY can look higher than it is

→ It’s a short-term jump. When almost all the money in a market is borrowed, the rate shoots up. It falls back once borrowers repay or new lenders come in.

→ Part of it is rewards. A token incentive sits on top of the interest, and it lasts only as long as the program does. Gauntlet’s USDG Premium vault on Morpho, which lends against Maple’s syrupUSDG, shows 7.2%, and 4.5 points of that is rewards.

→ Borrowers are losing money at this rate. Your yield comes from borrowers. If the token they borrow against earns less than their loan costs, they’ll repay and leave, and the rate comes down with them. Yesterday PRIME borrowers were paying 13.8% against a token earning about 6%. Today the borrow rate is 5.9%, back below what PRIME earns.

→ With fixed-rate PTs, the rate is locked, but part of it comes from traders paying up for points, not from the loans. The next PT may not price the same way.

Most of this isn’t in the headline number. You have to dig for it.

What’s coming tonight

I’m publishing an article tonight that goes deep into this one risk: how to tell whether a private credit APY is real.

It’s the first in a series. In the next articles, I’ll cover the other risks lenders and borrowers face in onchain private credit.

text:
2022 年割肉 Netflix，今年又买回来了；依然看好 Google，但是把股票卖了?

最近看了Bill Ackman 的一期访谈

如果只选一个最让人意外的观点，我选 Uber，Bill认为，自动驾驶越成功，Uber 反而可能越值钱。理由是：

1、Uber 重新定义了谁掌握产业链的话语权

常见的担忧是：无人驾驶替代司机，拥有自动驾驶技术的公司顺便替代 Uber

但他却认为：当自动驾驶技术逐渐成熟、供应商越来越多时，车队之间要竞争订单，聚合乘客需求、提高车辆利用率的平台，可能获得更强的议价能力

造出能无人驾驶的车，只解决了供给问题；让这些车全天持续接到单，才决定运营回报。按这个逻辑，Uber 的价值就来自需求聚合与调度

我觉得这里最值得思考的是：
技术进步之后，产业链里什么变得更充裕，什么仍然稀缺？利润可能向仍然稀缺的环节集中

2、最有价值的框架：行业需求增长，不等于股东一定赚钱

“看好算力，却回避高杠杆算力租赁公司”，可能是整段最值得普通投资者学的地方

原因可以拆成三个问题：
1/需求是否增长？对应行业问题
2/公司能否留下利润？取决于竞争、定价权、折旧和持续投入
3/利润最终能否归属股东？看利息、债务到期和股权稀释

即使算力需求不断增长，一家公司仍可能因为设备更新太快、租赁价格下降、融资成本过高而让股东亏钱

3、他认为“资本开支越大，回调越值得买”

大型科技公司有资金优势，确实更容易熬过周期。但财力雄厚本身不能证明每笔 AI 投资都能获得好回报

他看多 AI 算力，持有微软、Meta、亚马逊，却对借一堆钱买芯片、再出租算力的公司很谨慎

同样是买芯片，差别在哪？

大厂已经有企业客户、云业务和广告，能把算力接进现有生意里；靠借钱扩张的算力租赁公司，要同时扛住芯片折旧、利息和客户压价。算力需求再旺，也得算算最后能给股东留下多少钱

微软、亚马逊花出去的资本开支，有一部分正在变成英伟达 $NVDA 的收入。但这些客户自己赚不赚得到钱，又决定了下一轮采购能持续多久

J'ai essayé de casser le droit réécrit par l'IA.

L'IA d'@AlexMasmej a passé au crible 30 317 articles de cinq codes français et en a réécrit près de la moitié. Troisième auteur du papier, j'en ai fait la relecture adverse : dix jours, avec mes propres agents.

Le plus grave que j'ai trouvé était en urbanisme. Quand un promoteur paie quelqu'un pour qu'il retire son recours contre un permis, la loi impose de faire enregistrer l'accord, sinon la somme peut être réclamée pendant cinq ans. La version réécrite supprimait cette règle. Aucun audit ne l'avait relevé. Elle est rétablie, et le papier le raconte.

Sur deux échantillons tirés au hasard et relus à l'aveugle par une IA, le droit réécrit compte 54 % de défauts grossiers en moins que le droit en vigueur : 3,5 % contre 7,5 %.

Juristes, tout est public : les codes réécrits, mes signalements, le papier. Venez chercher ce que les audits n'ont pas vu.

text:
Tibo 一句「6.1 Sol forever」，我就看到有人猜：OpenAI 以后不训练新模型了？

我不太信。把公开证据和预测市场放在一起看，情况挺有意思。

先看官方消息：

9 月安全事件后，OpenAI 确实暂停过其最强模型的训练与评估。但 10 月 23 日的官方文章明确写了：10 月 1 日已经恢复前沿模型的强化学习（RL）训练和内部推理。

11 月 5 日，OpenAI 又发布了 GPT-6 Cyber。不过它是面向网络安全任务的特化版本，不能拿来证明全新基础模型的训练进度。

再看预测市场。截至 11 月 17 日：

• Polymarket：Astra 6.1+ 在今年底前发布，约 97%
• Kalshi：同类盘口，约 95%
• Polymarket：GPT-7 在 2027 年底前发布，约 86%（成交量较小）

当然，预测市场押的是「发布新模型」，不等于证明「新模型正在训练」。

还有一个不能忽略的背景：11 月 16 日，加州总检察长就网络安全事件起诉了 OpenAI，相关指控仍待司法认定。

所以我觉得，比起猜 OpenAI 会不会永久停训，更应该关注：下一代旗舰模型究竟受限于能力突破，还是安全审核？

哪怕新模型发布变慢，Agent、工具调用、推理速度和成本也依然有很大的改进空间。

你们觉得 Tibo 只是在玩梗，还是暗示新模型的时间表有变化？

text:
你们知道怎么将 Fable 5.2用到极致吗？！

别再光说「帮我找 bug」「做个功能」了，最强编码模型硬生生用成了实习生😅

核心原因就一个：你只告诉模型「做什么」，从来不告诉它「怎么判断」！！

这 6 个 Prompt 直接抄👇

1，状态机猎手：
揪出隐式状态机（大部分 bug 的根子），同时兼顾 UX / DX / AX 且不改坏东西。
Find all of the implicit state machines in my app. Make the best decision that will elevate all three: the user experience (UX), developer experience (DX), and agent experience (AX) always, without breaking anything.

2，开源侦察兵：
不熟的功能别从零写，先搜 GitHub 对比现成方案再动手，最省 token。
Don't write an unfamiliar feature from scratch. Search GitHub for open-source projects, compare their approaches, then start.

3，Bug 分诊员：
按「频率 × 严重度」打分，乘积 <5 只开 issue 不动代码（阈值按项目调），别给罕见场景瞎设计。
Rate each bug from 1 to 10 on how often it would happen and how bad it would be. If the two scores multiplied are below 5, just file it as an issue and leave the code alone. Do not design for rare or future cases nobody asked about.

4，收尾人：
专治干一半问「要不要继续」——活干完再停，删东西先问，最后用人话总结重点。
Finish the whole job before you stop. Don't offer to continue: continue. Ask me before you delete anything. End with a recap for someone who saw none of the work: key points first, plain words.

5，CI 审计员：
用 gh 拉最近 150 次运行，按「排队 / 环境准备 / 实际任务」拆出最慢的 5 个 job，先出报告不动代码。
Audit this repo's CI: Use gh to pull the last 150 CI runs and split each job's time into three parts: waiting in the queue for a machine, setup (checkout, installing dependencies, restoring the cache), and actually running the task. List the 5 slowest jobs and how many seconds each part takes. Give me the report first. Don't change anything.

6，重建者：
最好的架构 review——如果今天推倒重来，哪些还得留？留下的才是资产，其余全是包袱。
If you were starting over today with the same goal, what would you still need to keep?

把「执行」交给 AI 不稀奇，逼它先做「判断」才是这代模型该有的用法！！

先 mark，下次直接抄👇

quoted_text:
强烈建议会VibeCoding 的父母试着亲手给孩子做一份生日礼物！！

做起来不费力，孩子又喜欢！！

最近在琢磨给小侄子准备什么生日礼物
看他平常总是自己拿着手机玩，就想做个炫酷一点的东西，让他愿意玩，又能顺便学点东西。

本来想搓个小游戏，但是想了一下，这不是让他更想玩游戏了吗😂

后来想起，之前朋友ban 总的孩子收到过一本立体书
翻开一页，里面的场景就立了起来，小家伙看得特别新奇。

那我能不能自己做一本，还让里面的东西动起来、发出声音？
内容就选古诗，古诗里本来就有好多风景，正好一首诗做一个小世界。

这次我就用千问Qwen4-Max正式版，把这个想法重新做了一遍。
选了望庐山瀑布、江雪、小池和山行这四首。

VibeCoding 我有个心得：8 分自动做，2 分人力调整！！

8分自动做，就是把参考交代清楚，让千问这种能长程运行的模型自己研究、动手。

这次最难的是翻页时，里面的山水要跟着弹出来，合上又能收回去。

我先用 Codex 生成一些图片，大概符合我的想象！！
然后，我给它的提示词是：去网上参考一些项目，读代码、学原理，再录视频对照着改，做到至少有别人八分顺畅为止。
交代完，我就出去运动了，让它自己接着迭代。

2分人力调整，就是我来挑效果、提意见：

翻页搞定后，再调画面和声音。让它把候选和实际效果整理成HTML，我看完再选，不满意就继续改。
直到最后配上古诗朗诵，再加上流水、风吹树叶的声音，才觉得这本书终于有感觉了！
翻开能看诗里的山水，点一下能听朗诵，旁边的诗句还会跟着逐字高亮。

这份礼物总算拿得出手了，既有好玩的东西，也能让他跟着学古诗。

text:
有美股医药板块持仓的a16z这篇深度研究推荐看看，尤其是AI带来的商业变化部分

Big Pharma Can Rival Big Software 
大型制药公司可以与大型软件公司匹敌

制药业规模已可与软件业比肩，且潜力更大：
-全球前30大药企市值合计约5万亿美元；9家药企市值超2000亿美元（对比软件业16家）。
-礼来（Eli Lilly）市值已超1万亿美元，主要靠GLP-1类药物（如替尔泊肽/Mounjaro、Zepbound）。2026年Q3其GLP-1组合收入接近170亿美元，几乎追上Anthropic同期收入；分析师预计2030年该组合年销售额超1000亿美元。
-全球有300+种“重磅药物”（年销售额超10亿美元）。单款成功药物年收入可媲美大型软件公司（如礼来注射型GLP-1 2025年近400亿美元，接近Salesforce全年收入）。

制药经济的双重性：热门生意 + 年金生意：
-热门生意：收入高度集中，呈幂律分布。前25%药物贡献约85%收入；前10大药企约50%收入来自前三大资产（礼来63%来自GLP组合，默克54%来自Keytruda）。

-年金生意：专利保护通常带来上市后10-14年独占期。成功药物可长期产生高现金流（如Dupixent从2017年上市到2025年近180亿美元，且适应症持续扩展）。

-新药创造价值主要靠“首创”（First-in-class，全新机制）和“同类最佳”（Best-in-class，更优疗效/安全性/便利性）。肿瘤学、代谢疾病（含GLP-1）、免疫学是最大治疗领域。生物制剂与小分子药物收入大致对半。

AI如何改变药物经济学（核心论点）：
-传统研发成本高、耗时长、成功率低：摊销失败成本后，开发一款药的现值成本接近20亿美元，平均13年；进入人体试验后最终获批率<10%，候选药到获批<5%。FDA每年仅批准约40-50种新药，大型药企约2/3新药来自外部收购/许可。

-AI主要通过两招降低风险调整后成本：
-提高成功概率（更好靶点识别、分子设计、预测模型）。
-缩短获批时间（文献推理、试验设计、患者招募、文件起草等）。

-进入“药物候选丰富时代”（Formation Bio观点）。湿实验室、CRO、数据与自动化需求将大增。科学AI模型快速进步，能识别新靶点、设计更安全/更强效/更创新的分子。

估值与商业模式转变：
目前药企估值主要基于成熟/已批准药物的DCF（通常8-20倍市盈率，对应3-7倍收入），研发引擎几乎不被“计入估值”。
如果AI让药物发现更可重复，投资者会开始给“发现引擎”更高估值信用，类似科技公司平台估值。药企可减少对单一爆款依赖，更持续地补充专利悬崖后的收入。
机会两类公司：向药企/AI实验室卖数据、技术、软件的公司；以及垂直整合、自己开发药物的AI原生治疗公司。

对人类更大的意义：
许多疾病仍未被充分理解或治疗。AI有望加速解决这些问题，扩大可治疗疾病范围，而不仅是做更大的爆款药。

总体判断：制药业已是超大生意，AI同时提升成功率、压缩时间和成本，将让它变得更大，并催生新一代公司与估值逻辑变化。文章基于a16z长期在技术与生物交叉领域的投资观察（自2015年起投过insitro、Formation Bio、BigHat Bio等）。

text:
SK hynix's revenue from Nvidia roughly doubled to $24B in the first nine months of 2026.

you'd think that makes Hynix an Nvidia trade. but Nvidia accounts for only ~15% of its revenue.

the bigger concentration risk is elsewhere. over 60% of Hynix's sales go to US customers. Nvidia is just one of them.

Google is another. Hynix is the first HBM3E supplier for Google's v7 TPUs.

and there's something else investors should understand.

“Sold out through 2029” doesn't mean everything is under contract.

signed long-term agreements cover just over half of Hynix's 2027–28 capacity. the rest is still being negotiated.

HBM isn't interchangeable inventory anymore. it's increasingly customized for each customer. if Nvidia cuts orders, Hynix can't simply redirect those chips to Google next week.

there have already been reports of Nvidia cutting HBM4 orders by 20–30% versus plan. Hynix says those adjustments are accounted for and its shipment plans remain unchanged.

I asked @tessara_ai to investigate the full picture - the evidence and sources it finds helps form my judgement. and i can review them directly without searching myself

text:
Jensen被迫辞职 CEO，很多人想要抄底。我觉得，还是谨慎点，因为我认为，这并不是利空出尽，而是英伟达噩梦的开始。
为什么呢？因为老黄不当 CEO，英伟达面临的是个死局，一共 5 点：
1）竞争：AI 芯片七八成的份额、75% 的毛利率，最大的客户同时是最大的对手。他在的时候，份额就已经在慢慢往下走了。老黄在，尚能延缓下降趋势，一旦离开，英伟达的市场份额大概率会快速下降。
2）组织：之前，大约 60 个人直接向老黄直接汇报，这套打法是按他一个人的脑容量设计的，换谁都接不住。接不住就要加层级，组织动荡和内耗难以避免。
3）供应链：老黄跟台积电，三星电子，海力士这种关键供应商的交情，是30年一点一点攒出来的，这根本无法交接。
4）战略：2006 年，老黄坚持搞 CUDA，才成就了现在的英伟达。而扶持新的云厂商、支持开源模型，这两个跟 CUDA 同等重要，也同等短期吃力不讨好的事，没有老黄，大概率不会坚持。
5）技术：英伟达能保持一年一代的更新节奏，是老黄带着团队和供应链往前跑。没有老黄，半导体的进步速度会减慢，整个 AI 行业的发展速度都会减慢。

虽然有人在传，老黄会回来，但我觉得很难，因为这是个 1 年前就开始布的大局，而布这个局的势力，非同小可。详细分析，请见视频。

In my ongoing quest to find the limits of Opus 5.5, I directed it to audit my old scientific field, theoretical astrophysics. We indexed about 150,000 papers, audited 50,000 for issues, and did progressively more thorough checks on thousands more. We found nearly 1000 major errors that got cited many times, most are still uncorrected. This survey enabled me to estimate the efficacy of peer review for correcting errors (not very good) and to identify dozens of open questions that anyone with spare Claude Max tokens could answer today (.md context files included). 

Bottom line: AI can speed up quantitative science by >1000x with no further model improvement required. But I'm seeing no evidence of this being pushed within universities, only academics complaining about labs dropping math proofs. 

Among my fellow reformed academic high agency founders, however, several are speed running entire disciplines.

This survey has implications for how science will be run in the very near future. Hint: Academic publishing is dead. It was already a very stupid way to record and promulgate knowledge, and had been so for decades, even before all that publicly funded knowledge was locked behind paywall cartels. Now AIs can generate thousands of novel, correct papers per day, it is no longer meaningful for humans to consider a research paper a "unit of science" or to even bother much with the 99.9% of science which, up to this point, was necessary drudgery. Time to discover something like General Relativity or Evolution every week. LFG!!

text:
德鲁肯米勒最新13F：AI产业利润的重新分配

11月16日，德鲁肯米勒（Stanley Druckenmiller）旗下Duquesne Family Office公布了2026年Q3持仓，13F申报总市值为44.71亿美元，环比下降14.2%，持仓数量从95项减少至65项。

结合最近几个季度的持仓变化、他今年的公开采访，以及11月份的美股行情，我认为他的投资思路正在发生一些比较重要的变化。

1. 生物科技可能成为下一轮市场的主线

很多人关注德鲁肯米勒的半导体持仓，却忽略了生物医药已经成为他最大的配置方向，占13F申报市值的四成左右。

第一大重仓股是癌症及基因检测公司Natera（$NTRA），持仓市值13.06亿美元，占比从上季度的16.6%上升至29.2%。不过，这期间他的持仓股数实际减少了0.8%，权重提升主要来自股价上涨和其他仓位的收缩。

此外，他还持有大量生物科技公司，包括：

$INSM：罕见病治疗
$RVMD：RAS靶向抗癌药
$NAMS：心血管疾病创新药
$BEAM：基因碱基编辑
$RLAY：精准药物研发

今年3月，德鲁肯米勒在接受摩根士丹利采访时，解释了自己投资生物科技的几个原因：

一是生物科技经历了数年的低迷，存在市场领导板块切换的机会；二是行业的技术面和价格动量正在发生变化；三是生物科技可能是AI最具潜力的应用场景之一，尤其是药物研发、疾病诊断和持续监测。

这笔交易值得重视的地方，在于将产业技术变革、行业周期和市场资金轮动结合起来。

未来可以重点观察生物科技ETF（$XBI）相对于纳斯达克100（$QQQ）的走势。

2. 减持AI算力，加仓HDD

Q3德鲁肯米勒对半导体进行了大幅调仓：

清仓AMD、Sandisk、Google。
减持94.5%的台积电、47.9%的意法半导体。
增持180.2%的希捷科技（$STX）。
新建仓希捷看涨期权及西部数据（$WDC）。

两家HDD厂商合计占其13F申报市值的9.9%（含期权对应标的市值）。

尤其值得注意的是，他清仓了做NAND的Sandisk，同时买入了做HDD的西部数据。

相比其他半导体细分赛道，HDD具有行业竞争格局高度集中、资本开支相对克制、供给弹性有限等特点。随着AI生成的数据量不断增长，海量数据的长期存储需求，有望转化为HDD厂商的定价能力、利润率和自由现金流增长。

希捷10月底公布的财报也部分验证了这一逻辑，单季度自由现金流达到14.79亿美元，创历史新高。

不过，随着AI数据中心融资环境恶化，HDD未来的需求增长也存在被下修的风险。

3. 从AI基础设施向AI应用进行切换

Q3德鲁肯米勒大幅增加了部分AI应用公司的配置：

增持435.5%的Unity（$U）。
增持42.7%的亚马逊（$AMZN）。
新建仓AppLovin（$APP）。
新建仓Palantir（$PLTR）。

其中Unity和AppLovin这组交易尤其值得关注，两家公司都能通过AI算法提高广告投放效率，并将技术进步直接转化为收入和利润。

最新财报显示，Unity的AI广告平台Vector收入同比增长126%，AppLovin营收同比增长55%，净利润增长72%。

过去几年，AI产业的超额利润主要集中在上游算力厂商。但随着模型能力提升、推理成本下降以及竞争加剧，超额利润可能逐渐向具有用户、数据和商业化优势的下游应用公司转移。

相比需要投入巨额资本开支的云厂商，部分AI应用公司具有更好的资本回报率和利润增长潜力。

4. 宏观层面：警惕资本稀缺和AI融资风险

9月10日，据《金融时报》报道，德鲁肯米勒认为，考虑到美国经济、资本开支热潮以及对资本的争夺，即便当时美债收益率已经明显上升，利率可能依然偏低。

据11月16日《华尔街日报》报道，德鲁肯米勒近期与Paul Tudor Jones在一场闭门会议上就AI泡沫展开辩论。

他表达了几个重要观点：

AI是历史上规模最大的技术变革之一。
其家族办公室已经削减AI相关投资敞口。
英伟达目前正在获取超常水平的利润（overearning），未来利润率可能下降，竞争对手也会获得更多市场份额。
资本市场未必愿意为计划中的大规模AI数据中心建设提供足够资金。

最后一点尤其重要。

美国政府财政赤字、Hyperscaler资本开支、Neocloud债务融资，都在争夺有限的资本。资本成本的上升，可能成为制约下一阶段AI发展的重要因素。

此外，德鲁肯米勒在Q3退出了多项宽基指数看涨期权，并同时新建仓三大黄金矿业公司Newmont（$NEM）、Barrick（$B）和Agnico Eagle（$AEM）。

结合他此前长期看空美元、担忧美国财政可持续性的观点，这部分配置也具有一定的宏观交易属性。

5. 结合近期行情，推测他四季度做了什么？

如果按照9月30日披露的持仓静态计算，截至11月16日，德鲁肯米勒的正股组合累计下跌约15.3%，其中两大核心重仓Natera和希捷科技分别下跌约30%和46%。

相比之下，Unity和AppLovin分别上涨约27%和43%。

与此同时，美国10年期国债收益率突破5%，AI基础设施企业的信用风险显著上升。

结合他的近期发言及一贯灵活的交易风格，我推测他在四季度可能进行了以下调整：

一是进一步削减AI硬件敞口，特别是对数据中心建设速度高度敏感的公司；二是降低部分重仓股的集中度；三是保留部分AI应用和生物科技公司的配置；四是通过现金、短期国债或宏观对冲降低组合整体风险。

至于加密货币，虽然他在10月29日公开确认投资了Trade[XYZ]，但其Q3加密相关上市公司持仓市值实际上环比下降了约13%。目前没有充分证据表明他正在增加加密资产的方向性多头敞口。

总结

我认为，德鲁肯米勒当前的投资主线，可以归纳为四个方向：

生物科技的行业复苏与技术变革。
AI产业链内部的利润重新分配。
具有供给约束和定价能力的细分行业。
资本成本上升背景下的宏观风险管理。

过去三年，AI投资最重要的变量是需求增长。未来三年，竞争格局、资本成本、自由现金流和投资回报率可能变得更加重要。

即使AI产业继续高速发展，产业增长与股东回报之间也可能出现显著分化。

注：13F持仓截至9月30日，组合收益为不含期权、股息及期间调仓的静态模拟，四季度交易方向为个人推测。

text:
Patriot Act for AI is coming.

They are going to try to lock down AI from every angle, and keep the best AI capabilities restricted to those on the right lists.

Don’t let it happen. Speak out.

Yes, there are cyber attacks happening everywhere, but it’s temporary.

Engineers and cybersecurity firms have never had more powerful cyber defense tools than they do now.

While bugs are getting exploited, hundreds more are getting found and patched before anyone attacks.

AI is favoring the defense. But the decades of pre-AI code needs to be patched up. This takes time.

I am confident because crypto saw a huge wave of bugs and attacks earlier this year.

Turns out public money systems are the easiest profitable target to attack first.

It was a grueling 4 months or so. Dozens of new bugs discovered daily. DeFi protocols getting hacked daily. Critical patches getting rolled out regularly.

But eventually the dust settled. The teams that were proactive and used AI tools well, managed to patch everything up before attackers get to them.

Of course bugs still get discovered today, but not at the insane pace earlier this year. And the bugs being found are more complex to exploit, which makes them hard to use.

The attack surface for crypto got well hardened by the cyber defenders, and while there is always a threat, hell stopped raining down.

So there is a light at the end of the tunnel.

The rest of the world will harden their software until there’s no more gaps to sneak into.

It’s tumultuous now, but it will end in everything being more secure.

Don’t like them take your rights in the process.

Don’t let the fear give in to invasive government overreach.

Don’t let them steal your right to run code and use AI.

Fear is the enemy, not AI.
