author: TheStalwart
quoted_text:
Just read a Chinese article calling this "the darkest moment for Chinese AI." Seeing pushback in the comments, but basically it lays out the bear case quite extensively:

1. Getting compute is harder whichever way you go. Buying advanced NVIDIA chips is difficult, renting GPUs overseas is coming under pressure, and proposed restrictions on chipmaking equipment could make domestic alternatives harder to produce too.

2. Catching up could get a lot more expensive. If learning from leading models’ outputs aka distillaion becomes harder, Chinese labs have to spend more on their own data, experiments and training. That gets uncomfortable if investors are also losing patience. Independent labs don’t have an advertising or e-commerce business to pay the bills.

3. Robot-brain startups could find their advantage disappearing. Frontier labs are moving into robotics, potentially eating into what specialist models can offer. Meanwhile, robots still have to make economic sense against China’s relatively low labor costs.

4. More users don’t necessarily mean enough revenue. China has huge digital audiences, but getting people and businesses to pay sustainably for AI is another question. Everyone is competing on price, American models are getting cheaper too, and research isn’t getting cheaper.

5. Even the areas where China already leads face risks. Optical-component suppliers are benefiting from AI infrastructure spending, but proposed US restrictions could threaten access to major customers.

That’s a lot hitting at once. The worry is that companies keep making better models while needing more money to stay competitive, without earning enough to fund the next round.

Now, it feels like every six months it is a "darkest moment" for Chinese AI. But I think these are real concerns. We'll focus on this topic at @techbuzzchina (and present some hope, I think) next week.

quoted_text:
【说下circle和usdc的真实体感和投资价值】
身边很多深圳工作室老板朋友和大户都在定投 Circle，感觉多少都受了某饭影响。一个细小圈子很容易形成信息茧房。某一拨人靠类似的事情成功，就总想在别的领域复制：
1， 比如自己判断 BTC 四年周期做得成功，就把很大一部分仓位拿去玩美股
2，比如过去牛市里 MSTR 相对 BTC 有 Alpha，就线性推演未来Circle 相对 BTC 也有 Alpha

但我是真的在做加密支付，感受是USDC 在支付领域的真实 adoption，被圈内人严重高估了，虽然我不喜欢孙哥，但TRON的基本面好太多了。

几个关于稳定币支付的事实，大家可以去 check：

第一，现在推特上发言的加密 KOL 和用户，大多不是加密支付的主流群体。我们是稳定币的投资群体，不是消费群体。这些人会翻墙，也关注各种主流金融形式，手上都有信用卡。但凡有信用卡的人，基本不会用 U 付款，因为信用卡永远比 U 卡方便。

第二，整个加密 Web3 的支付机构，相比传统 PSP，有一个天然缺点，且没有传统 PSP 那种商户网络，他们作为稳定币兑法币的最后一站，可替代性非常强，而。这一点非常致命。最终形态大概率是成为传统支付商基建里的一环，而不是从后端去主宰、重塑整个行业链条。

第三，真正用稳定币支付的人，大部分在东南亚小国、非洲或南美。用户画像就两类：弱主权货币国家的小镇青年，以及灰产。他们往往只有钱包，可能没有交易所，大概率只认识TRON，基本上不持有metamask这类 EVM 钱包。

第四，关于usdc说几个反常识的数据。波场上流通的 USDT 大约 920 亿，以太坊大约 668 亿，波场多一些但你要明白tron上钱是以支付转账主导的，eth上是以defi投资生态主导的。从支付角度看，两者差距要大得多大得：2026 年，波场占稳定币支付金额约 66.6%，以太坊主网只有约 6.6%，差了 10 倍。即便把以太坊和它的 EVM 二层加在一起，也就十几个点，还是远被波场吊打。同期 USDT 贡献了约 84% 的支付金额，USDC 只有约 12%。

所以 USDC 在整个支付里的采用率，其实非常非常非常低。再加上波场的节点和商户深度绑定，它并不是短期内 L2 费用降低就能被取代的生态。波场现在比很多L2转账还贵，但大家仍然在用波场，不会换别的链。

基于这些，我对 USDC 作为稳定币支付基建、以及它的真实增长，是持保留态度的。

你说它会不会像 MSTR 一样，在牛市里相对 BTC 有 Alpha——牛市可能不看基本面，山寨起飞——那是另外一说，我不知道，一切皆有可能。

但如果你靠着 Circle 基本面给自己洗脑、动不动就 All in，来推导它会发展得很好，我并不认可。单从现在我对支付行业的体感，从基本面看，我觉得tron比 Circle 更牛逼。

我的感受是稳定币支付的底层是灰产，再说一遍，稳定币支付的底层是灰产

text:
Anthropic 明天定价，普通人看 IPO，先看懂这三个数

明天 11 月 18 日，Anthropic 敲定 IPO 价格，后天 11 月 19 日在纳斯达克挂牌，代码 ANT。数字很多，先看三个。

第一个数是价格区间：每股 70 到 78 美元，发行 8.25 亿股，募资最高约 644 亿美元。定价落在区间哪头，是市场给的第一张表态。

第二个数是估值：按区间算，公司估值约 1.26 万亿到 1.41 万亿美元。这个数比夏天市场预期的 2 万亿美元低了一截。估值缩水不等于便宜，也不等于捡漏，意思只是市场给的锚变了。

第三个数是散户配额：最高 20%。这个比例远高于一般 IPO 的散户份额，普通人能不能分到、能分到多少，就看这一条怎么落。

还有一个数值得顺带记下：招股书里写着，到 2045 年公司签下的算力承诺约 9000 亿美元，其中 2027 年到期的就有 290 亿美元。第三季度营收 170 亿美元，同比增了 11 倍多，但花钱的速度也在同步放大。

定价要是落在区间上沿，你觉得是强，还是贵？

author: leto_bao
quoted_text:
11 月 9 日，我做多了英伟达。

理由很简单：当时能决定黄仁勋去留的人都在保他。董事会说信任，特朗普说他该留任。

两天后，这两个理由都靠不住了。

今天早上我把整件事从头复盘了一遍，结论是：这不是两周的事，引线埋了四年。

2022 年美国出台首轮对华 AI 芯片禁令，黄仁勋的应对主要是商业上的：推出降规版芯片接着卖，嘴上批评管制，但没有亲自下场游说白宫。

2024 年初他认识了黄乐。2025 年起，他开始高调游说华盛顿，多次面见特朗普，结果是 H20 和 H200 先后放行。中国的大模型也从这时候开始快速缩短与美国模型的距离。美国情报部门的备忘录认为，推动英伟达游说正是黄乐的任务之一。

放行惹怒了两党的对华鹰派。与此同时，情报部门在调查 Megaspeed 时发现了两人的关系。2025 年 10 月和 2026 年 5 月，特朗普两次听取汇报，都没有动作，5 月还带着黄仁勋去了北京。10 月 6 日，英伟达收于 239.24 美元，创历史新高。

内部渠道走不通，就只剩媒体。10 月 29 日《纽约时报》首次曝光，11 月 8 日黄仁勋承认出轨。

11 月 9 日我的判断是：间谍这条线已经摊开，董事会和白宫都公开力挺，最坏的消息出完了，这事算翻篇。

结果今天早上第二轮报道出来：《纽约时报》称他与一名直接下属有染，《华尔街日报》称董事会准备罢免他。两条都是匿名信源，公司还没确认。这是我完全没预想到的黑天鹅。第一段关系是国家安全问题，白宫可以保；第二段是公司治理问题，董事会很难再保。

董事会不算黄仁勋本人有 10 人。按我的推测，保黄派只有 3 位元老，倒黄派有 5 人，另外 2 人摇摆，过半只需要 6 票。倒黄派里有 4 位持股很少，罢免带来的股价下跌对他们几乎没有影响，不罢免反而可能被股东追责。所以我认为罢免大概率会通过。没有黄仁勋的英伟达，估值要大打折扣，分析师估计还要再跌 25% 到 30%。

不管今晚结果如何，我都会在开盘后平掉全部 $NVDA 期权。即使罢免没通过，放料的人手里可能还有东西，短期看不清。

往后看，对华鹰派很可能成为华盛顿的主流。一直对华发疯的 Anthropic 会是 AI 板块里最大的赢家。

text:
There was a man who gave away $10,000,000 on Twitter because he wanted to see if money would make them happier 

His name was Yusaku Maezawa, Japanese billionaire, Ex punk drummer

That's why his handle is @yousuck2020 and the account has 9 million followers.

He was behind the biggest X giveaway (twice) :

For some context we go back to 1991.

He starts a hardcore punk band called Switch Style with his high school friends.

After school he skips college and follows his girlfriend to the US.

He starts collecting records you can't find in Japan.

1995.

He comes back and starts selling those records by mail. Directly from his house.

1998.

He turns it into a company and names it after a Gorilla Biscuits album: Start Today.

The same year his band signs with BMG Japan.

2004.

Start Today launches Zozotown.

It becomes Japan's biggest online fashion store.

2016.

He pays $57.3 MILLION for a Basquiat. Record.

2017.

He breaks his own record.

$110.5 MILLION for another Basquiat, bidding by phone from his home in Tokyo.

The most expensive work by an American artist ever sold at auction.

January 2019.

He tweets that he'll give ¥1,000,000 to 100 random people who retweet him.

5,455,411 RETWEETS.

Guinness World Record. The most reposted post in the history of the platform.

Yes, even today.

September 2019.

He sells control of Zozo to Yahoo Japan in a $3.7 BILLION deal.

Walks away with ~$2.3 BILLION and steps down as CEO.

January 1, 2020.

He does it again. Bigger.

¥1 BILLION. 1,000 people. ¥1,000,000 each.

About $9,000 per person.

All you had to do was follow and retweet.

4.1 MILLION retweets in a week.

He calls it "a serious social experiment" to test basic income.

But after that he started a beef with Meta for years

Back in 2024 scammers have been using his face in fake investment ads on Facebook and Instagram for a year.

He sues Meta and asks for ¥1 in damages.

Just one yen.

November 10, 2026.

A Tokyo court dismisses his case against Meta.

Curiously the man who handed ¥1,000,000 to 1,100 strangers couldn't get ¥1 out of Meta.

I'm still short, but looking for a spot to cover and take profits, possibly sooner than later. 

Why? 

Because an impending push up is growing likely.

Based on history, the current bull market is long in the tooth; the fifth longest on record. However, since 1950 the S&P 500 has never declined in the year after mid-terms elections. The average S&P 500 gain in pre-election years is 17.2%. What is noteworthy is: most of the gains have come in the first half of pre-election years. The S&P 500 has been flat-to-down in the second half (see chart).

We are heading into a period with multiple bullish tendencies working in the market’s favor. Year-end seasonality is one.  The historically strong first half of the Presidential cycle is another (see charts).

If we can get through this period without the Fed moving into a fast tightening cycle, those tailwinds should remain intact. Under that scenario, I would expect the current correction to be relatively short-lived and ultimately give way to a resumption of the broader uptrend.

Could we bottom soon?

There is an interesting historical precedent worth keeping in mind as we approach Thursday's scheduled meeting between the U.S., Russia and China. Going back to some of the most significant meetings between the world's major powers, the stock market was higher following nearly every one of them—sometimes substantially higher.

In 1945, Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin met at Yalta. Stocks rallied immediately following the meeting and continued higher over the next several weeks.

In 1972, Nixon's historic meeting with Mao in China was also followed by a rising market and new highs in the weeks that followed.

The Reagan-Gorbachev summits show a similar pattern. Following Geneva in November 1985, stocks moved higher.

Reykjavik in October 1986 actually ended without an agreement, yet the market shrugged off the disappointment and gained roughly 5% over the next three weeks.

Following the Washington summit in December 1987, where Reagan and Gorbachev signed the INF Treaty, the market rallied sharply, gaining roughly 7% within a week and continuing higher.

After their Moscow summit in 1988, stocks again rallied strongly, gaining roughly 7% over the next couple of weeks and close to 10% within a month.

Obviously, this is a small sample and every period had a different economic and market backdrop. But the pattern is noteworthy: these major superpower meetings were generally followed by higher stock prices over the ensuing days and weeks.

That matters to us because we're currently short the S&P 500 and sitting on a profitable trade. If the market gives us additional downside going into Thursday, I will likely use that weakness to cover some or potentially all of our short exposure ahead of the meeting.

There's enough historical precedent for a positive reaction that I don't see a reason to overstay a profitable short going into the event. 

I have not made the decision to cover my shorts just yet, but a decline from here could be just the opportunity to cover right into weakness at peak equity.

text:
我买 CRCL，买的其实不是稳定币支付。

这两天看到 Phyrex 和 Andy 都聊了 Circle，一个说稳定币支付挑战不了信用卡体系，一个说 USDC 在稳定币支付里只占 12% 左右，我觉得从基本面来说，是有一定道理的。

但是我的思考是，一个资产的价格往往会脱离基本面，像钟摆一样，有时候低于基本面，有时候高于基本面。

基本面好不一定意味着价格好，基本面不好也不一定证明价格不好。茅台的基本面很好，但是价格不是很好，曾经的 meme 币没啥基本面，却产生了无数财富故事。

其实只看基本面的话，我自己也不乐观。Q3 财报 USDC 平均流通量涨了 8%，储备收益反而降了 8%，然后最近整个稳定币市值都在缩水，从 5 月高点的 3155 亿刀掉到 11 月初的 2923 亿刀，不是 USDC 一家在缩。你说 USDC 以后真的能覆盖很多国家的稳定币支付吗，我觉得也不见得。

所以我买 CRCL 最核心的逻辑不在这里——我赌的是「加密流动性回归」的时候，会有一部分流动性蔓延到 CRCL，这部分流动性带来的溢价，会让价格涨上去。

我相信 BTC 回到 12 万只是时间的问题，这个我是非常有信心的。今天 BTC 6.5 万，回到 12 万是 85% 左右，接近一倍。

而 BTC 回到 12 万的时候，我觉得 CRCL 的涨幅可能不止一倍。上一次 BTC 站上 12 万是 2025 年 10 月，那时候 CRCL 在 130 到 150 之间，我相信下一次 BTC 到 12 万的时候，他的价格不止和上次一样，而今天是 56 多。

我的逻辑是，流动性回来的时候，会印更多的稳定币，会有更多的套利机会，即便 USDC 的基本面没有变得多好，情绪回来的时候，大概率也会把价格拉出合理估值的区间。

所以 CRCL 对我来说，更像是「加了杠杆的加密 beta」。我自己也没想过要拿多久、拿多少倍，我的思考是，只要 BTC 到了相对高点，CRCL 就可以去止盈了，最终是多少倍，我不知道。

这个逻辑我是用真金白银去下注的，最近两笔是 68 和 66 买的，现在是浮亏的。屁股可能决定脑袋，大家参考就好。

稳定币业务什么时候能做起来我不知道，我只是相信，加密流动性会回归。具体结果怎么样，等 BTC 突破 12 万的时候我们再看吧。

quoted_text:
Indian law enforcement froze $3M from an innocent Chinese investor after mistaking a crypto bridge for a pig butchering scam. Now an Indian court has ordered Gate to hand his funds to a person they never belonged to.

My analysis of how Indian LE traced through an unlabeled service and wrongly froze @xxxkeym's Gate account:

The case stems from a pig butchering victim who allegedly lost $1.7M of BTC, USDT, DOGE & SOL in May 2025.

Andhra Pradesh CID registered it as Cr. No. 10/2025 and filed a charge sheet in March 2026.

In July 2025, xxxkeym had Gate deposit address 17mpajZ6Nq3dG3T6wUhaXxYF4Qy9HJnYx5 frozen after depositing 15 BTC from 3NcBhqK in the following transaction:
885f3afab562251b222363cf12095e864ddb94636674b01f0cdb05997e5a54a0

This is one transaction Indian LE cites in its notice. 3NcBhqK was funded by xxxkeym's own OKX & Binance withdrawals in Jan 2023 and the coins sat dormant for years until the Gate deposit. 

Indian LE never froze his OKX or Binance accounts, the actual source of the 15 BTC, which tells you how flawed their justification is.

Gate froze his entire account, which held roughly $3M at the time and about $1.5M today.

The Indian court order hands all of it to the complainant.

Gate deposit address 17mpajZ also received two deposits for 15 BTC total in 2025 from bc1pkkwqyxn3rm608ryuqg9hyqna0syq4jx5pxkr7pzg8n3usx6tyqfst5u966, which is also controlled by xxxkeym.

Shortly before the deposits to Gate, bc1pkkw was funded in three transactions by bc1quzwkggdf6ly06mrrnnled0qdr57w770k45n5n7 & bc1qtu66zfqxj6pam6e0zunwnggh87f5pjr7vdr5cd.

bc1quzw & bc1qtu66z were reported as alibarbit[.]bit, the same scam named in Indian LE's press release. 

That was a mistake. Both belong to the Merlin Chain bridge, which is unlabeled in most compliance tools. 

xxxkeym is simply a normal Merlin user trading tokens on the L2. This wrong label is the only place the scam touches his transaction history.

Below is the blockchain data showing each Merlin withdrawal by xxxkeym matched to a BTC payout from those addresses, plus screenshots of the bridge activity.

xxxkeym bridged 50 BTC into Merlin on March 28, 2024, over a year before the alleged May 2025 theft. 

His three withdrawals came out of that balance. I found zero onchain connections between xxxkeym and the theft.

text:
今天特别开心@yaojingang 老师来我们公司交流，他分享了国内GEO行业的一些深度洞见：

1. 当前国内入局GEO的一些企业主要有：央媒、地方媒体、大厂、创业公司、各类模型厂商都以不同形式入局了，现在整体市场活跃度还是很高，但大量入局者都缺乏项目承接能力，普遍存在较强的合作需求。

2. GEO行业还比较新，现在算是爆发期，百家争鸣的状态，国内GEO相关的服务商总规模大约有数千家，包含外包服务商、私有化部署产品提供商、本地生活服务商等不同类型。

3. 目前行业也面临很多问题：比如行业还没有形成统一的效果评估标准，也没有出现具备公信力的第三方监测机构，行业通用的KPI体系都五花八门，不清晰，只能参考曝光、排名、舆情等前端指标开展评估。国内GEO业务对官网采用作用的占比仅为20%，远低于海外80%的占比水平。

4. 还有就是效果归因难，GEO业务的商业价值量化难度还是很高，因为一些低搜索量的关键词即使排名靠前，也几乎无法为客户带来实际商业收益，很难算ROI，核心原因是数据链路断裂。

5. 比较佩服金刚的地方是在于：做大会和活动的初心还是保持着创业者的那份纯粹，现在很多大会商业味很浓，很多赞助所以动作都变形了，也做不长久。他自己从4月份才开始做IP分享，也拒绝了很多早期赞助商，现在已经积累出很多行业的知识沉淀和势能，核心就是一直目标笃定的做一件事，很多事情慢慢做、踏实做一定会开花结果。

6. 做IP的价值还是个体最能撬动的杆杠，年轻人最不亏的就是赶快开始做自媒体。就算现在行业形势不好，但对个体来说还是有很多机会，去找到那些小需求点，日常学习迭代，上X吸收再输出，这些动作对长期个人成长都很有价值。

金刚马上要在这周六举办第二届GEO行业大会啦，感兴趣的伙伴们快关注！深圳周末聚起来！

text:
I'm still short, but looking for a spot to cover and take profits, possibly sooner than later. 

Why? 

Because an impending push up is growing likely.

Based on history, the current bull market is long in the tooth; the fifth longest on record. However, since 1950 the S&P 500 has never declined in the year after mid-terms elections. The average S&P 500 gain in pre-election years is 17.2%. What is noteworthy is: most of the gains have come in the first half of pre-election years. The S&P 500 has been flat-to-down in the second half (see chart).

We are heading into a period with multiple bullish tendencies working in the market’s favor. Year-end seasonality is one.  The historically strong first half of the Presidential cycle is another (see charts).

If we can get through this period without the Fed moving into a fast tightening cycle, those tailwinds should remain intact. Under that scenario, I would expect the current correction to be relatively short-lived and ultimately give way to a resumption of the broader uptrend.

Could we bottom soon?

There is an interesting historical precedent worth keeping in mind as we approach Thursday's scheduled meeting between the U.S., Russia and China. Going back to some of the most significant meetings between the world's major powers, the stock market was higher following nearly every one of them—sometimes substantially higher.

In 1945, Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin met at Yalta. Stocks rallied immediately following the meeting and continued higher over the next several weeks.

In 1972, Nixon's historic meeting with Mao in China was also followed by a rising market and new highs in the weeks that followed.

The Reagan-Gorbachev summits show a similar pattern. Following Geneva in November 1985, stocks moved higher.

Reykjavik in October 1986 actually ended without an agreement, yet the market shrugged off the disappointment and gained roughly 5% over the next three weeks.

Following the Washington summit in December 1987, where Reagan and Gorbachev signed the INF Treaty, the market rallied sharply, gaining roughly 7% within a week and continuing higher.

After their Moscow summit in 1988, stocks again rallied strongly, gaining roughly 7% over the next couple of weeks and close to 10% within a month.

Obviously, this is a small sample and every period had a different economic and market backdrop. But the pattern is noteworthy: these major superpower meetings were generally followed by higher stock prices over the ensuing days and weeks.

That matters to us because we're currently short the S&P 500 and sitting on a profitable trade. If the market gives us additional downside going into Thursday, I will likely use that weakness to cover some or potentially all of our short exposure ahead of the meeting.

There's enough historical precedent for a positive reaction that I don't see a reason to overstay a profitable short going into the event. 

I have not made the decision to cover my shorts just yet, but a decline from here could be just the opportunity to cover right into weakness at peak equity.

quoted_text:
A lot of people have been asking what AI companies should actually do if they are serious about pacing the frontier and preventing risks from runaway RSI. 

A clear and extremely important first step is to regularly disclose how much of their compute goes to work that accelerates recursive self-improvement (e.g., AI R&D), and let a third-party auditor verify those disclosures. Governments can and should require these disclosures, but there is no need for companies to wait for them to do so, and there is plenty of reason for them to start immediately voluntarily. 

Below is an outline of the argument for why this proposal for implementing pacing ("verified compute allocation disclosures," or VCAD) makes sense: 

(1) All pacing requires a restraint mechanism. Approaches differ mainly in what, if anything, triggers restraint. Conditional pacing uses a trigger, e.g., “pace until SL4 algorithmic security” or “pace if we can’t make a satisfactory safety case.” Unconditional (or inputs-based - e.g. compute caps) pacing buys time directly, with no trigger. Either way, something has to actually slow development.

(2) Compute reallocation – moving compute from risk-increasing to risk-reducing work – is a good restraint mechanism. The most commonly mentioned alternative to this “compute dial” is a “gate,” e.g., “pause pre-training." (this is true of certain implementations of safety cases) But a gate-only approach creates a software overhang: while the gate is closed, algorithmic and data quality progress continues apace, producing a discontinuous jump when it reopens without necessarily changing the long-term trendline. The overhang is also a security problem: company security is weak, so trailing actors keep accelerating by free-riding on leaked or stolen software progress.

(3) Common standards and verification make it so that companies can make claims that external parties will believe. OpenAI and Anthropic have both claimed to exercise restraint in recent months, but those claims are often met with skepticism. The more companies converge on a common, verified restraint mechanism, the more that commercially costly restraint will be credited by competitors and the public.

(4) Frontier-wide pacing is possible without regulation and without running afoul of antitrust law. Antitrust law prohibits agreements among competitors, not independent decisions. Public demand for restraint is growing and will keep growing as evidence of risk accumulates. A race to the top in response to that demand – built on a common, trusted restraint mechanism – requires no agreement between companies.

(5) Regulation is hopefully coming, and it will almost certainly include a mandated restraint mechanism. A mechanism that has been developed and stress-tested in advance will be more effective than one created at the last minute. 

We should start building a brake pedal before we’re careening down a mountainside. Verified compute allocation disclosures are a very logical place to start. There isn't time to waste! 

(this post is partially inspired by @eli_lifland's recent writeup on verified compute allocation disclosures linked in reply).

✅ 有一本库：出过好片的提示词被拆成一个个镜头块，八种兵器各配一张招式表，好句子拿来就能用，不用从零手写。
✅ 有一道关：写完先过检查，镜头够不够、招式写全没有、有没有踩过以前的坑，不过关就不准出片。

✅ 能接长片：每段都从上一段的最后一帧接着打，打坏的柱子不会在下一段又站起来。
✅ 会自己成长：好的段落收进库，出的问题记进踩坑表，每做一场，下一场都更稳。

Orca、T3 Code 和 Mirasim 三款编程工作台，跨窗口协作怎么做?

我把 Orca、T3 Code 和 Mirasim 这三款编程工作台在日常项目里轮流用了两周。我比较在意一个细节。前后端各开一个会话之后，怎么让它们直接传消息？

Orca 可以用命令行给已有的终端发消息，也有专门的任务协调功能。T3 Code 的项目说明里也写了，Claude 可以把任务交给 Codex。
Mirasim 的做法我用得比较顺手。在前端会话的输入框打个 @，选中已经打开的后端会话，就能直接问「字段改好了吗？」后端收到消息后，可以直接回复前端会话。

在 Mirasim 里，我还能选用自己的 Claude Code 或 Codex 账号，也能切换到 Mirasim 的云端额度。频道里可以请助手接任务，方案也可以接着在内置文档里写。图 3 是频道派任务的示意图。

三款都能用手机查看和继续编程会话。我用 Mirasim 手机端时，也会打开远程桌面，直接操作电脑上的窗口。图 4 是我用到的触控板模式、组合键和画质设置。

如果我只是并排跑几项任务，三款都能用。项目里前后端经常要等彼此回消息时，我更愿意留着 Mirasim，联调时少来回切窗口。

text: An always-loaded rule treats yesterday's choice as today's requirement. Adding more instructions can leave conflicting definitions active together. Retrieval alone can't decide which rule has authority or whether it still applies.

text: Keep reusable rules that still solve a recurring problem. Give each one a scope and someone who can update it. When rules conflict, resolve that before the agent changes the work; when the reason expires, retire the rule.

If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.

Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.

author: TheStalwart
quoted_text:
a revealing and original piece (in CN) by @initiumnews on china’s gender wars, a subject i think is very underreported. 

it follows 23-year-old Lin Wang and Shi Wu, a high-school teacher and manosphere blogger who has spent more than a decade fighting feminism. it offers a revealing look at the mood among china’s young people (male), and how downward mobility and stalled economy shape their grievances and worldview.

a few details from the article:

1. Lin calculates that his parents have invested at least 3 million yuan in raising and educating him. he cannot imagine a job that would let him repay it. eventually, he tells them: i may never earn that money back. no amount of anger from you will change that.

2. men in China are often expected to provide bride-price payments and an apartment before marriage. against a collapsing property market, those expectations can feel like an impossible admission fee to adult life. for many like Lin Wang, marriage also seems like their only way to sex and intimacy, adding sexual frustration to financial resentment.

3. feminism becomes the cause for everything in many men's mental model: unemployment, stalled careers, the inability to form a relationship. grievance is a major sentiment in the anti-feminism camp. 

4. Shi Wu deliberately punished a high school female student for supposedly “provoking a gender war” after she complained online that the boys smelled too sweaty. the classroom split into male and female camps that stopped speaking to each other. 

5. china’s manosphere borrows from western movements such as men going their own way (MGTOW). some chinese-speaking MGTOW adherents developed their own “localized” interpretations. one supporter translated, compiled, and uploaded a 209-page collection of “core MGTOW theory” to a public online repository. Zhihu and baidu tieba are major gathering places for china’s manosphere.

text:
Last week in quantum:

@glassnode reported that 7.12 million BTC have exposed public keys.

That's 35.4% of Bitcoin's issued supply, including 25.8% exposed through address reuse. A sufficiently powerful quantum computer could eventually derive private keys from these exposed public keys, putting those coins at risk.

@Microsoft began rolling out post-quantum TLS for Azure applications.

Azure App Service and Azure Functions are getting hybrid X25519 and ML-KEM-768 key exchange, combining classical and post-quantum protection. The rollout is phased, and compatible applications can use it without code changes.

@IBM announced Nighthawk r3 and plans for a 1,040-qubit system.

The next-generation processor is designed to execute 10,000 quantum operations across 520 programmable qubits. IBM plans to connect two of these processors in 2027, expanding its architecture toward larger quantum computations.

The Internet Architecture Board flagged major challenges in post-quantum authentication.

Its findings from an October workshop identified four obstacles: larger keys and signatures, slow migration of verification systems, the costs of alternative authentication approaches, and conflicting regulatory requirements. These could complicate the transition to quantum-resistant internet infrastructure.

@Cornell researchers demonstrated faster cooling for trapped-ion quantum computers.

Using chip-based laser technology, they reduced a targeted cooling operation from around 500 to 150 microseconds. The technique could help reduce delays in quantum operations, an important requirement for scaling trapped-ion systems.

The US Quantum Primacy Commission called for a stronger national quantum strategy.

Its preliminary report urged the US to move beyond research leadership and invest more in manufacturing, infrastructure, and commercial deployment. It warned that scientific progress alone would not guarantee leadership in quantum technology.

Bitcoin's exposed keys are becoming easier to quantify, while post-quantum protection is starting to reach everyday infrastructure.

author: xingpt
quoted_text:
为什么黄仁勋必须死？

首先我们来看一下，老黄在的时候做了什么、利好了谁。

他最提倡开源，提倡把芯片卖到全球，特别是通过一些灰色渠道流到中国，他是睁一只眼闭一只眼的，甚至可以说是纵容了这种事情发生。

他在位的时候，整个亚洲半导体产业链都吃饱了，特别是台湾的供应商。
所以黄仁勋在位的时期，整个 AI 硬件和半导体的投入增加是极其巨大的。

那为什么他必须“死”呢？

因为美国需要把 AI 的资本开支放缓了，大家实在是没有钱买卡了。
标普全球算过，六家大厂明年 Capex 加起来 1.3 万亿美元，自由现金流还是正的只剩微软一家。高盛估计明年还得发 4000 亿美元的投资级债。这个钱是花不下去的。 
他下台之后会怎么样？
中国的开源模型没办法拿卡了，或者说拿卡跟蒸馏的难度会非常大，跟美国frontier lab的差距会扩大。

美国本土的云厂商也会受益，可以减小 Capex 投入。而且没有中国开源模型在后面追，闭源模型公司也可以放缓买卡和训练，把更多算力放到更高毛利的推理上，不用再拼命赶新模型的进度。

所以未来一年你会看到，新模型发布的节奏一定是迅速放缓的。

另外一方面，整个半导体产业链因为老黄赚得盆满钵满，很多下游产业都在被吸血。消费电子因为服务器跟内存涨价，可以说是深受其害吧。

还有一点跟政治相关。数据中心因为算力竞赛，不断在环保和居民空间上侵害一些人的利益，民主党看到了这个机会，在中期选举上大做文章，把参众两院都拿下了。 

所以你可以看到，老黄下台，对闭源模型大厂有好处，对微软、谷歌、亚马逊、甲骨文这些买卡的大云厂商有好处，对民主党也有好处。

不利的是中国倒卡的二道贩子、中国的开源大模型厂商，还有靠老黄背书才拿得到融资担保的 New Clouds。

但是老黄在台上利好的这些力量，完全没有在美国争取选票的能力和政治影响力。受损的这些大厂，都有极强的背景和游说能力。

所以在 AI 资本开支不得不放缓的时候，老黄必须走，他也必须对此负责。不然大家都会崩盘，整个融资和负债都会出问题。

在 AI 时代要高歌猛进、堆算力的时候，黄仁勋就是那个被捧上神坛的旗手；当 AI 因为投入过大不得不放缓的时候，黄仁勋也会是第一个被推下神坛祭旗的人。

所以老黄必须死。

One of the more profound challenges in America is an outsized number of permastudents, who just put themselves in debt because they believed the fake sales pitch of elite universities...they thought a degree was a magic piece of paper that unlocks some infinite money printer, only to find out it was a total lie.

The University lie was that this somehow trickles down to esoteric degrees like gender studies, which have precisely zero market value in the real world. Even the humanities only functions to serve itself: with a degree in the humanities, you can really only get a job...teaching humanities. 

The best way to build a career as a writer is to write. The best way to build a career as a filmmaker is to film things...if, instead of spending $200K on film studies, you were to buy lights and cameras and a MacBook Pro for editing, you would be light years ahead within 8 months, while the film student languishes in GE class purgatory, only to find themselves suffering further once they get to their major classes 2 years later, and they're being forced to memorize nonsensical esoteric concepts like "syuzhet" and "fabula", and they still haven't touched a camera once.

After suffering through 4 years of overpriced adult daycare, they enter the job market, have no bearings, no market value in the private sector, but because they have a fancy degree, they feel that their pedigree is supposed to automagically confer some advanced level of wealth and status...they should be living in a penthouse apartment in Manhattan, and taking annual ski trips to the dolomites...but the only institution that will take a gender studies graduate is a scammy NPO or a Starbucks. 

They will never evaluate their life choices rationally...most people are incapable of critical self-reflection. Instead, they will continue to feel entitled, and thus angry at "the system" for robbing them of the promise of higher education...so they must dismantle the system because they can't dismantle their own ego. Thus you get...the communist malcontent.  

All the while, the blue collar guy who knows how to plumb a septic system has perpetual real world value, and – as long as he lives within his means – will be permanently content and hold gratitude for his country. In the old days, most people took this route...it was mostly just the doctors and lawyers and engineers and businessmen went to University, and things were balanced. But the propaganda in recent decades from the university system has been so effective, a bunch of people who really ought to be solvent welding PVC pipes are now sacrificing their lives to pay for the inflated costs of elite universities, only to get rug-pulled with a mortarboard and gown.

这两年美股天天创新高，大家FOMO得不行，最近他却一直在喊：水面下全是暗礁，全球债务和财政赤字已经走进了死胡同。

当年2020年3月疫情崩盘，他的全天候基金也挨了一巴掌，但他早早配了黄金和国债，整体上躲过了大跌，并在随后过程中，顺利抄底，赚得盆满钵满。后来他的著作《原则》和《经济机器是如何运行的》，基本成了全球投资人看宏观的入门书。

我把他的核心思路，掰开揉碎了整理一下👇

1️⃣ 经济是一台机器。短期看债务周期和利率，长期看生产力和创新。谁能看清这台机器的齿轮怎么咬合，谁就能在滞胀、通缩、衰退里活下来。

2️⃣ 全天候分散是唯一的免费午餐。你永远不知道明天是通胀、通缩、增长还是衰退。别去赌单一资产，把股票、债券、黄金、商品按风险均衡配好，让机器在任何天气下都能安全运转。

3️⃣ 历史是押韵的，太阳底下无新事。债务危机、帝国兴衰、大周期债务重组，过去几百年里发生过无数次。翻开历史书，就能看到今天的影子。

4️⃣ 彻底的极度求真与极度透明。桥水内部开会可以直接拍桌子对老板吼。好主意不是谁官大听谁的，谁手里有真理、谁能经得起压力测试，就听谁的。

5️⃣ 痛苦 + 反思 = 进步。达里奥破产过，在 80 年代初期差点把公司亏光。那次惨败逼他写下了第一版《原则》。他说，人生最大的成长，来自于直面自己的错误并把它变成算法。

6️⃣ 债务大周期是终极审判。当利率降到零，印钞机开到冒烟，传统货币信誉受损时，黄金和硬资产就是终极避难所。

7️⃣ 分解驱动因素（Alpha & Beta）：别为赚Beta的钱交高额管理费。把资产收益拆解成互不相关的独立回报源，凑够 15 到 20 个，你的胜率就稳了。

8️⃣ 算法化决策。把优秀投资人的大脑变成代码。把你的投资逻辑写成规则和算法，剔除人类情绪在恐慌和贪婪时的干扰。候看资产，不能只看财报，要看地缘政治和供应链重构。

9️⃣ 个人投资者唯一的优势，是时间与客观。散户没有机构强制平仓的压力，只要不被情绪吞没，看清宏观大趋势，拿住跨周期的硬资产，就能熬过所有的周期收割。

🎯 再回到当下，这波AI杀跌为啥应验了他的话？

• 首先美联储在走平衡木，但政府债务增速远超生产力增速，每次市场救市，都是在透支未来信用。

• 其次财政赤字推着国债收益率往上走，高估值资产自然被挤压。

• 最后他对AI的看法也很冷静，AI作为长期是生产力引擎没错，但短期解不了债务问题，也解不了地缘撕裂。

所以满街都在炒AI概念的时候，他盯的是杠杆率、赤字和货币贬值。流动性一收紧，信用成本一抬高，虚胖的资产先挨巴掌，这很正常。

📝 对咱们普通投资者的几点启发：

• 别把鸡蛋全砸在单一成长股或高杠杆赛道。不管玩美股还是加密，都问自己一句：假如市场流动性突然缩紧，我的投资组合扛得住吗？

• 敬畏周期。牛市里人人觉得趋势永远向上，但债务周期到了清算的时候，谁也跑不掉。

• 手里留点真正的硬资产，稀缺、抗通胀的那种，比如黄金和 #BTC 。

最后做一个总结，或许我们可以学一学达里奥，减少盯盘K线的时间，减少去做明天的预测，应该花更多时间去研究经济是如何运转的，地缘政治因素是如何影响大局的，以及经济周期因素下，如何做好全天候分散配置！

美银最新一期FlowShow很值得看看，Hartnett对市场的态度还是很谨慎，为什么他继续坚持Risk-off，什么条件下才会重新转向Risk-on？这也是理解未来几周美股走势的关键。这份报告最值得关注的有几个方面：
1）全球股票基金单周流入983亿美元，究竟是谁在买？
2）美国科技股遭遇大规模抛售，为什么全球科技基金仍然持续吸金？
3）美元、原油、美债收益率和全球流动性之间，正在发生什么变化？
4）标普500的8000点和7000点情景，背后分别对应什么样的市场结构？

聊聊Hartnett这期报告聊的几个要点
1、美元成"破坏之球"，全球流动性全面收缩
他的逻辑简明直接：美元飙升加上黄金跌破4000美元，等同于全球流动性的撤退信号。

2、Hartnett为转向风险偏好设定了三个前提条件：油价（WTI）跌破70美元、10年期美债收益率降至4.5%以下、美元开始下行。周五收盘时，三项条件无一达标。
他的逻辑是油价影响通胀、
10年美债收益率决定贴现率和融资成本、美元走强会增加新兴市场的融资压力。

3、而关于资金流向
这里其实有一个分化，前四周被动工具的买入规模约3171亿美元，而主动基金存在较大赎回压力。这背后有一个重要的点：
市场上涨究竟是主动投资者重新看好基本面，还是被动资金、ETF和长期配置资金持续买入的结果？

两者对市场的意义是不同的：
1）主动投资者推动，意味着风险偏好回归和盈利预期有更强共识。
2）而只是被动资金推动，意味着风险偏好和盈利预期并没有形成共识，这种情况容易出现指数上涨、个股分化、行业内部集中度上升的情况。一旦ETF资金流入放缓，市场的边际买盘就可能迅速减弱。

4、Hartnett 对未来市场的另一个判断：投资者情绪悲观，但实际仓位并没有那么悲观。
Hartnett 特别提到即将公布的11月17日美银全球基金经理调查需要重点关注三个指标：繁荣预期、现金仓位、实际股票仓位。
如果现金仓位上升至4.2%以上，说明基金经理开始真正降低风险资产配置。这反而可能改善市场情绪指标，减少之前的拥挤交易风险。

这里有一个潜在的风险：
同一天美银经济团队认为，通胀持续高于2%目标，可能迫使美联储重新考虑此前的宽松路径，甚至需要进一步提高利率。
同时，该团队也承认如果经济明显放缓、美国与伊朗达成协议导致油价回落，或者股票市场大幅下跌，后续加息可能推迟甚至取消。

把本期Hartnett报告与近期看到的的机构资金流、AI融资、美国财政和美联储政策结合起来，我的判断是：
市场可能已经完成一轮仓位清洗，但宏观压力和流动性风险尚未解除

1）短期：市场有反弹条件，但不能简单理解为新一轮牛市已经开始
对冲基金已经大幅降低杠杆，部分拥挤交易被清理。长期基金却仍在持续买入股票。
这意味着市场下跌时的边际卖盘可能减少，出现空头回补和逢低买入推动的反弹。但反弹是否能够持续，需要观察主动基金是否重新增加风险敞口。

2）中期 最大的风险来自宏观金融条件与AI政策及融资态势的碰撞

我认为目前最值得警惕的组合是：油价长期维持高位、美元继续走强、美债收益率居高不下、科技公司债券发行增加且融资成本进一步上升。
这些因素同时发生，就可能出现AI产业需求仍然旺盛，但资本市场对投资回报率的审视和挑剔更高，这会导致科技产业内部出现更加明显的分化。

拥有强大现金流、资产负债表和商业化能力的公司，会比依赖外部融资的公司更有优势。

所以未来核心是看中期宏观环境的变化，个人角度就聚焦就看三个层面：
1）油价/通胀的走势；
2）中期选举新政治生态下AI政策确实是进一步收紧还只是纠偏；
3）AI商业化是不是还处于加速状态（大云厂的云业务增速和模型厂的实际营收增速）。

text:
A good example of this effect is last year, around February 2025, I was sitting on my couch, with a pillow on my legs and my laptop on top of it (as per usual)

I was trying to make my own Mario Kart style game for hours with Claude, but of course it didn't work at all

This was the time of Claude 3.5 Sonnet and AI couldn't really make games well yet

Anyway I kept trying, and then tried to make a flight simulator, because I was so frustrated by Flight Simulator 2020 loading so slow with endless updates (like most modern games)

That ended up working a bit better and I built a basic blocky looking plane game and I'd tweet updates about it, and people seemed to like it

It was funny because as always with AI a lot of people on here kept telling me "no you can't just make a game with AI", then when I wanted to add multiplayer, even more game developers (even very famous ones) told me "you'll never ever make that work"

Then just 2 days in Claude 3.7 Sonnet came out and suddenly it was actually able to make games for the first time pretty well

And thanks to that, I did get it to work, and we had thousands of people flying at the same time in multiplayer (see pic) and it went really viral

Lots of companies ended up sponsoring the game itself with in-game blimps (remember?) and it made $85,000 in just a month (and $200K total)

I coded that game in Cursor and then @mntruell messaged me my DMs to ask feedback how to improve Cursor (introducing himself as just a "Cursor dev" so humble), so I gave feedback

In that convo I asked if I could ever invest in Cursor (as Dutch people say "not shot is always a miss") and he said sure, and then I wired the money the same week

Meanwhile seeing how much attention these vibe coded games made I thought it'd be nice to direct that to other people's games, so I made Vibe Jam (named after @karpathy's vibecoding term): a game dev competition for vibe coded games, which got 1000+ people to make games and over 1 million people playing the games

Then a year later, Cursor ended up being acquired by SpaceX!

So me messing around on the couch with no goal whatsoever on some stupid game had lots of positive second order effects and literally made me millions, but it'd be hard to imagine that  if you'd see me sit there in February 2025 on the couch working on a Mario Kart clone that by any measure sucked 

So I guess the point is, let people mess around and see where things end up!!!

If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.

Accelerating improvements in model capabilities has made it possible to build a new kind of financial institution — made of agents, protocols, and stablecoins.

FX is a $195T market stuck in the 1970s. There are three forces culminating now that make it possible to build a new kind of financial institution.

- Technological: intelligence is commoditizing, opening products and cost structures that were previously impossible

- Social / Political: the passage of key legislation like the genius act is legitimizing stablecoins as cash equivalents

- Economic: Fundamentally stablecoins are more efficient than fiat and rates rising make stablecoin issuance more interesting and liquidity formation easier

Every major technological shift has produced new financial institutions. The railroads produced JP Morgan.

Stablecoins today are a niche market today numbering in the hundreds of billions. we are on track to dominate this niche. That alone is a good business but not that interesting.

We are working on this because we are betting that stablecoins will continue to eat global commerce.

If we are right, then we will have built generationally important financial infrastructure that will shape how global commerce works for the next century

text:
问了下AI给的回复：
第一点：美国没有管辖权
这个说法太绝对了。美国法院这类命令针对的是币安这家平台，以及平台上的资产，不是针对用户本人，所以和用户的国籍关系不大。币安 2023 年和美国司法部达成了认罪协议，之后要接受美方的合规监管，它实际上没法不执行美国法院的命令。用户当然可以争辩"管辖权延伸得太远"，但不能说"美国没有管辖权，所以冻结不合法"。

另外，作者说的"应该由中国警方发冻结令"那条路，现实中也走不通。币安不在中国境内，中国警方对它发不了冻结令。中国又把虚拟货币交易认定为非法金融活动，基本不会替用户出面主张这笔资产。中美之间确实有刑事司法协助协定，但这只是其中一条渠道，而且这个案子可能是民事没收程序，不一定走刑事途径。

第二点：仓位亏损的钱，对手方要不要也被冻结
这个推理不成立。冻结令锁定的是命令里写明的那个账户，对手方是通过正常交易赚到的钱，不会因此变成"冻结资金"。合约的对手方也不一定是做市商或者币安，大多是其他交易者。不过作者背后真正有价值的问题是：账户被冻结后用户没法操作，仓位继续亏损甚至被强平，这个损失该谁承担？这确实值得追问，可以向法院主张平台或申请冻结的一方应该保全资产价值。

第三点：手续费是不是也该冻结
冻结之前收的手续费，是平台提供服务的正常收入，和冻结无关。说"币安收了手续费，它自己的账户也该被冻结"，逻辑跳得太远了。比较站得住的问法是：冻结之后，强平之类的操作还从被冻结的资产里扣手续费，这样做合不合规？

text:
a few years ago tokens were something u launched after the product, mostly for governance or maybe to pay incentives. I don't think anyone truly saw the token as the product, it was the reward

that changed with the years. Today the token is as important as the product itself. It's used for buybacks, fee switches, revenue share.. so it needs a serious design, it matters as much as the protocol

so there are two products to analyze, and they can definitely go in different directions. A useful model is what i call the Token/Product Quality Matrix, which has four quadrants as pictured:
- good product, good token
- good product, bad token
- bad product, good token
- bad product, bad token

if both the token and product are good, u are one of the, idk, 7 crypto companies doing it really well, with massive traction. Hyperliquid, for example.

good product with a shitty token, you’re probably be fine. Aave for example.

bad product with a good token, everyone is happy until the moment the product reveals how shitty it actually is.

and bad product, bad token, 98% of crypto protocols land here, assuming they are still alive

before buying any token, try to put it in one of the 4 quadrants. If u can't, u don't know what u are buying

text:
我还是维持11月会出现阶段底部的观点，逻辑在于在明年二月份前各方想要的都是终结AI的超预期，而不是美股彻底崩盘。

Trump Trade的逻辑就是用5-10%的题材股（半导体）带动整个大盘，信的人赚钱，这也是之前涨得那么夸张的核心原因。

半导体相对于其他题材的好处是有业绩支撑，业绩预期一大半靠产业内的套娃（更像是Defi）。但市场对于现在的价格已经计入了未来三年的业绩预期（加了需求杠杆后的），在上涨的过程中一部分人脑补新的估值模型。三年后是否能承接上，我的理解是Trump下台不会管身后洪水滔天。

所以民主党上台后的预期是修复AI的估值模型到正确的水平，同样的市场因为战争，原油价格高企这一系列原因本来就属于脆弱状态，那么崩盘是顺理成章。

但民主党真的要股票死掉吗？我觉得不是，只是把估值框架回到一个合理的状态，尤其是半导体，硬件的高利润率很难维持（需求降低），会更强调优化软件（模型）去增加token/GPU 的使用效率，那么首当其冲的就是杀硬件估值。

Trump呢？他的任期还有两年，在丢失了两院后他最大的依仗是美联储（政策无需过两院批准），他的诉求是在他的任期内平稳落地，民主党也要支持他的政策框架，那么股票是个很好的抓手。所以我相信接下来的非农到12月议息会议会是正向的结果。

text:
Giveth - 10 years - WOW.

Truly an incredible milestone. We've done so much and had so much fun along the way! 

I'm so proud of our work.  We've raised millions of dollars for nonprofits, and impacted countless lives around the globe, including countries that are normally out of reach for traditional financial rails.

For the last 10 years Giveth has been on a mission to build something better than governments, and the mission has taken us around the world and back, with dozens of start-ups and countless of collaborators. 

It's been a long hard battle, we've almost shut down in every bear market & yet somehow the generosity of the community has kept us alive. 

There was one point in 2019 where Giveth was just me & Amin, and then 4 years later, we grew into ~75 people working on 7 or 8 different projects all exploring how to make public goods profitable. 

Throughout this decade we've completely redesigned the Giveth platform 6 times!

We were working on bonding curves in 2018, we ran the first Ethereum scaling conference, we pushed for open source block explorers & we even ran Burning Man camps. 

But our journey is not complete... no where near it. 

I am still convinced that we will one day find a model that can make nonprofits profitable. Nonprofits create value, and Giveth's primary goal has always been to produce a novel economic system that can appreciate the value that nonprofits produce. 

It's not easy, and we don't know where this road will take us, but the journey continues.

Right now we are focused on making crypto safe to use for normal people. We rebuilt the Giveth platform to have a much safer experience (thanks to Turnkey) and our work with TheDAO Security Fund will hopefully extend a safer crypto experience to the entire Ethereum community.

Because no matter what cool model we find for appreciating the value that nonprofits produce... It won't work if normal people can use blockchain tech safely.

I couldn't be more proud of the work we've done over the last 10 years & of all the people I've worked with.

It's been quite the journey, one decade down, many more to go.

text:
我还是希望老黄回来，但这条路很窄

我写过，黄仁勋的回归之路有盼头。这个希望，我到今天也没放下。

但这几天把特拉华州的公司法、英伟达的章程和股权披露翻了一遍，得承认，制度上这条路，比我当时想的难走得多。

先说董事会。

昨天，川普对记者说，他可以回来，很多人希望他回来。同一天，董事会那边就有人跟CNBC透了风：没在考虑请他回来，现在只盯着调查。

做调查的是Wachtell的Joon Kim，前纽约南区的代理检察官，当年纽约州长Cuomo的性骚扰调查就是他做的。董事会请这种人进来，是给自己留底的，不是来帮CEO洗白的。

就算报告最后说他没泄密，有一条也很难洗掉。路透手上有他10月发给首席法务官和CMO的消息，说跟那位Alice Huang只是正常的客户往来。11月8号，他才在全员信里认了婚外情。

间谍的事可以吵，对自己公司的法务说谎，在美国上市公司里，基本没有商量的余地。

再说官司。

两单官司在他走之前就立案了：11月9号的证券集体诉讼，11月11号的股东衍生诉讼，衍生那单连董事一起告。

特拉华有个Caremark判例，董事对公司合规有监督责任。2023年麦当劳那个案子，法院又把这个责任延伸到了高管身上。

我的理解是，接受辞职，本身就是董事会在法官面前交的功课。调查还没完，又明知他对法务说过谎，转头把他请回来，等于自己承认上次辞职是做样子。商业判断规则那层保护，D&O保险，都可能保不住。

换我坐在那张桌子边，也很难拿自己的身家去赌民意。

那撤掉董事呢？

股份才是创始人的护城河，这句我写过。英伟达一股一票，老黄大概3.58%，8亿多股，已经是最大的个人股东。可Vanguard、BlackRock、State Street三家加起来接近两成，差不多是他的五倍。何况CEO是董事会过半数就能任免的，他连董事也一起辞了。

票，确实不在他手上。

先例也不多。乔布斯、Altman那两次是抢权、吵路线。因为跟下属的关系或者瞒报下台的，Intel的Krzanich、麦当劳的Easterbrook、BP的Looney，都没回去。

唯一让我还留着点念想的，是RH的Gary Friedman，不到一年就回去了。可他走的时候RH还没上市，背后是几家私募大股东，说了算的就那么几个人。英伟达不是这样的公司。

翻到最后，最让我感慨的是股权设计。

英伟达1999年上市，那个年代就是同股同权。之后才有扎克伯格的B股一股十票；Palantir的创始人拿F类股，投票权锁在49.9%左右；还有快上市的 Anthropic，七个创始人合持唯一一股F类股，固定拿走50.1%的投票权，另外还有独立信托拿着T类股，能选、能罢免过半数的董事。

新一代创始人，都是看着老一辈的教训长大的。老黄把英伟达做成了全世界最值钱的公司之一，手里却没有一张这样的牌。

所以理性上，我知道短期内回英伟达当CEO，几率很小。

情感上，我还是希望他回来。哪怕不是回英伟达，也希望他处理好家里的事，再回到AI这条赛道。

支持一个人，和判断一件事会怎么走，我尽量分开看。但这两件事，我都不想骗自己。

你觉得，他还有别的路吗？

$NVDA

text:
Indian law enforcement froze $3M from an innocent Chinese investor after mistaking a crypto bridge for a pig butchering scam. Now an Indian court has ordered Gate to hand his funds to a person they never belonged to.

My analysis of how Indian LE traced through an unlabeled service and wrongly froze @xxxkeym's Gate account:

The case stems from a pig butchering victim who allegedly lost $1.7M of BTC, USDT, DOGE & SOL in May 2025.

Andhra Pradesh CID registered it as Cr. No. 10/2025 and filed a charge sheet in March 2026.

In July 2025, xxxkeym had Gate deposit address 17mpajZ6Nq3dG3T6wUhaXxYF4Qy9HJnYx5 frozen after depositing 15 BTC from 3NcBhqK in the following transaction:
885f3afab562251b222363cf12095e864ddb94636674b01f0cdb05997e5a54a0

This is one transaction Indian LE cites in its notice. 3NcBhqK was funded by xxxkeym's own OKX & Binance withdrawals in Jan 2023 and the coins sat dormant for years until the Gate deposit. 

Indian LE never froze his OKX or Binance accounts, the actual source of the 15 BTC, which tells you how flawed their justification is.

Gate froze his entire account, which held roughly $3M at the time and about $1.5M today.

The Indian court order hands all of it to the complainant.

Gate deposit address 17mpajZ also received two deposits for 15 BTC total in 2025 from bc1pkkwqyxn3rm608ryuqg9hyqna0syq4jx5pxkr7pzg8n3usx6tyqfst5u966, which is also controlled by xxxkeym.

Shortly before the deposits to Gate, bc1pkkw was funded in three transactions by bc1quzwkggdf6ly06mrrnnled0qdr57w770k45n5n7 & bc1qtu66zfqxj6pam6e0zunwnggh87f5pjr7vdr5cd.

bc1quzw & bc1qtu66z were reported as alibarbit[.]bit, the same scam named in Indian LE's press release. 

That was a mistake. Both belong to the Merlin Chain bridge, which is unlabeled in most compliance tools. 

xxxkeym is simply a normal Merlin user trading tokens on the L2. This wrong label is the only place the scam touches his transaction history.

Below is the blockchain data showing each Merlin withdrawal by xxxkeym matched to a BTC payout from those addresses, plus screenshots of the bridge activity.

xxxkeym bridged 50 BTC into Merlin on March 28, 2024, over a year before the alleged May 2025 theft. 

His three withdrawals came out of that balance. I found zero onchain connections between xxxkeym and the theft.

Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me.

I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA.

I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation. 

Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.

Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.

Jensen

text:
查了一下土豆姐 Lauren Tan 第一次参加技术大会还是在2015 年，那也是她第一次分享，就得站到台上，给几百个程序员做分享。她紧张得直发抖，而且此前连大会观众都没当过。

她从小在新加坡长大，十几岁就折腾过设计和网页，后来却去读了金融。大学接触过 Excel 里的 VBA，毕业后又和朋友创业，钱花完了，生意也没撑起来。她在 2014 年的回顾里写，那时刚开始认真学前端，总觉得自己是混进来的，别人都比自己聪明，几次想干脆放弃。

但她一边学 Ember，一边把学到的东西写成博客，再发到 Twitter。结果框架社区的人看到了，邀请她申请大会演讲。她怕得要命，最后还是报了名，给自己留了三个月准备，硬着头皮上了台。

后来，这次演讲帮她拿到 DockYard 的工作，搬去了美国。再后来，她又通过演讲获得了 Netflix 的机会。在伦敦的一场大会上，她认识了 Dan Abramov，保持联系后，对方问她，愿不愿意来 React 团队。

她中间还主动拐过一次弯。已经在 Netflix 做了工程经理，2020 年却决定辞职，回去当工程师，因为她发现自己最想念的，还是亲手把东西做出来。

在 Meta，她参与了 React Compiler 的研发，2025 年的 1.0 发布文章里就有她的署名。2026 年 3 月，她加入 Cursor，后来又参与做出了 Grokbot。

她在 X 上回顾这些经历时说，每一份工作，都和在这里建立的关系有关。

但这些关系也有个很具体的起点：别人读到了她的文章，看到了她怎么理解一个问题，后来又看到了她能站上台，把它讲清楚。

一个自学程序员，没有 CS 学位，却把自己的学习过程变成了别人判断她的依据。公开分享给技术人的机会，就在这里：你还没有一份漂亮履历，别人也能先看到你会做什么。

Lauren 还在担心自己配不配的时候，那些文章已经替她敲门了。
author: qihang_zeng6688
quoted_text:
兄弟们，Lauren新形象，好戳我啊，她访谈里面说她自己一个月提交了4000多次代码，太牛了！

Lauren Tan 在 YC 的访谈里说，她已经做到让 Agent 自己合并代码，且自己不用每一份都从头读完。

她举了个很具体的例子：自己、同事和一个叫 Potato 的 Bot，在同一条 Slack 讨论串里做功能。Bot 派出云端 Agent，在自己的电脑上运行应用，带着截图和视频回来，大家直接在群里看结果、提意见、继续改。

整条讨论有两百条消息，她说，那个项目自己甚至没打开 Cursor。

但她紧接着讲，做到这一步花了很长时间。

得先把工程师反复检查的东西，写进代码库、自动检查和工具里。再教 Agent 把应用跑起来，检查实际表现，发现问题后回去修改。基础设施、数据库、部署这些关键环节，她仍然认为人应该参与。

她分享的内容里面重要的是把自己的验收标准做成能自动执行的检查。

你每天提醒 AI 同一种错误，说明这条经验还只存在于聊天里。把它变成一条检查规则，以后每次改代码都能自动拦住，才真正省下了你的时间。

更有意思的是，他们现在遇到的新瓶颈，是功能做出来以后，到底该不该合进去。同事刚提出一个想法，旁边已经有人说，代码我周末写好了。

开发越来越快，决定做什么、什么算做好，就越来越值钱。能让 Agent 稳定交付的人，积累下来的每一条判断，都能变成下一次工作的起点；一直靠自己逐条收拾结果，开再多 Agent，也只是给自己多招了几份活。 https://t.co/SvhvErR0ft

For decades, companies needed huge teams, expensive software, support departments, agencies, consultants, manual operations, and layers of management just to deliver a service. Customers got used to paying for all of it because there was no real alternative.

Now a focused team can build and operate meaningful parts of those businesses at a fraction of the cost.

That does not just create better margins. It changes what you can charge, how fast you can move, and who gets access to products that used to be reserved for companies with big budgets.

I think many of the next great companies will take something people already need, remove the old cost structure, and make the incumbent’s price feel impossible to defend.

That is where I plan to build.

text:
It's always difficult to shut down gracefully but Mem seems to be doing a better job than most. Their site offers export options and migration guides for Obsidian and other apps.

Looking back at the history of the company, I was surprised to find they'd raised $29 million in funding. That made Mem among the most funded VCware apps in the space. For comparison:

- Notion: $340m (that we know of)
- Evernote: $290m
- Mem: $29m
- Tana: $25m
- Craft: $20.8m
- Anytype: $13.4m
- Roam: $9m
- Logseq: $4.1m
- Obsidian: $0

I have always admired @_ericaxu and @shida_li for knowing early that they would shun the VC path and build Obsidian without investors.

Having watched the downfall of Evernote from afar, and experienced the pressures of VC first hand, I was afraid they might be swayed by investors waving big checks at their noses. It's one of the reasons I wanted to join Obsidian because I felt it was possible to build a 100% user-supported company in this space.

Being bootstrapped has many downsides. It means Obsidian can't subsidize pricing, can't make big speculative bets, can't hire as many people, can't parallelize projects as much...

There is certainly survivorship bias, but as I look at the landscape six years after launch, Obsidian is still alive and well. I think building without investors made us stronger.

It's a twist of irony that OpenAI's VC fund was one of the biggest investors in Mem, yet the app never adopted Markdown as a storage format.

I could have never predicted that Markdown would become as popular as it is today. Even before LLMs, I felt confident .md files would outlive Obsidian. Now I feel more confident than ever that "File over app" is a philosophy that will outlive us all.

Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me.

I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA.

I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation. 

Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.

Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.

text:
I work in export compliance at Supermicro. I have some insider information regarding our co-founder’s phone passcodes, and I’d like everyone to stand up.

111111

According to his lawyers, those were the codes on Wally Liaw’s work phone and personal phone. He was arrested at 6 a.m. in March. His lawyers say 17 armed FBI agents were in the room. He asked to call his lawyer, so he unlocked his work phone to find the number. 1111. An agent asked whether his personal phone used the same code. He said 111111. The agent told him to type it in to “prove that it worked.”

It worked. Of course it worked. Everything Wally touched worked.

Security people will tell you 1111 is weak. A study of 3.4 million PINs ranked it second, right behind 1234. I call that battle-tested. About 6% of humanity trusts it. Wally didn’t even use 1234. 1234 is a pattern. 1111 is a commitment.

Then, for his personal phone, he used 6 ones. He took a proven design and scaled it. That’s the Supermicro way. We’re famous for rack-scale. Wally gave us rack-scale authentication.

I’ve written 1111 on a sticky note and put it on my monitor. It reminds me what leadership looks like.

His lawyers now say the warrant only allowed a face or fingerprint unlock, and nobody read him his Miranda rights. They want everything on both phones thrown out. If the judge agrees, the phones will join the dummy servers: physically present, legally empty. We’re building a collection.

Let me tell you who we are. On March 19, the day of the arrest, Supermicro said it “maintains a robust compliance program.” We were robust that morning, and we were robust that afternoon. Then our CEO wrote a letter. He said Supermicro appears to have been “a victim of the elaborate schemes orchestrated by these individuals, which deceived both federal authorities and our internal compliance team.”

I’ve read that sentence at 2 a.m. more times than I’ll admit.

Both federal authorities and our internal compliance team. Side by side. Same scheme, same boxes, same hair dryer. Most compliance teams spend their whole careers getting fooled by small-time operators. We got fooled at the federal level. Nobody can take that from us.

Here’s what fooled us, according to the indictment. Starting around October 2023, a company in Southeast Asia ordered servers loaded with Nvidia GPUs and said it was the end user. The servers went to Taiwan, then to Southeast Asia. A logistics company moved them into unmarked boxes and shipped them to China. The customer bought about $2.5 billion worth. From late April to mid-May 2025 alone, at least $510 million went to China.

Bloomberg has reported that the customer was OBON, a Bangkok company. OBON hasn’t been charged. It was a public partner of Thailand’s National AI Strategy. Bloomberg also reported that U.S. prosecutors believe Alibaba was among the final customers.

Think about that. Our customer was part of a national AI strategy. They had a national strategy. We had a checklist. You would have approved them too.

They grew fast. By fiscal 2024 they were our 11th largest customer in the world, with $99.7 million in revenue. Know Your Customer is the first rule of my job. We knew they were big.

The demand was incredible. In December 2024, according to the indictment, Wally told the customer that “the only way” to get Nvidia to commit B200 allocations was to create monthly forecasts. Our customers had to forecast just to be allowed to buy. In China’s gray market, a B300 server has reportedly sold for $1 million, about double the sticker price. Demand like that is a compliment.

We audited them twice. In late 2024, the indictment says, Steven Chang arranged for a “friendly” auditor to do the inspection. It went very well. Friendly audits usually do.

The second audit came in August 2025. This one was rigorous, so the other side got serious. According to the indictment, they staged thousands of dummy servers in our boxes. Ting-Wei Sun planned for about 100 workers, forklift operators and arranged meals. He also wanted a “20-person shuttle bus for easy travel between the hotel and the warehouse, allowing for short breaks.”

Their staging crew got a shuttle bus with short breaks. Our auditor got entertainment. Everyone was taken care of.

Our auditor’s job was to count the servers. The indictment says the auditor was “off-site enjoying entertainment paid for by Company-1.” Sun sent the auditor photos and videos instead. The final count was 2,107 units across 3 warehouses. Sun texted Wally that the audit had run smoothly. According to the indictment, Wally wrote back, “That’s spectacular!”

Wally was right. It was spectacular. 2,107 units counted. 0 units working. If you measure by boxes, our inventory accuracy was perfect.

I’ve seen the photos of the dummy servers. They’re beautiful. Same boxes, same labels, same serial numbers. They can’t compute anything, so nobody wants to smuggle them. Every dummy server we ever audited stayed exactly where it was supposed to be. Our export compliance record on dummy servers is 100%.

Later, the Commerce Department scheduled its own inspection. The indictment says Sun and a broker unboxed the same dummy servers. Then they used a hair dryer to peel the serial number stickers off and stick them back on. Surveillance cameras recorded all of it. That hair dryer went up against the federal government. I’d like it in our trophy case. It’s the only device in this case that did every job it was given.

Our training teaches employees to escalate concerns, and the system works. In January 2025, new AI export rules were announced, set to begin May 13. According to the indictment, Wally texted the customer, “We need to speed these up before May 13!” A few days later he wrote, “We can ship all your 512 x B200 by Feb. Let us run fast before May 13!”

In March, the customer’s executive sent Wally an article about chip smugglers and wrote, “I’m very concerned Wally.” That’s an escalation. In August, a broker sent Wally a Justice Department press release about more smuggling arrests. Wally replied with a string of sobbing-face emojis. That’s also an escalation. Our hotline accepts emojis now. It was the most requested feature.

In October, Sun pleaded guilty to 4 counts, including conspiracy to obstruct justice. Asked for comment, Supermicro pointed to its earlier statements that the indictment had no impact on its business operations. Our former contractor admitted conspiring to obstruct justice, and our business operations didn’t notice. That’s resilience.

Some people say we should have seen this coming. We had seen it before, which is different. In 2006, Supermicro pleaded guilty to exporting motherboards to Iran through a distributor in Dubai. We paid a $150,000 criminal fine, a $125,400 civil penalty to Commerce and $179,327 to the Treasury. The sentencing memo said the fines were “sufficient to deter other companies from committing similar crimes.”

Other companies. We read that very carefully.

20 years later, someone used a pass-through company in another country to send our hardware where it wasn’t allowed. We recognized the pattern immediately, in March 2026, when we read the indictment.

Then there were the accounting years. In 2020 the SEC charged Supermicro with “widespread accounting violations.” The company had recognized revenue on goods “sent to warehouses but not yet delivered to customers.” It also used a marketing program to avoid recognizing expenses, including “for Christmas gifts.” We paid $17.5 million. Our CEO wasn’t charged, but he paid back $2.1 million in stock profits under the Sarbanes-Oxley clawback.

Warehouses have always been where our numbers look their best.

Wally resigned in January 2018, during that accounting investigation. In May 2021 he came back as a consultant. In December 2023 he rejoined the board. In November 2024, a special committee of our board reviewed the rehiring of former employees. Here is its finding, word for word: “With respect to the rehiring of former employees, the tone at the top of the Company is appropriate and fully consistent with a commitment to proper financial reporting and legal compliance.”

I had that sentence engraved. The tone was appropriate. The passcode was 1111.

The same committee found some “lapses.” It held one executive primarily responsible. He was our Chief Financial Officer, and he was also our Chief Compliance Officer. The man who counted the money also checked the rules. Our meetings were the most efficient in Silicon Valley.

The board said it would start searching for a new CFO “immediately.” That was November 2024. The new CFO started in October 2026, “effective immediately.” The first immediately took almost 2 years. The second one took a day. That’s a 99.9% improvement in immediacy.

Our old auditor didn’t wait around. In October 2024, Ernst & Young resigned, saying it was “unwilling to be associated with the financial statements prepared by management.” Our special committee said EY’s conclusions weren’t “supported by the facts.” The auditor who doubted us left. The auditor who trusted us was off-site.

In August 2026, our independent investigation wrapped up. It found no evidence that any current senior manager knew about the scheme. Some people in sales, technical support and business development were let go for failing to follow company policies. Nobody in compliance was on the list. You can’t fire people for being deceived. It’s our core competency. I want it in the 10-K.

The investigation also described diversion as an “industry-wide challenge.” That’s my favorite kind of challenge. It belongs to everyone, so it belongs to no one.

The market has been very understanding. The day after the indictment, our stock fell 33% and lost more than $6 billion in value. Last quarter we reported record revenue of $19.9 billion. We now expect $72 billion to $82 billion this year. The market forgave us faster than the board found a CFO.

Nvidia reports earnings today without Jensen Huang, our CEO’s friend of 30 years. Jensen resigned last week after reports about his relationship with a woman U.S. officials reportedly suspect is a Chinese intelligence asset. Different scandal. Same GPUs.

I’ve updated our password policy. Executives now need 8 digits.

111111

We were victims. We’re excellent at it. And if anyone ever smuggles $2.5 billion of our servers again, I promise you this. We’ll be the first to read about it.

author: TheJensenLetter
quoted_text:
Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me.

I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA.

I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation. 

Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.

Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.

Jensen

$NVDA  - NVIDIA STOPS DISCLOSING SINGAPORE SALES AS REVENUE SURGES TO $104 BILLION

Nvidia stopped separately reporting Singapore-linked revenue after changing its geographic reporting methodology from customer billing addresses to headquarters locations, according to the Financial Times.

Its Singapore subsidiary booked $104 billion in external revenue in 2025, up 72%, representing nearly half of Nvidia's global sales.

The disclosure change comes amid U.S. investigations into Megaspeed, a major Singapore-based customer suspected of diverting advanced chips to China.

Nvidia says most Singapore-billed products were shipped elsewhere.

The shift raises transparency and export-control concerns, though it does not establish wrongdoing.

text:
英伟达今晚这份财报，数字已经不重要了

北京时间明早 5:20 出数，6:00 电话会。

共识营收 1,091 亿、EPS 2.47 美元。季报的数字其实早就落袋了——过去四个季度它都超自己指引中点 4.6% 到 5.7%，这次大概率还是超。

所以今晚唯一还算数的数字，是四季度指引：市场要 1,250 亿。给不到，就是问题。

但真正的定价权在「话」上。念数字的人换了：临时 CEO Colette Kress，干了 13 年 CFO，董事会还在挑正式人选。

而这场电话会上最有杀伤力的一句话，三个月前就是她自己说的。8 月 26 日她给了 FY2028 营收增长约 70% 的展望，当场定性为「受供给约束」——当时华尔街只预期 44%。今晚她敢不敢原样再说一遍，就是全部。

三个看点。

一，四季度毛利率。她自己说过底部在 71%–72%，市场现在只给 70.2%。底部要是往下挪，整条 AI 硬件链一起重估。

二，内存。8 月她把毛利率下滑归因于「内存极端定价」，而下游定价在涨、上游成本也在涨。重点不是成本多高，是她能不能把成本转出去。

三，中国。指引里写死了「中国数据中心收入为零」，但做空机构 Culper 指控 FY26 有约两成计算收入由中国驱动，英伟达否认。

市场会追着问东南亚那部分到底是谁的需求。

钱已经在表态：一天之内至少九家机构下调目标价，均值从 343 砍到 217；期权隐含单日波动约 8%，对应 140 到 172 的区间。

没有Jenson的第一个财报，Jenson之前的承诺还作数吗？

quoted_text:
Giveth - 10 years - WOW.

Truly an incredible milestone. We've done so much and had so much fun along the way! 

I'm so proud of our work.  We've raised millions of dollars for nonprofits, and impacted countless lives around the globe, including countries that are normally out of reach for traditional financial rails.

For the last 10 years Giveth has been on a mission to build something better than governments, and the mission has taken us around the world and back, with dozens of start-ups and countless of collaborators. 

It's been a long hard battle, we've almost shut down in every bear market & yet somehow the generosity of the community has kept us alive. 

There was one point in 2019 where Giveth was just me & Amin, and then 4 years later, we grew into ~75 people working on 7 or 8 different projects all exploring how to make public goods profitable. 

Throughout this decade we've completely redesigned the Giveth platform 6 times!

We were working on bonding curves in 2018, we ran the first Ethereum scaling conference, we pushed for open source block explorers & we even ran Burning Man camps. 

But our journey is not complete... no where near it. 

I am still convinced that we will one day find a model that can make nonprofits profitable. Nonprofits create value, and Giveth's primary goal has always been to produce a novel economic system that can appreciate the value that nonprofits produce. 

It's not easy, and we don't know where this road will take us, but the journey continues.

Right now we are focused on making crypto safe to use for normal people. We rebuilt the Giveth platform to have a much safer experience (thanks to Turnkey) and our work with TheDAO Security Fund will hopefully extend a safer crypto experience to the entire Ethereum community.

Because no matter what cool model we find for appreciating the value that nonprofits produce... It won't work if normal people can use blockchain tech safely.

I couldn't be more proud of the work we've done over the last 10 years & of all the people I've worked with.

It's been quite the journey, one decade down, many more to go.

text:
I CANCELLED MY FUNERAL™
by Ulyssesfve2™
CHAPTER 5: 
THE MANSA MUSA WALK

Post 1/13
Bury the knife story.
Stay silent like the stars in front of the barn.
Don’t mention the blood.
Don’t mention the thirty pieces of silver you sold Baldur for.
Not again.
That’s what those forty-five seconds of fame in chapter 4 keep whispering.
Hunting. Persistent.

Post 2/13
Why was I so broke at the peak of my financial achievements?
The farm was paid for.
Abel had filled my pockets with silver — paid in advance for Baldur’s blood and two hundred and fifty pigs for a Christmas celebration.
All this was supposed to feel like success.
I said that to an old boar named Prometheus.
He was begging for a back scratch at the edge of his cage.

Post 3/13
Prometheus was used to my rhetorical questions.
He always expected the scratch on his back as payment for agreeing with my philosophy.
How do you put a hand on him like a friend
after you have already scheduled him for sausage?

Post 4/13
I wandered off the farm that night.
Heavy.
God on one shoulder. The devil on the other.
Get rid of one and you lose your balance.
You fall out of democracy into some totalitarian hole.
That’s what I told myself so I could keep walking.

Post 5/13
Two in the morning.
Stars hiding under an unfriendly sky.
Then a building full of friendly lights.
If this was hell, those were the gates of heaven in the middle of a cold night.
People going in looked happy.
Dressed for a special event.

Post 6/13
A beautiful young woman tried to throw me out.
Very polite. Casino door.
I did not match the clientele.
Blood on the clothes.
Smell of death in the beard.
Smiling like a madman.
She had no idea the dirty jacket was hiding more silver than the flat her husband rented.
She thought I was there for the free coffee.

Post 7/13
Behind the madman smile sat one cruel thought.
Money is the fastest baptism.
Turns beggars into kings.
Turns sinners into saints.
I didn’t speak.
I opened the zip on the chest pocket.
Suddenly I’m VIP.
Suddenly I’m family.

Post 8/13
I watched the instant love hit her face when the silver caught the light.
I started to doubt the idea that money cannot buy happiness.
Dirt under the nails.
Smell of the dead on my body.
I sat at the table like a king.
I changed Baldur’s blood into chips.
I put the chips on number 14.

Post 9/13
I stood up.
Walked the other way.
Screamed into a busy casino:
“TELL ME IT’S NUMBER 14.”
People dressed like saints stared at a man dressed like a grave.
They couldn’t help it.
They ran to the wheel to see what the hell was happening.

Post 10/13
Hard to say how many seconds passed.
Then strangers screamed it together:
“It’s 14.
It’s ...... 14.”
Hugs from people I had never seen.
From the woman who tried to throw me out.
From the security I had pissed off twenty seconds earlier.

Post 11/13
The maths in my head went clean.
Casino = bad people.
Me. Cain. Blood still on the hands. = good people tonight.
That’s it.
Robin Hood with a wheel.
Steal from the house.
Give it to the broken.

Post 12/13
I took the money and made it rain.
I felt what Mansa Musa felt.
I walked like him.
I showered everyone on the road back —
casino staff,
beggars,
the crew at the farm.
It felt like charity.
It felt like revenge.

Post 13/13
The woman who tried to throw me out invited me to her place.
Showed me love only a poet can describe.
She told me why she doesn’t trust her husband.
He counts.
I made it rain.

End of Chapter 5

text:
DeepMind CEO 哈萨比斯发了条消息，说他自己的那家公司 Isomorphic 又融了 50 亿美元。

印象中他们五月刚融过一轮，翻回去看了下那次，有 21 亿，到现在也就半年时间。

Isomorphic 是从 DeepMind 拆出来专门做药的公司，AlphaFold 那套技术，他们直接拿过来用了。

但到今天为止，它手里还没有一个药真正到人身上试过。

进临床这个事，最早说的是 2025 年，后来又改成今年年底，今年年底的话，其实也就剩一个半月了。

不过投钱的人好像完全不着急。红杉和 Greenoaks 领投，a16z 这次新进来，Alphabet 自己又加了一笔，老股东也全都跟了。
红杉那边的说法是，他们觉得 Isomorphic 摸到了自己模型的 scaling law，就是算力和数据往上加，效果会一直往上走。

模型在变强这个我是信的。但做药这行有个绕不开的地方，最值钱的那部分数据，得一个病人一个病人去试，一试可能就是好几年，这个你算力再多也没法一下子变出来，钱多也没法让它快多少。

我琢磨投的人应该也不是在赌哪一个药能成。
它现在挣钱的路子，其实更像给药厂打工。礼来、诺华前两年都跟它签过合作，先付一笔钱，药往后推进一步再给一笔。这种生意不用等自己的药上市，也能一直有钱进来。

那 50 亿砸进去，我猜是想把这个位置先占住。以后药厂找分子，第一个想到的是它，就跟现在大家做模型绕不开英伟达差不多。

可问题也在这儿。药厂是很现实的，合作签了，最后看的还是有没有东西真走进临床。第一个药要是今年年底又推迟，或者进去了数据不好看，那个 scaling law 的说法就得重新被问一遍。

并且这事会传下去。现在一堆 AI 做药的公司融资，拿的都是这套讲法。Isomorphic 是最贵、背景最硬的那家，它这一步走得怎么样，后面那些公司的估值都得跟着重新算。

我猜这 50 亿很大一部分，买的其实就是等它这几年的时间吧。就看它等不等得到了。

《老黄本人开口了：董事会让我回来，我就回来，你们这帮傻逼现在还有什么话说？》

卧槽，有戏啊。

11月17号上午，老黄辞职 5 天之后，第一次公开开口了，在社交平台上亲自发的，华尔街日报第一时间转的，63 万次查看，4 万个赞，5,500 多条评论，1 万次转发。

他说的第一句话，是认错。

他说，我没达到英伟达对每个人的标准，我在个人生活里犯了严重的错误，我给董事会制造了问题，我深深后悔，我完全认错，我会配合董事会的独立调查。

没甩锅，没狡辩，没说我没错，没说都是别人害我。认错认得干干净净，这才是老黄。

他说的第二句话，是表白。

他说，53 年前来到美国，成为美国公民是他人生最伟大的礼物和最骄傲的时刻。英伟达是他一生的工作，只有在美国才可能有英伟达这样的公司。他爱这个国家，他爱英伟达。

这还不够清楚吗？一个爱美国、爱英伟达、把 33 年青春都砸进英伟达的人，会是间谍？会是走私芯片的内鬼？你们那帮人编故事之前，能不能先看看他写了什么？

他说的第三句话，才是最重磅的，也是我们之前分析了整整一周的东西，终于被他本人证实了。

他说，自从我离开之后，英伟达的员工、投资者、商业伙伴、客户，铺天盖地地呼吁我回来当首席执行官。很多人还在直接联系我。如果董事会认为我的回归符合股东、员工、公司和美国的最佳利益，我将非常荣幸地回应这些呼吁，回来当首席执行官。

听清楚了吗？如果董事会让我回来，我就回来。

这不是金融时报 11 月 15 日报的作战室传闻了，这不是马斯克、斯威尼、加里·谭在请愿书上签名了，这是老黄本人，亲口说的：我愿意回来。

我们之前说的分析，一条一条，全对上了：

第一，金融时报 11 月 15 日说，老黄在考虑回归，跟亲信讨论过，盟友在组作战室游说董事会，争取白宫支持，老黄本人支持这个行动。今天老黄自己出来了，亲口承认了，他就是在考虑回归。

第二，川普 11 月 16 日早上在白宫门口说不介意他回来，说不相信那个女人是间谍，说老黄回去不是个坏主意。今天老黄出来了，等于接住了川普这句话：总统说不介意，我说我愿意，球现在在董事会脚下。

第三，请愿书已经超过 18 万签名，包括 8,800 多名英伟达员工，马斯克、斯威尼、卢特克全站出来了。今天老黄自己说了，员工、投资者、商业伙伴、客户都在呼吁他回来，很多人还在直接联系他。这不是左媒编的，这是老黄亲口说的。

第四，商务部司法部 11 月 16 号晚上发声明，2025 年 6 月英伟达就断供那家新加坡公司了，查的是那家公司，不是老黄。今天老黄出来了，配合调查，认错，但不认间谍、不认走私。公司归公司，个人归个人，间谍锅官方没扣，老黄自己也不背。

现在球在董事会脚下，董事会昨天刚说没兴趣让他回来、连别的职位也没兴趣，今天老黄就公开说我愿意回来。董事会今天还新成立了一个国家安全和出口管制监督委员会，让苏珊娜·诺拉·约翰逊当主席，说要管国家安全和全球贸易合规。

什么意思？董事会也在找台阶下。你让老黄回来，总得有个理由，总得有个新制度，总得有个监督委员会来兜底。今天这个委员会，就是台阶。

贝森特还在那嚷嚷要外面找人、要大换血，可贝森特是财政部长，不是总统，不是董事会，不是老黄。白宫那个盟友，就是川普本人，川普已经表态了。董事会那个没兴趣，是昨天的表态，今天老黄表态了，明天董事会还敢说没兴趣吗？

12 月 1 日众议院闭门，12 月 3 日参议院公开听证，12 月 10 日卢特尼克也要去作证。老黄今天这封公开信，就是在听证会之前，先把态度亮出来：我认错，我配合调查，我爱美国，我爱英伟达，如果你们让我回来，我就回来。

那帮人 11 月 19 日的上市，踩着老黄的尸体上市的梦，该醒了。纽时，你们 11 月 7 日、8 日、11 日三刀捅完老黄，以为大功告成了，现在老黄本人站出来了，你们还编得下去吗？

我们的分析，从第一天就没错过。老黄会回来的，不是 2028 年 1 月，不是 2028 年 3 月，是现在，球已经在董事会脚下了。

I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA.

I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation. 

Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.

Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.

Jensen

Fed理事持续放鹰，10月零售放缓，12月加息50BP概率走低，但是连续加息风险并未解除！

昨天沃什讲话对利率与经济的解读并不多，重点讲的是AI，其中谈及AI风险这个话题其实值得注意

沃什表示，如果大规模AI基础设施投资的回报不及预期，可能引发股市估值调整，并拖累就业与经济，这句话说的是美股，但是其背后意味着Fed政策近期特殊的“反身性”

前两周我一直提及的反身性，即如果市场预期美联储政策收紧，并且市场超预期对未来政策收紧进行定价，导致金融流动性收紧，那么Fed反而会削弱继续加息的必要

而沃什这段话的后半段，股市的估值调整影响经济与就业，如果沃什在12月份议息会议中表示金融环境足够紧，美股调整影响经济，那么未来继续加息的必要性就削弱，这就是特殊时期Fed 政策反身性的逻辑

而今晚的10月零售数据，虽然名义数据走弱，但是提出汽车之后的消费数据依旧强劲，虽然数据可以看出通胀在逐渐侵蚀购买力，但是距离通胀抑制消费的预期还很远

而CME 概率上，12月加息50BP的概率下降为4.6%，12月加息25BP的概率回归96%，而1月继续加息的概率依旧维持在60%以上，这意味着市场还在预期到2027年3月份之前最少有2次加息，最多可能是3次持续加息

政策预期上，我认为到12月9日之前利率市场的预期还是处于相对高压的，尤其是本周10月议息会议记录公布+近期多位Fed官员放出鹰派观点，这无疑会让市场持续笼罩在未来利率收紧的高压状态下

当然，市场如果已经代替Fed完成了金融流动性收紧的工作，Fed在12月后继续加息的可能性会变弱，但是政策反身性的发酵没有那么快，所以，未来20天，各位小伙伴要注意抗住宏观压力！

11月16日—11月22日全球宏观指引：12月加息预期锁定，未来Fed政策节奏成为关注点！英伟达财报迎来AI盈利终考，APEC首脑聚会是否可以改变世界走势！？

本周三大核心主题：

中国APEC峰会，三大首脑聚集能否再次改变世界格局？（涉及地缘、贸易、经济多方走向，影响能源，黄金与风险资产走势）

宏观定价，12月加息预期锁定，本周10月议息会议记录公布，市场根据10月会议纪要+近期Fed官员讲话，判定未来Fed政策节奏！

Q3财报收尾，英伟达财报本周18日凌晨公布财报，算是本季度财报的收尾，Q3美股财报季整体情况比较坎坷，虽然行业基本面依旧健康，但是受到政治不确定性、利率不确定性因素压制，估值出现较大调整。而英伟达作为龙头企业，财报更是决定了市场信心，能否对抗宏观压力逆转趋势

接下来整体解读三大主题的：

第一主线——中国APEC峰会，中美俄三大首脑会晤，能否改变世界格局？北京时间11月19日

1，地缘格局，本次期望值最大的就是看本次峰会能否让持续了几年的俄乌战争进入谈判和平阶段，这将会有助于全球经济，贸易以及地缘局势的稳定性

2，美伊局势，如果俄乌出现重大和平转机，其实对美伊局势不太乐观，没了俄乌拖住美国的精力，特朗普很有可能将压力重新给到伊朗

3，坡脚总统，失去国会两院特朗普未来两年在政策是必然是跛脚的，从刚上任的意气风发，到现在的跛脚总统，面对国内政治压力，看特朗普是否会选择对外妥协，尤其是对俄罗斯放松制裁，对中国放松贸易对抗，提升自己在国内的支持率。

4，从地缘，经济与贸易角度来看，如果本次三方可以谈的愉快，短期起码可以提振股市，核心政策的乐观可以为风险市场带来一定信心，尤其是对中美股市，短期是有提振效果，但是能否逆转趋势，还是要看峰会后中美双方官方是否公布相关的积极政策信号

5，峰会期间中美股市节奏，峰会前开始反弹，期间看是否有乐观信号出现加速反弹，峰会后回落，然后等待准确政策信号进行定价

第二主线——宏观定价，10月FOMC会议纪要11月19日凌晨03:00（北京时间）与零售数据！

1, 截止目前，12月加息基本上板上钉钉，市场不在关注12月是否加息，而是在通过更多的信息来预期12月加息多少，以及到2027年3月份加息几次的节奏

2，10月会议纪要成为重要政策观察点，10月利率决议中有两位理事支持加息50BP，所以市场需要通过这份10月的会议纪要来看当时Fed官员对通胀对利率的态度，然后结合近期多位发言的官员言论以及宏观数据对未来政策预期进行在定价

3，这份会议纪要要解决五个关键问题：

a，10月暂停到底是等待数据，还是认为金融条件已经足够紧缩？如果多数认为金融条件不够紧，必然增加后续加息的预期，
b，否有更多官员支持连续加息？美银在预期到2027年3月份有三次加息，目前数据支持，如果会议纪要显示更多官员支持连续加息，将会进一步加重连续加息预期
c，Fed如何评价能源冲击？如果Fed认为能源冲击已经向核心商品、工资与服务价格扩散，那么仅靠Brent下跌未必足以改变政策方向。
d，关于Fed政策“反身性”，如果高长端收益率、信用利差扩大与风险资产下跌已经明显抑制需求，那么Fed继续加息的边际必要性可能下降。
e，Fed调整了2027年2028年议息会议时间，节奏，10月会议纪要中是否体现出讨论情况，有助于预期后续沃什政策能否落实，尤其是对减少议息会议，取消点阵图等重要事项

4，美国10月零售数据，11月17日21:30（北京时间），零售数据本周影响权重增加，如果过强，意味着当前利率并未压制需求，可能会让Fed有更多的加息政策施展空间，所以本周零售数据重点看整体零售销售、剔除汽车、Control Group（控制组）以及实际消费能力

零售温和走弱，对风险资产以及加息预期最有利，过强则增加加息风险，过弱会有衰退风险，后两者对风险资产都属于负面

第三主线——英伟达财报成为AI产业链关键验证，能否扭转高利率下的估值压力？

1，本周三凌晨英伟达公布财报，算是为本季度财报画上一个句号。Q3季度美股财报整体来看，行业基本面依旧稳定，但是受宏观与政治不确定性因素干扰，企业资本开支过快，盈利能力较弱成为估值调整的核心

2，英伟达财报作为收尾也是行业龙头，关乎行业信心，所以本周财报关注数据中心收入、Blackwell平台需求、毛利率、订单交付、下一季度指引及客户资本开支持续性

3，重申一下Q3财报季之后美股企业的验证逻辑变化为：AI资本开支增长 → 订单兑现 → 收入增长 → 利润增长 → 自由现金流改善 → 投资回报得到验证，而对于英伟达财报来说，可以验证算力供应商是否赚钱，但是不能单独证明所有购买GPU的云厂商都获得了理想的AI投资回报，这需要注意

4，本周英伟达财报需要回答市场五个问题：

a，数据中心收入能否继续超预期？如果收入增长继续加速，说明AI基础设施采购仍然强劲。
b，毛利率能否保持稳定？收入高速增长但毛利率下滑，可能意味着产品组合、成本、竞争或者客户议价能力发生变化。
c，下一季度指引是否足够强？估值是交易未来增长，所以未来指引对估值影响更大
d，Blackwell平台订单和交付是否健康？看需求是否增长，是否有供给瓶颈，以及客户订单与最终收入确认的情况
e，云厂商资本开支能否持续？这点本季度几大云厂商的财报已经给了答案，英伟达财报二次验证即可

5，英伟达三种财报的可能性：

a，收入超预期+毛利率稳定+指引上调，意味着需求与盈利同时改善，有助于提振科技股估值修复
b，收入强+毛利率一般+指引一般，意味着保持增长，但是估值要求提高，对目前来说并不乐观
c，收入与指引都不及预期，AI需求增长叙事信心下降，英伟达估值进一步调整

6，英伟达临时换帅，导致估值提前调整，尤其是失去黄仁勋的加持之后，一份普通财报好像是无法满足市场对估值的信心，如果黄仁勋有回归的可能性，则可以忽视财报中的一些瑕疵

辅助线——美伊局势

本周美伊局势不作为重点，参考上周的逻辑，特朗普应该是要集中精力在三方首脑会晤中解决俄乌问题，如果俄乌方面乐观，美伊和平预期变差，如果特朗普无法促成俄乌和谈，则可能对伊朗做出缓和态度！

整体总结：

本周对美股对加密都是一场重要考验，市场下跌中信心不足，筹码稳定性变差，此时如果全球局势，地缘，贸易不确定性继续增加，如果AI叙事再出关键问题，那么对市场来说就是一场灾难，当然我依旧认为未来是乐观的！
