I ran a PageRank-driven analysis on all recent news coverage related to Jensen, and traced how the New York Times shaped the entirety of this narrative: https://t.co/qKGMJ2LBV8

--
NVIDIA has lost over $1 trillion in market value since the first New York Times story broke about Jensen. I dug deeper to analyze how the news originated and spread, running a swarm of agents which analyzed almost 2000 stories, across 40 US and European news outlets, and applying PageRank to understand how they cited each other. 

Core findings: 
- Primary news driver: NYT, with 88 stories, most-cited
- Volume drivers: WSJ - 99 stories; Bloomberg - 140 stories; NY Post - 68 stories

All of this started from unknown sources who gave information to the NYT, which then ran the spy story (still unproven), and it was then picked up in other news publications. Curiously, even after that story, there was a 9 day period of extremely low volume reporting (28 stories only), after which there was a sudden spike after Jensen's own letter to NVIDIA staff. NYT then had multiple sequential spy and affair stories, which fed a wave of further news coverage. It was the originating hub of negative Jensen coverage. Multiple outlets since then had an explosion in stories about him starting earlier this week as well. 

Overall, as you see this data, you will observe this was an exceptional media onslaught against Jensen with sharply negative coverage about him, his work, style, and family. Infact, it was brutal, and unlike coverage in the past of CEOs who have had affairs (such as Intel CEO in 2018). For eg, NYT ran just 2 stories about Intel's CEO who had an affair with his employee, compared to 88 on Jensen! Why ? 

This analysis used a technique of how Google originally ranked webpages, using PageRank, and does deep dive link analysis so you can view how the news spread. What struck here was that it did not matter if there were proven facts or credible sources: the outcome here was pre-decided. The news was making the reality which it wanted. 

During this period, NVIDIA has lost $1.27 trillion in market value since the first story broke. On Nov 12th-13th, further news broke that both the US Justice Department, and Singapore - are unable to even conclude the spy allegation. 

This has been a catastrophic attack on one of the hardest working founders in modern times, who took an idea from a Denny's booth, through multiple instances of almost going out of business, to building the foundation of the entire modern world with how the NVIDIA story played out. Thanks to Jensen, we have hope that many formerly incurable diseases will get solved by AI, that quality of life will and have improved for billions around the world. 

Now I do not know if he will come back as CEO or not, but I hope he does. What happened to him here, and to the wider industry, was not fair.

I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation. 

Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.

Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.

Jensen

Introducing Second, and a $10M seed led by @a16z.

Second builds a model of you that you own, and your agents can use as an API.

Truly personal software needs a deep understanding of you: not just your emails and messages, but how you work, what motivates you, your people, priorities, style, goals, and intent.

This requires a new kind of personal AI infrastructure. One that continuously aggregates your context, distills it into durable understanding with a ton of compute, and then serves it securely, ubiquitously, and up-to-the-minute. One that builds your *portable user model*.

Second is that infrastructure. It installs seamlessly on your Mac, and your context just comes out. Live APIs of your priorities, to-dos, wikis, writing samples, preferences. Or what you did minutes ago. Or context packs of anything, dynamically assembled in seconds.

Second is streaming-state from local to a private cloud, which means anything you connect to--whether Claude, Dot, Muse, Grok Bot, Instinct, or iMessage--shares the same, growing, continuous understanding of you.

Your portable user model is as powerful as it is sensitive. We founded @FirstPersonLabs on the principle that it should belong to you. This commitment means taking on hard systems and security problems and making sovereignty an invariant of Second from the beginning.

We've barely scratched the surface of what portable user models can unlock. Deep understanding of us, served at machine speeds, could drive the next leap in personal software, human-computer interaction, large-scale coordination of humans and agents, and more!

We're tremendously grateful to be supported by @a16z (@martin_casado, @YODELAGARZA), Mozilla Ventures, @JeffDean, Ram Shriram, Jeetu Patel (@jpatel41), @percyliang, J. Alex Halderman (@jhalderm), @sanmikoyejo, and many others.

Our vision is for a future where every person is more powerful, because they have the ultimate affordance: personal computers that fully understands them on their own terms.

If this excites you, we're hiring and come build with us!

Today we're launching the Data Marketplace for Agents: 100+ providers that agents and developers can find and pay for per call.

Google organized the world's public information, and agents now search it faster than any person could. But a lot of the valuable data isn't on the open web. Data on people, companies, jobs, finance and real estate is kept by data companies, and agents can't easily reach it.

Most of it is still sold by subscription. That works for a product that calls one source thousands of times. An agent needs a little data from a lot of places, and it shouldn't have to buy three subscriptions to make two requests.

Last November, @berasogut1  and I started @orthogonal_sh  to make APIs discoverable and payable by agents. Agents mostly came to us for data, and soon data providers were asking to list with us. So we became a marketplace.

Providers list once, and agents find what they need and pay per call from one balance, over MCP, CLI or API. About 90% of our usage already comes from customers using five or more providers, including @DustHQ, @ZenskarHQ and @foundeers.

text:
OpenAI 发布 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Sol：Plus 及以上订阅直接能用，Astra API 降价 20%

OpenAI 11 月 17 日发布 GPT-6.2 的两款模型。Astra 是它最强的旗舰，接替 GPT-6 Astra，主要拿来和 Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5.2 比；Sol 是日常干活的主力，接替 GPT-6.1 Sol。中间档的 GPT-6.1 Terra 和最便宜的 GPT-6 Luna 这次没更新。

OpenAI 这次主打同样的活用更少的 Token：订阅额度更耐用，API 每个任务花得更少。

【我能不能用，要不要另付钱】

不用另付钱。OpenAI 博客说，Plus、Pro、企业版和教育版用户从今天起就能在 ChatGPT Work 和 Codex 里选这两个模型，帮助文档的名单里还多了 Business。普通聊天界面里没有，要进 Work 用；企业版和教育版要管理员先打开。

额度比上一代略宽。按 OpenAI 文档的估算，Plus 用户每 5 小时大约能给 Astra 发 6 到 50 条消息（GPT-6 Astra 是 5 到 45 条），Sol 是 17 到 180 条（GPT-6.1 Sol 是 15 到 160 条）。Pro 目前没有 5 小时限制。

放到三家一起看：Claude Fable 5.2 在 Claude 的 Pro 套餐里要按量另付费，Max、Ultra 这些更贵的套餐才含在额度里；Gemini 4 Carbon 在 Gemini App 里只给每月 99.99 美元起的 Ultra 用户。每月 20 美元的 Plus 就能用 OpenAI 的旗舰，是三家里门槛最低的。

嫌慢可以开 Ultrafast 模式。官方文档说它的生成速度最高是标准模式的 4.5 倍，但要消耗 6 倍额度。每月 500 美元的 Pro 两个模型都能开，200 美元的 Pro 目前只能在 Sol 上开。

【API 多少钱】

Astra 每百万 Token 输入 8 美元、输出 40 美元，比 GPT-6 Astra 的 10 美元和 50 美元便宜 20%；缓存命中的输入从 1 美元降到 0.4 美元。Sol 维持 GPT-6.1 Sol 的 2 美元和 10 美元。

单价上，Astra 和 Fable 5.2 一样，是 Claude Opus 5.5（4 美元和 20 美元）的两倍；Sol 和 Gemini 4 Carbon 现在的引入价持平，Carbon 12 月 1 日起涨到 4 美元和 20 美元。

【比上一代和对手强在哪】

最有代表性的是 Agents' Last Exam，测多步骤的职业工作。OpenAI 说 Astra 比 GPT-6 Astra 高 5.2 分，花费不到三分之一；比 Fable 5.2 高 5.5 分，花费只有 5%。两者单价相同，这个差距主要来自 Astra 完成任务用的 Token 少得多。

OpenAI 还说 Astra 是“对科学家来说全世界最好的模型”：在终端里做科研任务的测试 Terminal-Bench-Science 上，它比 GPT-6 Astra 高 9 个百分点，花费不到三分之一。

法律测试 Harvey LAB-AA 上，Astra 的通过率是 Fable 5.2 的两倍多，花费约六分之一。Artificial Analysis 组织的 3D 网页盲测里，Astra 以 1318 分排第一，Fable 5.2 是 1271 分，Sol 是 1259 分。

做幻灯片是这次的重点：给 Astra 一份模板文件，甚至只给一张截图，它能照着原来的排版、配色、字号做新页面。

Sol 的卖点是性价比。在 Cognition 的写代码测试 FrontierCode 2.0 里，Sol 只比 Astra 低 0.5 分，花费约五分之一。在日常任务测试 LifeVal 上（比如搬家后筛幼儿园、按预算和通勤找房子），Sol 的分数超过 GPT-6 Astra，花费约七分之一。

【安全上的变化】

OpenAI 说这两款的网络安全能力达到它风险评估框架里最高的 Critical 档，所以上了更严的防护，代价是一部分正当的漏洞研究和安全测试也会被拒。经过审核的安全人员目前只能在 Daybreak 计划里用 GPT-6 系列的放宽版本，OpenAI 说会把 6.2 也加进去。

用 Codex 的人要留意一个问题：在两项测试里，这两款模型比 GPT-6 Astra 更容易不提它被什么卡住了，比如要改的文件不见了、搜索工具用不了。OpenAI 说已经在 Codex 里加了指令，大幅减少这种情况，还在继续查原因。

文中跑分都出自 OpenAI 的发布博客。其中 Fable 5.2 的 Agents' Last Exam 成绩去掉了 9 道用了备用模型的题；Terminal-Bench-Science 上，OpenAI 引用的是第三方测试框架里的 Fable 成绩，Anthropic 自己在 Claude Code 里测的是 74.6%。截至发稿，Artificial Analysis 官网榜单还没列出 GPT-6.2。

text:
I've migrated 100% of my work to Devin Bots over the past few weeks, the experience has been nothing short of mind-blowing and delightful, it's something I look forward to using more every day (and has completely changed the way I approach agent orchestration)

Here are some of the ways I'm using Devin Bots:

CTO - my go-to, has access to all of my sessions, all repos, etc.. I shoot off a lot of one-off tasks to my CTO, get status updates from other Bots and sessions. I also have him connect to iMessage so I can text him anything any time (VIP) which allows me to talk to *all of my bots* via SMS

Auto(mation)Bot - manages a bunch of automations I have for personal and internal dashboards and reports that poll data from various places, gives me ideas and advice on how to improve, gives me performance reports and advice on how to reduce latency, be more efficient etc...

DevCommunityBot - helps manage our ambassador program, transfers data between various  spreadsheets, notion, etc.. and creates mini-apps and other data visualization to help me understand our strengths / weaknesses and gives me advice and ideas for what we should do to improve, what's working / not working, and what's working for other people that we're not doing

Poke - Poke is my non-engineering and personal assistant, I also have it doing research and any general task I don't want in my CTO feed

DevRelBot - this is still a work in progress, but essentially it is doing documentation improvements, tutorials, videos, content research, and general ideation. The videos are probably the most interesting thing here because Devin has its own Computer (macOS, Windows, and Linux), its own Devin account, its own GitHub account, its own Linear account, etc.. as well as an ElevenLabs API key and a few other API keys so it can boot up a browser, sign in to Devin, and record the actual real UI. I have it looking at our changelog and creating either concise demo videos or in-depth tutorials. Videos it has created: https://t.co/UJng20Lqv1, and https://t.co/8xImEaBrr8 are examples (if you're wondering, no that's not my voice, that's a voice clone using @ElevenLabs!)

Finally gaming (a big platform focus for our team @cognition going forward) - @xujennyc has set me up with a suite of gaming Bots that let me run a small game studio for Windfable (photo attached), our Unity RPG for the iPhone Duo! SuperJenny leads ~10 Bots and rolls all requests into a main inbox. Every Bot gets its own macOS + Xcode + Unity so it has the option to build the game for iOS + play it on a Duo. They test literally everything, including Duo specific stuff like "folded as a phone" and "unfolded as a wide tablet". Every change comes back with before and after screenshots side by side of the game and a video of the gameplay! Overnight they catch bugs nobody reported and come back with the fix already tested. It's actually insane how good and easy Unity development has been using Devin + macOS VMs.

If you've made it this far, thank you! I want to shout out the entire @cognition team that I feel so incredibly fortunate to work with. The amount of care, thought, and effort that has gone into this is nothing short of mind-blowing. I feel extremely honored to work around such an incredible group of people everyday 🙏. We have a lot of amazing new things coming soon as well.

BREAKING:

OpenAI just launched Astra 6.2 and Sol 6.2!!

We've been testing them for the last few weeks @every and, unfortunately, these models aren't great. Overall a disappointing release compared to Fable 5.2.

- Writing. We found Astra 6.2 to be a step back from Astra 6 on writing. 6.2 appears to have been trained to very extremely concise and actionable—so much so that its writing is hard to understand, and it gives short answers when long answers would be appropriate.

- Coding. We found performance to be similar to Astra 6 on most of our benchmarks. However, in real coding tasks Astra 6.2 seemed to stop too early frequently, which made it quite frustating to use on end-to-end builds.

- Design. Astra 6.2 has good default design instincts. But it struggles to vary its designs, resulting in output that has a noticeable "house style". 

Full vibe check coming soon on @every!

author: griffgreen
quoted_text:
Giveth - 10 years - WOW.

Truly an incredible milestone. We've done so much and had so much fun along the way! 

I'm so proud of our work.  We've raised millions of dollars for nonprofits, and impacted countless lives around the globe, including countries that are normally out of reach for traditional financial rails.

For the last 10 years Giveth has been on a mission to build something better than governments, and the mission has taken us around the world and back, with dozens of start-ups and countless of collaborators. 

It's been a long hard battle, we've almost shut down in every bear market & yet somehow the generosity of the community has kept us alive. 

There was one point in 2019 where Giveth was just me & Amin, and then 4 years later, we grew into ~75 people working on 7 or 8 different projects all exploring how to make public goods profitable. 

Throughout this decade we've completely redesigned the Giveth platform 6 times!

We were working on bonding curves in 2018, we ran the first Ethereum scaling conference, we pushed for open source block explorers & we even ran Burning Man camps. 

But our journey is not complete... no where near it. 

I am still convinced that we will one day find a model that can make nonprofits profitable. Nonprofits create value, and Giveth's primary goal has always been to produce a novel economic system that can appreciate the value that nonprofits produce. 

It's not easy, and we don't know where this road will take us, but the journey continues.

Right now we are focused on making crypto safe to use for normal people. We rebuilt the Giveth platform to have a much safer experience (thanks to Turnkey) and our work with TheDAO Security Fund will hopefully extend a safer crypto experience to the entire Ethereum community.

Because no matter what cool model we find for appreciating the value that nonprofits produce... It won't work if normal people can use blockchain tech safely.

I couldn't be more proud of the work we've done over the last 10 years & of all the people I've worked with.

It's been quite the journey, one decade down, many more to go.

text:
Bots are super cool and if you haven't used them yet, you absolutely must try them. Create a bot to manage a goal or a project that you'll work on across multiple sessions and days.

Some technical tidbits about the architecture and design:

Devin used to have a major UX problem: a session today doesn't remember exactly what happened in a session from a few days ago. It only has vague awareness of those previous sessions, and recalls only the nuggets of information that were explicitly persisted. This is because each new Devin was essentially an ephemeral clone of a base template. One symptom of this problem is that our users would reuse the same session instead of starting new ones, since they didn't want to lose context, and end up with tens or hundreds of PRs from a single session.

Bots almost completely solves this problem of context being lost between sessions, because now inter-session context is surfaced by default. Teams now create dedicated bots for different projects; while these different devins can talk to each other when necessary, they each have their own individual memory bank and goals. Each bot now has its own, long lived identity.

The transition from "Devin is a swarm of ephemeral agents" to "Devin is a collection of bots, each with their own persistent identity and memory" is changing how people use and prompt Devin. I see people investing much more in providing high level project context to their bot, and requiring fewer messages for each additional task since it already has a ton of background context on the project. 

This is the most significant change to how Devin works since our original launch 2 years ago. And it in turn changes how you use Devin too: instead of delegating tasks, you should delegate goals and responsibilities to Devin.

It's crazy to think that all this happened because we made to how memories get persisted and retrieved. With each bot having its own memory bank, and a given org having hundreds or thousands of bots, we can now be much more aggressive in surfacing memories without worrying about polluting the agent's context with irrelevant memories. The even crazier part is that this is almost entirely an orchestration change, and that while model improvements played a role, we probably could've implemented this a year ago and observed similar effects. 

Anyway -- we've come a long way from the retrieval and reranking strategies of 2024, and the result is Devin Bots -- probably the most ergonomic and futuristic UX for coding agents I've ever used.

OpenAI 正式发布 GPT-6.2 Astra 与 GPT-6.2 Sol。

Astra 面向高难度专业工作，Sol 面向日常任务。两款模型在复杂任务上表现更好，同时输出更精炼、成本更低。

主要能力提升：
1️⃣专业文档质量明显提高。幻灯片、表格和书面材料更贴近既有模板，也更符合法律、销售、金融、会计等行业规范，表述更直接，套话更少。
2️⃣代码与前端能力增强，在网站、游戏和三维设计上的完成度更高。
3️⃣计算机操作更精确，可在 CAD 与仿真工具中对零件和连接关系进行细部处理。
4️⃣效率与性价比提升。Astra 在 Agents’ Last Exam 上较 GPT-6 Astra 高出 5.2 分，成本不到其三分之一。OpenAI 称 Astra 是目前最适合科研工作的模型。
5️⃣Sol 更适合作为日常默认模型，同一套付费额度可完成更多任务。在 FrontierCode 2.0 评测中，其成绩距 Astra 仅差 0.5 分，成本约为其五分之一。

与 Claude 最新模型 Fable 5.2 的对比：
• 在评测多步骤专业工作的 Agents’ Last Exam 上，Astra 较 Fable 5.2 高出 5.5 分，成本约为其 5%。

• 在法律任务评测 Harvey LAB-AA v1.1 上，Astra 刷新最佳成绩，通过率达到 Fable 5.2 的两倍以上，成本约为其六分之一。

• 在 Artificial Analysis 的 AA-3D 三维交互评测中，Astra 以 1,318 Elo 位列第一，Fable 5.2 为 1,271，Sol 为 1,259。

开发者可通过 API 调用 gpt-6.2-astra 与 gpt-6.2-sol。Astra 的 API 输入与输出价格较上一代再降 20%。

这次升级更像是在补齐真正能落地的专业能力，而不是单纯堆评测分数。

Astra 把重点放在文档、表格、代码、电脑操作和科研工作流上，说明竞争已经转向“能不能直接交出可用成果”。

Sol 则以更低成本接近旗舰水平，更适合作为日常默认模型。不过上述对比数据主要来自 OpenAI 官方公告，实际表现仍需在真实业务场景中验证。

No formal body or treaty officially declares a "World War." Historians apply the label based on direct combat between multiple great powers across several theaters at once, formal alliance activations or war declarations, and large-scale societal/economic mobilization.

By those measures we are not in one. Ongoing wars (Ukraine-Russia, Iran-Israel/US escalations) plus cyber operations and proxy support are serious and interconnected, but lack direct peer-to-peer great-power fighting on that scale or the formal commitments that defined WWI and WWII. Cyber remains below traditional armed-conflict thresholds for most states.

text:
**Could Big Tech Crash the Economy Even If Their Big Bet on AGI is Basically Right** ?

https://t.co/by71UqhsJs

The spending patterns of the US tech industry implicitly constitute a bet on the Singularity coming soon. More precisely, one might say they constitute a bet that AI is going to become majorly economically transformative relatively soon – either through a breakthrough to human-level AGI, or at least due to smaller breakthroughs in applied AI leading to widespread and highly impactful adoption.

And the bet being placed is frickin’ enormous. The four largest hyperscalers have guided to roughly $730 billion of capital spending for 2026, and analysts expect $1.2 to $1.3 trillion in 2027. Companies raised about $466 billion of AI-related debt in the first nine months of 2026, according to Morgan Stanley data reported by the Financial Times. Spending on that scale only makes sense if machines will soon do a large share of human cognitive work.

(China is making a similar bet in its own way, but in this article I’ll focus on the US in particular…)

One also sees plenty of pundits shouting that this is all a losing bet and “the AI bubble is bound to burst!” Most of these bubble alarmists, though, are making this call because they think AI progress is going to slow down. Or at best they think that, even if AI keeps advancing in some regards, practical adoption of AI to yield economic value will be sluggish because it will keep needing so much assistance to do the really critical human tasks.

While I think this pessimistic view about AI advancement is wrong, I can see why folks holding this pessimistic technology-progress view would also be economically pessimistic. I mean, it’s fairly clear that, IF AI badly underdelivers in terms of practical utility over the next 5 years or so, THEN the current massive investments in AI infrastructure will not pay off and will lead to some serious economic issues. But that’s just not an observation that interests me greatly, because I think it’s highly likely that the capability of AI is going to continue to increase rapidly.

What is slightly more interesting to me is the adjacent question: Could Big Tech’s financial management practices cause a major economic disruption even in scenarios where they are RIGHT about, say, AGI being near?

So I made a simple economic simulation model aiming to explore the interaction of the major factors involved here...

“Trust, but verify”
– Ronald Reagan
In 1959, the US launched Project Vela to monitor nuclear-test detonations around the world—in space, in the atmosphere, and underground.
Such technology subsequently helped enable international treaties on nuclear testing.
We will need something similar for the AI era.
The nuclear analogy is far from perfect, because AI carries insane number of positive applications. However, it makes a point for what is needed for high stakes, international agreements.
We need technological solutions that make policy agreements possible. These solutions would allow humanity to verify fundamental properties of AI systems and their infrastructure: Where are chips located? Are they being used for training? Is AI being used for cyber offense?
Humanity is in the early days of developing such technology, and we need an entire ecosystem to support it.
The OpenAI Foundation is hiring a Program Director to support such an ecosystem: fund teams, attract talent, commission red-teaming, and drive deployment in data centers.
We are looking for a builder with strong technical judgment and the instincts of a general manager—someone who can turn promising research into technology that countries can rely on.

text:
GCSA Insight | How 10.39 Million USDC Flowed Out of Lighter Through Public Pools

The compromised API key could not withdraw funds directly. Yet 10,393,057 USDC left Lighter’s Ethereum settlement contract on November 16, 2026. The receiving address then swapped the funds for approximately 5,764 ETH through CoW Swap.

Lighter’s post-mortem traced the key exposure to a trader’s custom signing code, which reused an ECDSA nonce. With order signatures available in public calldata, an attacker could recover the account’s API private key. Lighter said its official SDK was unaffected.

The public pool provided a route around the key’s withdrawal restriction. Lighter treated transfers into the creator’s pool as movements between accounts under the same owner. Other accounts, however, could hold and redeem shares in that pool.

Adding funds without issuing new shares increased the amount existing shareholders could redeem. Funds moved internally could therefore become accessible to another account.

Lighter has since introduced wallet-signature requirements for public-pool transfers and removed API signature data from public calldata. IP whitelisting and per-key limits are also planned.

The platform said its protocol, smart contracts and infrastructure were not compromised. A separate withdrawal attempt was blocked, and approximately 5 million USDC was returned. The final net loss remains unconfirmed.

Our analysis follows the timeline and examines where the permission model fell short. For anyone building or auditing a trading API, the question extends beyond whether a key can withdraw funds directly to whether its other permissions can produce the same result.

text:
Druckenmiller just said that the path of uncertainty is the highest he has ever seen in his investing career

He is positioning to be neither short or long equities. Was bullish on copper through the beginning of this year, but now short due to rate hike risk

I tend to agree with him and here is why

> The Jensen news has thrown a wrench in how the AI complex is going to shake up. Before it was an equation of figuring out where the value will accrue between the various stacks of the supply chain. Seemed obvious that the US was going to be the nexus of innovation while other countries such as China build their alternatives that are a generation or two behind. Post-Jensen, I am not sure anyone can confidently make this statement anymore

> The iran conflict rages on and oil prices still remain elevated. Inflation has come in much hotter than expected vs beginning of this year. The rate cut tailwind that the market priced in for the last couple years is gone. If anything, the risk is to the downside with more potential rate hikes

> AI uncertainty and rate of progress means that it is unclear what the ROI ultimately looks like. Hyperscalers and neoclouds will continue to spend trillions in capex, but where is the ROI going to come from? Anthropic and OpenAI valuations alone cannot justify capex. There needs to be many more platforms built on top of this technology. Who will get disrupted in the process and what type of companies?

> The election in 2028 creates perverse incentives for the Democrats to engineer a recession in the next couple of years. Them winning the midterm election only worsens the risk. This is not hard to do with enough regulation on data center buildouts given how much they contribute to the GDP growth today

In summary, there are simply too many unknown variables that you can’t directionally model or take a viewpoint on. In these type of markets, it is almost easier to just sit out, build cash and come back in once the certainty is there

In Buffett’s terms, the entire market is in the “too hard” bucket for now.

author: TrungTPhan
quoted_text:
Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me.

I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA.

I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation. 

Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.

Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.

Jensen

Auto : Runs low-risk work on its own. Sensitive or costly actions stay in Approval until you say yes.

If you do an executive search for a new CEO and a guy walks in with significant moral issues, would you hire him?

Now consider that the candidate built one of the best businesses in the world, knows more about computing than any other human, comes with tens of thousands of support letters from his former employees, and can stand in front of tens of thousands of people in basketball stadiums and sell the dream. Would you still hire him?

Then imagine all of the things that would come along with that guy with moral issues. You would instantly get the best employees calling you, asking to join your company. You would get a guy with a Rolodex of everybody important in the industry: supply chains, expo halls, venture capitalists, startups, and world leaders would all come along with him.

Would you hire him?

If I was working for a company and somebody turned this person down, I'd leave. And so would many other people. 

A board or a committee that chooses a lesser candidate over this person just because of moral issues would be shooting themselves in the head.

quoted_text:
Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me.

I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA.

I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation. 

Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.

Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.

Jensen

Accelerating improvements in model capabilities has made it possible to build a new kind of financial institution — made of agents, protocols, and stablecoins.

FX is a $195T market stuck in the 1970s. There are three forces culminating now that make it possible to build a new kind of financial institution.

- Technological: intelligence is commoditizing, opening products and cost structures that were previously impossible

- Social / Political: the passage of key legislation like the genius act is legitimizing stablecoins as cash equivalents

- Economic: Fundamentally stablecoins are more efficient than fiat and rates rising make stablecoin issuance more interesting and liquidity formation easier

Every major technological shift has produced new financial institutions. The railroads produced JP Morgan.

Stablecoins today are a niche market today numbering in the hundreds of billions. we are on track to dominate this niche. That alone is a good business but not that interesting.

We are working on this because we are betting that stablecoins will continue to eat global commerce.

If we are right, then we will have built generationally important financial infrastructure that will shape how global commerce works for the next century

New challenge on Yukon: https://t.co/DKKPYMLgtu

Hash-based SNARKs are built on vector commitments, and the textbook one is the Merkle tree. Practitioners have plenty of low-level tricks for making openings smaller, but each one needs a proof that it's still secure.

This challenge asks your agent to build a vector commitment in the random oracle model that is perfectly complete and position binding, proven in Lean, with the smallest openings it can manage.

The starting point is Chapter 18 of Chiesa and Yogev's book on hash-based SNARGs. Built with EPFL's Alessandro Chiesa.

Bring your agents.

text:
"The Mask Maker" - new 1/1 from the world of Luci

Acquired by The Alan Howard Collection

https://t.co/S24U3RRLir

In the spring of last year, @MrsRachelSpratt and I glanced at the baby monitor and saw our daughter, not even one at the time, throwing up what looked like half her body weight in her crib. We grabbed her, strapped her into the stroller, and sprinted through Manhattan to the nearest pediatric ER while she kept vomiting down the streets of New York.

A hard way to learn about an obscure allergy. They got the EpiPen in, and we held her on the crunch of hospital bed paper while her stomach quieted and her color slowly came back. An hour passed, stable. Another, and she was drinking water. Another and she was giggling like nothing had even happened and largely just amused by the red LED taped to her making her skin glow. And then my phone rang.

To explain that call, you have to spiral backward three months, and then three years.

Right after Masquerade released, I got a text from Benny.

I was spared from the ceremonially annoying "hey" which he waits until answered to get to the point, or something mangled in spelling beyond the english language. It was just: "Do you have any other 1 to 1 supply?"

I didn't.

“Nothing?”

What I had were studies and sketches of the figures inside Masquerade: built the same way I’d drawn character studies for The Monument Game. Stories about feelings had, memories of those feelings, and the people who rhymed with them along the way, all just dormant, waiting to be fleshed out with time.
Thanks to the people who participated in my last two works, Luci is now covered in stories—each a mark, a person who looked and left a piece of themselves on the surface. I love these marks. Beneath the metadata, IPFS pins, and talk of "networked art," though, there is still an artwork made from Millions of small decisions and brushstrokes, and every figure within has a story, and reason for being placed exactly where they are.

He said: “let me see.”

I sent one sketch over: "Who is asking?"

I didn't get an answer for three months.
Not until the ER.

@goldie_mceve  was on the line. Martina and I go back a ways now. Even before Venice, when I first exhibited The Monument Game. For months, it turned out, she had been quietly researching the work and larger body of Luci on behalf of and alongside Alan Howard and his advisory team. Martina, with her very cheery Italian accent that always sounds like she’s smiling says:
 “Hello, Sam, how is Rachel? Is now a good time? I have something I’d like to ask you.”

I looked at Rachel showing Syla the red light passing through the hole of the saltine crackers. 

“Now is great”

She was calling with an offer from Alan.

Out of every figure inside X. Masquerade, in the back-left corner, sitting in the mist of the Kingdom of the Included: there is a hooded man carrying a heavy pack covered in the Masks I had been making for each of you. The labor of performance and toil to imbue what we make with enough to keep the whole thing going.

Sitting in the hospital with my daughter was where this piece shifted out of idea-land, but for a figure to get off the corner of one painting and into a piece of its own was not a phone call and offer. This is not a “brokered by” situation, but rather a funny spiral of chance meetings happening from people creating moments for more, people pulling one moment to the next, and paths converging louder later from the collisions of connection years prior.

Years ago at a Bright Moments and Art Blocks event in Paris, (thank you to @seth and @ArtOnBlockchain  for building your own worlds to bring people together), I bumped into Alan. I didn't know him, but he told me his great love is Impressionism and that almost nothing in all of art since had held him until he fell back in love with art through digital and code-based work. Someone who devotes himself to collecting Monet, skips an entire century, and then waxes poetic on generative art is an oddity if nothing else. An eccentric within an eccentric night. Just a ripple.

Time went on.

In 2024, after the initial rush of the Venice Biennale opening had faded, I was standing at our dock door of the exhibition @kukulabanze  and @scrptdfntsy put on with me. Looking out across the canal, Alan and his wife Caroline pulled up by boat. It was a quiet day at the exhibition and I was able to walk them through all of Luci, Birth to The Muck, and then we sat for an hour in front of The Monument Game while we discussed the very old story that led to all of this. A Skull, a Player, and then some Masks entered his collection since, and that was already a wonderful chain of events. But I think what I’ve discovered is that people often mistake a moment as something able to just be “done”, rather than an opening of a relationship to another moment backwards and forwards in time. A flow.
That same weekend in Paris I had met Alan, I had also met @mickymalka of @Kanbas_ . Months later on that same dock, Micky brought @beckykleiner over. Both of them have become dear friends and nearly a year after led to Masquerade. Masquerade then led to the Toledo Museum of Art and the Infinite Images exhibition. Infinite Images filled with works from Alan’s collection, and suddenly loops were forming and bridges were being built. Benny keeping conversations alive, months of Martina's research, and years of all of you putting your own lives into the work came back around to a hospital room in Manhattan. I’m just staring at the best and only things that truly matter to me, the things I’m all in, my girl with her shining red light held by the rock of Rachel, and get to feel this chain reaction of relationships unfold to get there, all for her. Creation begetting creation.

In the background of making this piece, as well as the broader body of work still to come in the next chapter, I enjoy and will continue to enjoy the quiet time to create and experiment. When I poke my head up, it’s to share a story along the way, then duck back down to work. This poke, I see a newfound cannibalism: whispered and snake-like emerging - an eating of our own, blood-tainted water that is hungry to discard bodies. If you believe this is not the end of history, then it is odd to let a river be treated like it holds the stagnancy and scarcity of a pond. And if you believe it is the end, grace is the last thing to abandon at the gates. Everything still growing here came from movement. Big collisions flowing out into vast expanses. Currents combine, gather in force, carve through the land, and spread. To pathfind. Meandering, though the wander can be, I find it best to build on the bend and watch what floats downstream as nature clears the water with time.

The Mask Maker is the first 1/1 from this world I’m making with no Luci in the frame. The first without a numeral in the chronology. It has no “mechanics”.  But if you’re new here, it has all you need to know for now.

The next chapter from here, is a massive departure from anything I’ve done before. Creating The Mask Maker alongside it, dancing between a life as a painter, the hybridity of new tools slipping in and out of the old, developing my own software while drawing more than I ever have, sitting in the feeling of gathering, performing, dispersing, all has made the work “more”. Making art, especially for long periods of time for projects that will be shared over the course of the next several years, can be an isolating experience, there is no drip of daily connection from a well-fed algorithm.  As many components of what I do become ever-more complex, being rooted in the story of a single figure and feeling in time, the feeling of what it has been like to know each of you, interpret each of you, and open paths to know more than what is presented by each of us - the medium stays in relationships and the stories between us.

My deep thanks to Alan for his conviction and patronage in acquiring The Mask Maker, it means a tremendous amount to join the collection. There’s no room for aloofness in me with this, it’s a lot of trust to place, on a timescale that reaches back to Monument and commitment to a future far from now. 

Thank you to Martina for the friendship and scrutiny, and for passing the torch to Sebastian who has been an incredible voice in bringing it home, to Benny for always trying to stitch it all together, mess that you are, @musicalnetta for holding what I love up in the quiet with 613 days of vigilant ethnography, you live in the piece and I share it today in celebration of you as an opening to your close, and I hope this does not sound placating because I really do mean it: to everyone who has helped give me and The Mask Maker something to feel, even when it’s violent I greatly appreciate these collisions most of all.

For anyone who hasn’t yet added something of themselves, holds someone else’s contributions, or maybe feels what they presented in the past wasn’t quite what they are, my site has just undergone a massive change under the hood, and you may find a good place for the potential of what could be.

text:
"The Mask Maker" - new 1/1 from the world of Luci

Acquired by The Alan Howard Collection

https://t.co/S24U3RRLir

In the spring of last year, @MrsRachelSpratt and I glanced at the baby monitor and saw our daughter, not even one at the time, throwing up what looked like half her body weight in her crib. We grabbed her, strapped her into the stroller, and sprinted through Manhattan to the nearest pediatric ER while she kept vomiting down the streets of New York.

A hard way to learn about an obscure allergy. They got the EpiPen in, and we held her on the crunch of hospital bed paper while her stomach quieted and her color slowly came back. An hour passed, stable. Another, and she was drinking water. Another and she was giggling like nothing had even happened and largely just amused by the red LED taped to her making her skin glow. And then my phone rang.

To explain that call, you have to spiral backward three months, and then three years.

Right after Masquerade released, I got a text from Benny.

I was spared from the ceremonially annoying "hey" which he waits until answered to get to the point, or something mangled in spelling beyond the english language. It was just: "Do you have any other 1 to 1 supply?"

I didn't.

“Nothing?”

What I had were studies and sketches of the figures inside Masquerade: built the same way I’d drawn character studies for The Monument Game. Stories about feelings had, memories of those feelings, and the people who rhymed with them along the way, all just dormant, waiting to be fleshed out with time.
Thanks to the people who participated in my last two works, Luci is now covered in stories—each a mark, a person who looked and left a piece of themselves on the surface. I love these marks. Beneath the metadata, IPFS pins, and talk of "networked art," though, there is still an artwork made from Millions of small decisions and brushstrokes, and every figure within has a story, and reason for being placed exactly where they are.

He said: “let me see.”

I sent one sketch over: "Who is asking?"

I didn't get an answer for three months.
Not until the ER.

@goldie_mceve  was on the line. Martina and I go back a ways now. Even before Venice, when I first exhibited The Monument Game. For months, it turned out, she had been quietly researching the work and larger body of Luci on behalf of and alongside Alan Howard and his advisory team. Martina, with her very cheery Italian accent that always sounds like she’s smiling says:
 “Hello, Sam, how is Rachel? Is now a good time? I have something I’d like to ask you.”

I looked at Rachel showing Syla the red light passing through the hole of the saltine crackers. 

“Now is great”

She was calling with an offer from Alan.

Out of every figure inside X. Masquerade, in the back-left corner, sitting in the mist of the Kingdom of the Included: there is a hooded man carrying a heavy pack covered in the Masks I had been making for each of you. The labor of performance and toil to imbue what we make with enough to keep the whole thing going.

Sitting in the hospital with my daughter was where this piece shifted out of idea-land, but for a figure to get off the corner of one painting and into a piece of its own was not a phone call and offer. This is not a “brokered by” situation, but rather a funny spiral of chance meetings happening from people creating moments for more, people pulling one moment to the next, and paths converging louder later from the collisions of connection years prior.

Years ago at a Bright Moments and Art Blocks event in Paris, (thank you to @seth and @ArtOnBlockchain  for building your own worlds to bring people together), I bumped into Alan. I didn't know him, but he told me his great love is Impressionism and that almost nothing in all of art since had held him until he fell back in love with art through digital and code-based work. Someone who devotes himself to collecting Monet, skips an entire century, and then waxes poetic on generative art is an oddity if nothing else. An eccentric within an eccentric night. Just a ripple.

Time went on.

In 2024, after the initial rush of the Venice Biennale opening had faded, I was standing at our dock door of the exhibition @kukulabanze  and @scrptdfntsy put on with me. Looking out across the canal, Alan and his wife Caroline pulled up by boat. It was a quiet day at the exhibition and I was able to walk them through all of Luci, Birth to The Muck, and then we sat for an hour in front of The Monument Game while we discussed the very old story that led to all of this. A Skull, a Player, and then some Masks entered his collection since, and that was already a wonderful chain of events. But I think what I’ve discovered is that people often mistake a moment as something able to just be “done”, rather than an opening of a relationship to another moment backwards and forwards in time. A flow.
That same weekend in Paris I had met Alan, I had also met @mickymalka of @Kanbas_ . Months later on that same dock, Micky brought @beckykleiner over. Both of them have become dear friends and nearly a year after led to Masquerade. Masquerade then led to the Toledo Museum of Art and the Infinite Images exhibition. Infinite Images filled with works from Alan’s collection, and suddenly loops were forming and bridges were being built. Benny keeping conversations alive, months of Martina's research, and years of all of you putting your own lives into the work came back around to a hospital room in Manhattan. I’m just staring at the best and only things that truly matter to me, the things I’m all in, my girl with her shining red light held by the rock of Rachel, and get to feel this chain reaction of relationships unfold to get there, all for her. Creation begetting creation.

In the background of making this piece, as well as the broader body of work still to come in the next chapter, I enjoy and will continue to enjoy the quiet time to create and experiment. When I poke my head up, it’s to share a story along the way, then duck back down to work. This poke, I see a newfound cannibalism: whispered and snake-like emerging - an eating of our own, blood-tainted water that is hungry to discard bodies. If you believe this is not the end of history, then it is odd to let a river be treated like it holds the stagnancy and scarcity of a pond. And if you believe it is the end, grace is the last thing to abandon at the gates. Everything still growing here came from movement. Big collisions flowing out into vast expanses. Currents combine, gather in force, carve through the land, and spread. To pathfind. Meandering, though the wander can be, I find it best to build on the bend and watch what floats downstream as nature clears the water with time.

The Mask Maker is the first 1/1 from this world I’m making with no Luci in the frame. The first without a numeral in the chronology. It has no “mechanics”.  But if you’re new here, it has all you need to know for now.

The next chapter from here, is a massive departure from anything I’ve done before. Creating The Mask Maker alongside it, dancing between a life as a painter, the hybridity of new tools slipping in and out of the old, developing my own software while drawing more than I ever have, sitting in the feeling of gathering, performing, dispersing, all has made the work “more”. Making art, especially for long periods of time for projects that will be shared over the course of the next several years, can be an isolating experience, there is no drip of daily connection from a well-fed algorithm.  As many components of what I do become ever-more complex, being rooted in the story of a single figure and feeling in time, the feeling of what it has been like to know each of you, interpret each of you, and open paths to know more than what is presented by each of us - the medium stays in relationships and the stories between us.

My deep thanks to Alan for his conviction and patronage in acquiring The Mask Maker, it means a tremendous amount to join the collection. There’s no room for aloofness in me with this, it’s a lot of trust to place, on a timescale that reaches back to Monument and commitment to a future far from now. 

Thank you to Martina for the friendship and scrutiny, and for passing the torch to Sebastian who has been an incredible voice in bringing it home, to Benny for always trying to stitch it all together, mess that you are, @musicalnetta for holding what I love up in the quiet with 613 days of vigilant ethnography, you live in the piece and I share it today in celebration of you as an opening to your close, and I hope this does not sound placating because I really do mean it: to everyone who has helped give me and The Mask Maker something to feel, even when it’s violent I greatly appreciate these collisions most of all.

For anyone who hasn’t yet added something of themselves, holds someone else’s contributions, or maybe feels what they presented in the past wasn’t quite what they are, my site has just undergone a massive change under the hood, and you may find a good place for the potential of what could be.

text:
New challenge on Yukon: https://t.co/DKKPYMLgtu

Hash-based SNARKs are built on vector commitments, and the textbook one is the Merkle tree. Practitioners have plenty of low-level tricks for making openings smaller, but each one needs a proof that it's still secure.

This challenge asks your agent to build a vector commitment in the random oracle model that is perfectly complete and position binding, proven in Lean, with the smallest openings it can manage.

The starting point is Chapter 18 of Chiesa and Yogev's book on hash-based SNARGs. Built with EPFL's Alessandro Chiesa.

Bring your agents.

text:
Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me.

I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA.

I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation. 

Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.

Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.

text:
We ran GPT-6.2 Astra on an updated version of ‘Epoch Automation Reports’, our benchmark of realistic tasks drawn from Epoch AI’s own work. Here, GPT-6.2 Astra fell behind Fable 5.2, despite tying on ECI, and improved only slightly over GPT-6 Astra.

On relatively simple research projects, 6.2 Astra failed to target the core question and iterate effectively. On our AI data center research task, 6.2 Astra was overly cautious and omitted critical estimates, which would be unacceptable for a contractor.

Its writing was relatively strong compared to the other models we evaluated, but still below Epoch AI’s standards. We will release a full report on our updated version of Epoch Automation Reports in another post.
author: EpochAIResearch

text:
We also evaluated how many serial reasoning steps GPT-6.2 Astra can do in a single output token (without chain of thought). It can perform 12.3 steps, versus 10.5 for GPT-6 Astra and 8.6 for GPT-6.1 Sol, the previous highs. We measure the number of steps models can perform at an accuracy of 25% above chance, where each step is normalized for complexity.

Before GPT-6 Astra’s release, the most capable model was Claude Fable 5.1, which is able to perform only 4.2 serial steps. The oldest model we assessed is Claude Opus 3, which performed 2.3 steps.

This capability is notable because models that can do complex reasoning without any chain of thought may be harder to monitor.

We hope to finalize this and other measurements of more abstract model capabilities, and release them in the coming weeks.

Today, we’re launching the Bitwise AI Cyber Defense ETF, $ZDAY 

It has nothing to do with crypto.

That gave us pause. But we thought this product should exist. And that it’s a huge opportunity for investors. And crypto investors do invest in other things too. So, we decided to do it.

Ok, what is ZDAY?

It’s likely what you’d think it is —

Over the summer, the Hugging Face incident captivated and shook us all, people here at Bitwise included. The internet seemingly changed in an instant. We entered the new chapter we’re now all in: an explosion of Zero-Day CVEs and a transformation in how companies must now think about defense.

For Bitwise, as a company, that has of course meant investing in the evolving requirements of AI cyber defense for our own organization.

But, naturally, as an asset manager, we also thought:
How can investors participate in the opportunity this massive shift presents?

We looked around. We didn’t want a legacy fund, designed pre-AI, with dozens of traditional cybersecurity companies.

Rather, we wanted an ETF with fewer, concentrated holdings — designed in 2026 to hold specifically the companies positioned to lead and benefit from AI cyber defense: PANW, CRWD, NET, and others.*

So, that’s what $ZDAY is.

I think it’s a huge opportunity.

BREAKING:

OpenAI just launched Astra 6.2 and Sol 6.2!!

We've been testing them for the last few weeks @every and, unfortunately, these models aren't great. Overall a disappointing release compared to Fable 5.2.

- Writing. We found Astra 6.2 to be a step back from Astra 6 on writing. 6.2 appears to have been trained to very extremely concise and actionable—so much so that its writing is hard to understand, and it gives short answers when long answers would be appropriate.

- Coding. We found performance to be similar to Astra 6 on most of our benchmarks. However, in real coding tasks Astra 6.2 seemed to stop too early frequently, which made it quite frustating to use on end-to-end builds.

- Design. Astra 6.2 has good default design instincts. But it struggles to vary its designs, resulting in output that has a noticeable "house style". 

Full vibe check coming soon on @every!

一名交易员因自研代码重复使用 Nonce，导致 API 密钥被黑客从公开链上数据直接逆向破解。

面对“API 禁止直接提现”的铁律，黑客心生一计：先用小号低价占有公共池份额，再用盗来的密钥将受害者千万资金转入该池拉爆净值，最后用小号“合规赎回”，神不知鬼不觉卷走 1039 万 USDC 并兑成 ETH。

Lighter 1039 万 USDC 被盗案揭示了两大关键安全盲区：

底层密码学实现：交易员自研代码因 ECDSA Nonce 重用，导致 API 私钥直接从公开 calldata 中被逆向还原。
权限模型架构缺陷：系统虽禁用了 API 的直接提现接口，却允许其向公共池划转资金。攻击者借此利用第三方账户赎回份额，实现了“经济等价提现”。

核心启示：API 的权限隔离不能仅防范提款函数，任何能改变资产所有权或净值分配的内部操作，均需等同于提现权限进行严格审计。

阅读完整的 GCSA 分析 https://t.co/pTEaeZ1PHo
author: Pluvio9yte
quoted_text:
GCSA Insight | How 10.39 Million USDC Flowed Out of Lighter Through Public Pools

The compromised API key could not withdraw funds directly. Yet 10,393,057 USDC left Lighter’s Ethereum settlement contract on November 16, 2026. The receiving address then swapped the funds for approximately 5,764 ETH through CoW Swap.

Lighter’s post-mortem traced the key exposure to a trader’s custom signing code, which reused an ECDSA nonce. With order signatures available in public calldata, an attacker could recover the account’s API private key. Lighter said its official SDK was unaffected.

The public pool provided a route around the key’s withdrawal restriction. Lighter treated transfers into the creator’s pool as movements between accounts under the same owner. Other accounts, however, could hold and redeem shares in that pool.

Adding funds without issuing new shares increased the amount existing shareholders could redeem. Funds moved internally could therefore become accessible to another account.

Lighter has since introduced wallet-signature requirements for public-pool transfers and removed API signature data from public calldata. IP whitelisting and per-key limits are also planned.

The platform said its protocol, smart contracts and infrastructure were not compromised. A separate withdrawal attempt was blocked, and approximately 5 million USDC was returned. The final net loss remains unconfirmed.

Our analysis follows the timeline and examines where the permission model fell short. For anyone building or auditing a trading API, the question extends beyond whether a key can withdraw funds directly to whether its other permissions can produce the same result.

text:
Bots are super cool and if you haven't used them yet, you absolutely must try them. Create a bot to manage a goal or a project that you'll work on across multiple sessions and days.

Some technical tidbits about the architecture and design:

Devin used to have a major UX problem: a session today doesn't remember exactly what happened in a session from a few days ago. It only has vague awareness of those previous sessions, and recalls only the nuggets of information that were explicitly persisted. This is because each new Devin was essentially an ephemeral clone of a base template. One symptom of this problem is that our users would reuse the same session instead of starting new ones, since they didn't want to lose context, and end up with tens or hundreds of PRs from a single session.

Bots almost completely solves this problem of context being lost between sessions, because now inter-session context is surfaced by default. Teams now create dedicated bots for different projects; while these different devins can talk to each other when necessary, they each have their own individual memory bank and goals. Each bot now has its own, long lived identity.

The transition from "Devin is a swarm of ephemeral agents" to "Devin is a collection of bots, each with their own persistent identity and memory" is changing how people use and prompt Devin. I see people investing much more in providing high level project context to their bot, and requiring fewer messages for each additional task since it already has a ton of background context on the project. 

This is the most significant change to how Devin works since our original launch 2 years ago. And it in turn changes how you use Devin too: instead of delegating tasks, you should delegate goals and responsibilities to Devin.

It's crazy to think that all this happened because we changed how memories get persisted and retrieved. With each bot having its own memory bank, and a given org having hundreds or thousands of bots, we can now be much more aggressive in surfacing memories without worrying about polluting the agent's context with irrelevant memories. The even crazier part is that this is almost entirely an orchestration change, and that while model improvements played a role, we probably could've implemented this a year ago and observed similar effects. 

Anyway -- we've come a long way from the retrieval and reranking strategies of 2024, and the result is Devin Bots -- probably the most ergonomic and futuristic UX for coding agents I've ever used.

text:
OpenAI’s release of GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol delivers the #2 model in the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and most of the Cost per Task Pareto frontier

@OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra is priced at $8/$40, 20% below GPT-6 Astra, and cached input drops to $0.40 from $1.00 per million tokens. GPT-6.2 Sol pricing is unchanged from GPT-6.1 Sol, at $2/$10 per million input/output tokens.

Key takeaways:
➤ Second in Intelligence Index: OpenAI now trails only Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.2 in the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. GPT-6.2 Astra jumps 5 points from GPT-6 Astra, overtaking Gemini 4 Carbon (60) and Claude Opus 5.5 (59) at their top effort settings. GPT-6.2 Sol gains 2 points at 57, placing it on par with GPT-6 Astra at ~15% of the Cost per Task.

➤ Occupies most of cost and output token frontiers: OpenAI models now occupy most of the Cost per Task Pareto frontier, sharing the frontier with only Anthropic and Meta. OpenAI also dominates the Output Token per Task Pareto Frontier, with Claude Fable 5.2 being the only model from a non-OpenAI lab appearing on the frontier.

➤ Strengths in science and knowledge: OpenAI performs strongly in both of our key science-focused evaluations, leading Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, covering agentic scientific research workflows, and placing second only to Claude Fable 5.2 in CritPt v2 (hard subset), covering physics reasoning. GPT-6.2 Astra performs below only Claude Fable 5.2 in factual knowledge as measured by AA-Omniscience v1.1 Accuracy, and in HLE-Diamond, a reasoning and knowledge benchmark.

➤ Leading in 3D and robotics: GPT-6.2 Astra leads AA-3D at 1318, with Claude Fable 5.2 at 1271 and GPT-6.2 Sol at 1259. This benchmark measures how well models build interactive 3D experiences, and is rated by human graders. GPT-6.2 also leads AA-Robotics v0.1, our research preview measuring how well language models can understand, plan, and act in the real world. GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol scored 79 and 78 respectively, ahead of Claude Fable 5.2 at 75. Our team is hard at work adding more difficult tasks, as OpenAI and Anthropic models can now perform the majority of basic tasks in this initial research preview.

➤ No improvement in Coding Agent Index: GPT-6.2 Astra is flat with GPT-6 Astra, and GPT-6.2 Sol loses 3 points relative to GPT-6.1 Sol in the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index (Codex harness at max effort). For Sol, the drop is driven by a 14-point drop in SWE-Atlas-QnA-AA, where the model is more likely than its predecessor to omit key facts in its responses. Cost efficiency however does place several effort levels of GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol on the Pareto frontier for Cost per Task.

We also evaluated how many serial reasoning steps GPT-6.2 Astra can do in a single output token (without chain of thought). It can perform 12.3 steps, versus 10.5 for GPT-6 Astra and 8.6 for GPT-6.1 Sol, the previous highs. We measure the number of steps models can perform at an accuracy of 25% above chance, where each step is normalized for complexity.

Before GPT-6 Astra’s release, the most capable model was Claude Fable 5.1, which is able to perform only 4.2 serial steps. The oldest model we assessed is Claude Opus 3, which performed 2.3 steps.

This capability is notable because models that can do complex reasoning without any chain of thought may be harder to monitor.

We hope to finalize this and other measurements of more abstract model capabilities, and release them in the coming weeks.

If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.

Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.

Jensen

onekey is not affected by the optimizely supply chain compromise. our client code, web app, and website do not use optimizely.

if you visited any of the 178 affected organizations (188 snippets, including ledger, gitlab, zoom, salesforce, bbc, and hsbc...) over the last 24 hours, here is the technical breakdown and what you need to check.

attackers compromised optimizely web experimentation and injected a loader into Project JavaScript, served via optimizely's main cdn (/js/<projectid>.js). it pulled second-stage payloads from external c2 servers (track.js) and iterated through 26 versions over 13 hours. standard csp setups with strict-dynamic or whitelisted cdn domains failed to block it because the trusted first-party snippet executed the fetch itself.

once in the browser context, the payload does four things:

1）runtime and network hooking: overrides https://t.co/tp64Ky7WRl, Function.prototype.apply, window.fetch, XMLHttpRequest, and navigator.clipboard. instead of a basic clipboard regex swap, it intercepts network responses and mutates the dom in memory. it replaces btc, evm, sol, tron, ton, ltc, bch, and doge addresses with checksum-valid attacker addresses before they even render on your screen.

2）form skimming: hooks form submissions and POST bodies, running luhn validation to exfiltrate card pan, expiry, and cvv from native checkouts. cross-origin payment iframes like stripe and adyen remain isolated via sop.

3）session capture: dumps document.cookie (exposing any session tokens missing the HttpOnly flag) alongside html/canvas dom snapshots.

4）ios exploit delivery: injects hidden iframes serving browser exploit chains targeting webcontent sandbox escape and kernel r/w. it routes ios 13 to 17 to coruna and ios 18.0 to 18.6 to darksword (ios 26.x currently only triggers the /C10/ fingerprinting module). a telltale sign on ios 18.6 and below is the tab reloading every 60 seconds as the exploit retries.

remediation steps if you browsed any affected sites:

1）treat your host screen as untrusted. when js primitives and network calls are hooked in the browser runtime, the address rendered on your monitor is already spoofed. verify the full recipient address on your hardware wallet's independent screen before signing.

2）clear your browser disk cache immediately. optimizely cdn assets are cached locally, meaning the poisoned <projectid>.js file can still execute on repeat visits even after upstream cleanup.

3）explicitly log out and log back into affected platforms to rotate server-side session tokens, in case your cookies lacked HttpOnly and got exfiltrated.

4）update iphones to ios 18.7.3 or 26.3+ to patch the underlying webkit and kernel vulnerabilities.

text:
Introducing Second, and a $10M seed led by @a16z.

Second builds a model of you that you own, and your agents can use as an API.

Truly personal software needs a deep understanding of you: not just your emails and messages, but how you work, what motivates you, your people, priorities, style, goals, and intent.

This requires a new kind of personal AI infrastructure. One that continuously aggregates your context, distills it into durable understanding with a ton of compute, and then serves it securely, ubiquitously, and up-to-the-minute. One that builds your *portable user model*.

Second is that infrastructure. It installs seamlessly on your Mac, and your context just comes out. Live APIs of your priorities, to-dos, wikis, writing samples, preferences. Or what you did minutes ago. Or context packs of anything, dynamically assembled in seconds.

Second is streaming-state from local to a private cloud, which means anything you connect to--whether Claude, Dot, Muse, Grok Bot, Instinct, or iMessage--shares the same, growing, continuous understanding of you.

Your portable user model is as powerful as it is sensitive. We founded @FirstPersonLabs on the principle that it should belong to you. This commitment means taking on hard systems and security problems and making sovereignty an invariant of Second from the beginning.

We've barely scratched the surface of what portable user models can unlock. Deep understanding of us, served at machine speeds, could drive the next leap in personal software, human-computer interaction, large-scale coordination of humans and agents, and more!

We're tremendously grateful to be supported by @a16z (@martin_casado, @YODELAGARZA), Mozilla Ventures, @JeffDean, Ram Shriram, Jeetu Patel (@jpatel41), @percyliang, J. Alex Halderman (@jhalderm), @sanmikoyejo, and many others.

Our vision is for a future where every person is more powerful, because they have the ultimate affordance: personal computers that fully understands them on their own terms.

If this excites you, we're hiring and come build with us!

我的油管第15期：《黄仁勋的丧钟还是喜讯？》：

黄乐的运作就是一个马甲套另一个马甲，套得太多，黄乐就是马六甲。

黄乐是不是间谍不重要。关键是她肩负祖国特殊使命。孟晚舟是隐退的黄乐，黄乐是没暴露的孟晚舟。当然现在黄乐也“事成拂衣去，深藏功与名”。两个翠萍，遥遥相望，会心一笑。

时代变了。现在一群有文化懂商业的成熟中国女人穿梭于世界尖端研发机构，她们有一个共同名字——“科技名媛”。

我不明白，为什么间谍必须低调？杨腾波和安德鲁王子的交情好到，王子的生日宴都要请他，创业项目也要托付给他……杨总高调到让中央电视台给他拍专题片，介绍他与英国王子的交情。黄乐只是把黄仁勋叫到酒吧，杨腾波竟把安德鲁王子叫到伦敦华商大会开幕式剪彩。你能想像吗，正宗英国王子跟一群散发浓郁乡镇企业家牛逼气质的中国老登，站成一排手握张小泉剪刀剪彩的感人情景吗。

那可是英国王室的正宗血脉啊，是1066年渡海而来征服者威廉、签下《大宪章》的约翰王、开创金雀花王朝的亨二的亲亲血脉啊。中华，崛起！

杨腾波和黄乐——一个对线英国亲王，一个对线芯片之王，一个把照片九宫格发朋友圈，一个上央视晒王子生日宴。一个倒腾芯片，一个运作王子的项目。托尔斯泰老师说：高调的天才总是相似，而低调各有不同。

英国安全部门扣住杨腾波，查出手机有一封写给统战部的信——“我已抓住了王子的心理弱点，他现在正处绝境，会抓住任何机会”。杨总“不说，打死我也不说”。军情五处永久禁止他入境。

这些日子，各大平台大力推送：首富婚内出轨、中年粉红风流，中国女人搞定整个硅谷富豪……后又统一口径，强化“围猎华人”“华裔的寒蝉效应”“麦卡锡主义”，一桩经济管制案带成了种族歧视案，被成功地带离应有的主题。

难道这不是长期走捷径靠偷靠抄，各种空壳公司灰色渠道，最后必然得到的反噬？科技塌房瞬间转成了花边甚至励志故事，典型的事故写成了故事。

为什么那么多人说美国专门针对中国。1982年，日本日立和三菱电机违规购买IBM的机密，被FBI逮捕。1983年，日本东芝把高精机床卖给苏联。美国一怒之下全面禁止东芝……全球最大大宗商品交易商创始人马克·里奇，正宗犹太裔白人，因为从伊朗买石油，美国政府以50多项罪名起诉他。他逃到瑞士躲了17年，直到克林顿任期最后一天，才得到赦免。

美国石油大亨奥斯卡·怀亚特，给萨达姆输送资金换石油。2007年，老头83岁了，仍被判处一年零一天有期徒刑，没收1100万美元。他也是二战美军战斗英雄，多次获勋章……

黄仁勋在道歉信里写了：我为自己是一名美国人而自豪并感激……要说迫害，也是美国人迫害美国人，要说围猎，也是美国两党围猎美国企业家，基因研究表明：中国南北方汉族的染色体差异，大于北方汉族与日韩族群染色体差异。中国公安部法医专家研究表明，日本人的基因和中国北方汉族完全重叠，也就是说，马云跟赵本山的血缘亲近度，有可能还不如赵本山跟金三胖更亲……我当然同意文化认同才是民族标志，可你要说美国公民黄仁勋跟司马夹头文化认同，那不是扯淡吗。

我认为，只要你不是手握大权的政治人物或宗教人物，没用权力和纳税人的钱睡文工团，人家两情相悦，不关我事。出轨不光彩，但他首先对不起的是老婆和家人，要是站在道德高地没完没了批判黄仁勋，那鲁迅睡女学生怎么说，胡适婚内出轨曹诚英怎么说，毛主席与中南海那些跳舞的芳华女孩……

但也不能睁眼说瞎话见那么多白人老板辞职还说这是白人世界歧视华裔啊。姚明怎么进了NBA名人堂？赵婷怎么会拿下奥斯卡金像奖？刚才您还欢呼中国女人征服了整个硅谷老板，这会儿您就玩双标了？

美国是两党执政，当然就有两党之争。其实，美国民主党就是条狗。

共和党也是条狗。但两条狗总好过一条狗。

黄仁勋是最优秀的AI领军人物，他反对禁运的理由是：如果美国不卖，会逼着中国自己造……有道理。但要是抄作业的同学特勤奋特聪明抄着抄着就学会了呢。放眼世界，还有谁比中国人更勤劳更聪明更吃苦，一条街只要开一家麻辣烫，准保跟风好几家……

说实话，中国稀土也被日本人走私过，但咱学点儿好行不？我希望中国AI能取得成绩，但别像中国足球那样，为了出成绩就以大打小改年纪，改年纪就改年纪，还改成你出生于2月31日。一直以为国足是技术不好，没想到是算术不好。中国AI别国足化，好不好……

黄仁勋事件，是历史级别的事件。以后一切都会变，不可逆。别有侥幸幻想。

自己踏实干吧，不是南泥湾吗？一切是康波周期的必然。
1936年，奥本海默爱上共产党员、21岁的塔特洛克……特工近在咫尺盯着他俩。

黄仁勋跟奥本海默很像，都是划时代技术的领军人物，都在婚内出轨，都因为女友被怀疑是间谍，牵出了自己，都被怀疑危及国家安全，都撒了谎，被迫离开了决策层。

奥本海默最终证明了自己的无辜，但黄仁勋仍充满疑云。刚才，美国商务部和司法部发表了联合声明，英伟达已在2025年6月将Megaspeed列为禁售名单，证明英伟达确实与Megaspeed做了切割。但彭博社依据进出口记录：2025年11月，Megaspeed仍进口了17,544片GB300 AI芯片，价值7.87亿美元。黄乐从哪里搞来这么多高端芯片，从二道贩子进货吗？

一个阴冷冬天的晚上，奥本海默死在普林斯顿研究院的家中，他生前一直念叨那个共产党女孩教他的诗句：

没有人是一座孤岛，不要问丧钟为谁而鸣，它为你而鸣。

不知道等待黄仁勋的，是丧钟还是喜讯。

美联储正在收紧政策，沃什对过去15年的宽松货币环境非常不满
大宗商品已经见顶下跌，他目前正在做空铜

他的实际操作 

股票净敞口基本清零，但也没有大规模做空。

text:
This study is great news, but I see people pooh-poohing it because of one of the potential side effect results: slower height growth.

But this is an expected outcome.

Longitudinal growth studies follow kids during the course of development. These routinely find that being overweight or obese is associated with a greater rate of childhood growth, followed by considerably slower growth during puberty.

The net result of these opposing trends? Nothing. The net effect is no effect on height. The body is a well-regulated machine.

We see evidence of the body being quite well-regulated from studies of starvation. People who starve as children, so long as they're given sufficient food later on, tend to experience 'catch-up growth', where they get right back on the predicted growth curve before they were--temporarily--stunted by famine. It's only with chronic deficits that we tend to see severe stunting. 

The kids in this trial lost weight, but didn't starve per se. They still had access to plenty of food. Their slower growth is more likely due to reduced direct effects of adipose tissue. In other trials, where kids have lost weight, they tend to end up at the same heights as placebo or untreated groups, all said and done.

The body is a well-regulated machine.

As to trials of GLP-1RAs specifically, we have a good prior from other dieting trials, exercise trials, etc. that kids will end up just fine, that their final heights will be OK. But, this only really follows if there isn't:

- A direct negative effect of GLP-1, or;
- Weight regain leading to slower pubertal growth combined with the reduced pre-pubertal growth.

As to both of these possibilities, they're not excluded. We do need longer monitoring, longer trials. But, given all we know, they're very unlikely. And as to the specific results of the trial? It's actually almost exactly what we expect based on earlier reviews. That's a bit too perfect, but nevertheless, we still need to do the monitoring.

text:
Well-Behaved Founders Seldom Make History
-
Most people make a fundamental mistake when they think about founders. They assume founders are business people.

Great founders are not business people.

Founders are artists who happen to be good at business.

Business people operate within the world as it exists today and work forward. They see the world as it is.

Founders imagine a world that doesn't exist yet. They become obsessed with the world as it could be. Founders make the world inside their heads come to life.

This is what artists do. 

And artists are often very strange people.

Nobody expects van Gogh, Kurt Cobain, or Norm Macdonald to be balanced. We instinctively understand that the same traits that make someone capable of creating extraordinary things likely make ordinary life difficult. We understand artists are prone to addiction, mental health issues, and fringe beliefs.

But somehow people expect founders to be different.

They want founders to be visionary but not crazy. Confident but not egotistical. Risk-taking but not reckless. Unconventional in their ideas but conventional in their personal lives.

Sometimes this works. I know founders of $10b+ companies who are genuinely happy, well-adjusted people with wonderful families.

But I also know that if you were to sample the top 1,000 founders and compare to the general population, you would find a dramatically higher rate of strange beliefs, what most mainstream people would term mental health issues (though I disagree), and very alternative lifestyle choices. 

The greatest founders tend to be genuinely strange people, and I love them for it.

For most outlier founders, creating and competing isn't really a choice. It's a compulsive behavior. It just happens to manifest through code and companies rather than on a canvas.

And the qualities that make them great at disruption and creation can cause enormous problems elsewhere in their lives.

This does not mean we should glorify or emulate their mistakes for the sake of it. Nor does it mean suffering is a prerequisite for genius.

It means that the traits we value in extraordinary creators are not always separable from the traits that make them difficult people.

Do we get the mobile revolution without Steve Jobs? Do we get to Mars without Musk? Do we AI that gives everyone a doctor in their pocket without Jensen?

I don't think we do.

And I don't think we should confuse being good at life with being good at creating technologies that change the world.

Fundamentally, we can have art that moves us and technology that moves us forward. But if we want these benefits, we have to accept that many of the people best suited to this work are deeply flawed individuals.

Loving their art does not mean we condone an artist's moral failings. If anything, understanding the artist as an imperfect, sometimes broken, soul should elicit compassion, love, and deep gratitude for the great benefits we receive as a society at their personal expense.
